# Rustroom — development journal

The session-by-session record of how Rustroom got built: what each milestone did, what it
measured, what it retracted, and which sabotages its tests failed to catch.

> **This file is NOT auto-loaded into context.** It exists to be *searched*, not read. It was
> split out of `CLAUDE.md` on 2026-09-16, when that file had reached **1.2 MB (~337,000 tokens)**
> and was being force-fed into every session — more than a whole context window before any work
> began. `CLAUDE.md` now carries only the durable facts and the live state; everything historical
> is here.
>
> **How to use it — grep, don't read:**
> ```
> grep -n 'M8\.11' docs/JOURNAL.md          # one milestone
> grep -n '^### ' docs/JOURNAL.md            # every section title
> grep -n 'RETRACT\|retracted' docs/JOURNAL.md   # things this file got wrong and fixed
> grep -n 'sabotage' docs/JOURNAL.md         # tests that failed to catch a deliberate break
> ```
> Then `sed -n '<start>,<end>p' docs/JOURNAL.md` to read just that section.
>
> **Newest first.** Content below is verbatim from `CLAUDE.md`; only `###` headings and this
> preamble were added.

### M8.11 confirmed by use (2026-09-16)

✅ **Reported working on a photograph — *"works, confirmed"* — with no defects found by using it.**
M8.11 is therefore closed in the strong sense: merged, green, *and* seen. The GUI was launched
`--release` and exercised against the checklist below.

⚠ The report did not enumerate which checklist items were exercised, so **the luminance-range
case is confirmed only as part of the whole** rather than named. It is the one whose failure mode
is a *plausible photograph* rather than an error — see `crates/gpu-pipeline/src/mask.rs:104`,
where the coverage dispatch's position is called load-bearing. If a range mask is ever seen to
drift while its own sub-stage moves, start there.

⚠ This milestone is also the first whose handoff was recorded under the new rule that **a
superseded block moves here rather than accumulating in `CLAUDE.md`**. The block it replaced:

> ### State (2026-09-16)
> 
> **2529 tests, 63 goldens.** The repo is **`main` alone** — no other branches, no worktrees, clean tree.
> 
> **M8.11 — a mask's coverage and blend on the GPU — is merged fast-forward and its branch deleted.**
> A whole mask is now one `GpuStage`: seed, coverage, sub-stages and blend in a single compute pass,
> with the composite folded into one coverage dispatch. `fmt` / `clippy --all-targets --all-features
> -D warnings` / `test --workspace` green together, **each exit code read from its own command**;
> **63 goldens ran and none moved**; `crates/pipeline/tests` unmodified.
> 
> ⚠ Journal section: `M8.11 — a mask's coverage and blend on the GPU (2026-09-16)`.
> 
> ### ▶ Next action — two things, neither of them code
> 
> **1. CONFIRM M8.11 BY USE. The check is that the picture does not change, not a stopwatch.**
> 
> With **Settings → Rendering → "Use the GPU"** on, open the photo carrying the real sidecar and drag
> that mask's sliders: visibly quicker, and **the picture must not change**. Then build a **composite**
> — a mask plus a Subtract or Intersect refinement — the shape that was not accelerated at all before.
> 
> > **⚠⚠ THE HALF A STILL FRAME CANNOT CATCH IS A RANGE MASK KEYED ON ITS OWN OUTPUT.** The coverage
> > dispatch is recorded *before* the sub-stages precisely so a luminance or colour range selects on
> > the **base** pixel; get that wrong and lifting the shadows moves them out of the band that
> > selected them — a plausible photograph, not an error. So exercise **a luminance-range mask
> > carrying a large exposure lift**, where the selection must stay put as the slider moves.
> 
> ⚠ Then **pan at 1:1 with a mask selected**: coverage is defined over the FRAME, so a mask that
> slides across the photograph as you pan is the region half — guarded by
> `a_region_is_masked_as_that_part_of_the_whole` and by nothing else.
> 
> ⚠ **Do not expect a global slider drag over a masked photo to gain anything (1.00×, by
> construction).** Such a drag changes the base the auto-mask gate reads, so the coverage cache misses
> every frame; a gating brush then has no prebuilt map and the twin declines. Fixing it needs
> `GpuBrushRaster` to take a GPU-resident base — real work, and the obvious next item on this path.
> 
> **2. ⚠⚠ OFFER THE DEMOSAIC TIER BEFORE PROPOSING ANOTHER PORT.** Owed for three milestones now.
> His stored export tier is **`Best`**: a **10.78 s** decode against `Fast`'s **2.82**, while the whole
> render is ~0.58 s on the GPU. M8.4's own validated comparison found `Better` and `Best`
> *"indistinguishable at 4× nearest-neighbour"*. **That is ~8 s a photo from a dropdown he already
> has** — against M8.9's entire lens-correction port, which bought under 5% of an export. It is a
> conversation, not a milestone.


> **▶ RESUME HERE (fresh session).**
>
> **FIRST: check the real state before anything else** — this block goes stale the moment the user pushes.
>
> ```
> git branch --show-current && git log main..HEAD --oneline && git log origin/main..main --oneline
> ```
>
> Run that command rather than trusting any state written here. If a branch shows up ahead of `main`, do not start the next feature on top of it — ask whether to merge, **and never push either way; the user pushes to `github.com/wladiKrin/rustroom` himself.**
>
> **⚠ Conventions that are not negotiable:** commit messages carry **no `Co-Authored-By` trailer**; **branch per feature** without asking; **never push**.
>
> **Run the GUI:** `export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/lib/pkgconfig:/opt/homebrew/opt/libraw/lib/pkgconfig:/opt/homebrew/opt/little-cms2/lib/pkgconfig:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH"` then `cargo run --release -p app` — always `--release`, in the background, and **launch it after every big update without being asked**, saying what to look at. Skip it for small tweaks in a tuning loop.
>

> **⚠⚠ THE LESSON OF THE WHOLE MILESTONE: EDGE QUALITY AND EDGE SELECTION ARE DIFFERENT PROBLEMS, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS ALGORITHMIC.** The contrast floor and the contiguity rule both made the detector find *genuine* edges. Neither could make it know which edges are the **building**, because a Hough accumulator cannot tell a colonnade from a cliff face or a person's silhouette. That is semantic knowledge, and the only thing in the room that has it is the person looking at the photograph. **Two rounds were spent improving quality before that was recognised.**
>
> - **Round 1 — an absolute contrast floor on display-encoded luminance.** ⚠⚠ An absolute floor on **linear** luminance would be meaningless: 0.01 in shadow is a visible edge, the same 0.01 near white is nothing. **This project already had that exact bug on record in the Whites slider**, where perceptual thirds were read off linear luminance. So `verticals` display-encodes before the Sobel, after which `MIN_EDGE_LEVELS` is expressible in **8-bit levels across an edge**, divided by Sobel's step gain of 4 so it means what it says. ⚠ The encode lives **inside `detect::verticals`**, so a caller cannot hand it the wrong colour space — `LensCorrectionStage`'s reasoning for building its own `Corrector`.
> - **Round 2 — a candidate must have one CONTIGUOUS run of support.** `MIN_LENGTH_FRACTION` counted votes *anywhere* along the infinite line, so a candidate reached its threshold from fragments scattered over the frame. Measured, the winning lines had **24–41% of rows voting but a longest contiguous run of 7–13%** — statistically collinear noise, not edges. Hough finds candidates; a walk along each survivor now verifies them.
> - **Round 3 — Auto became a refinement of guides you draw.** `Auto` with no guides, **`Refine guides`** once any exist. Each near-vertical guide is replaced by the strongest real edge within `SNAP_RADIUS`, or **returned bit-identical** with the status line saying so.
>
> **⚠⚠ THE TWO CONSTANTS TRADE OFF, AND THAT MOVED THE FLOOR BY A FACTOR OF THREE.** `MIN_EDGE_LEVELS` was tuned to **24** while the length test still counted scattered votes — it was the only thing rejecting noise. With contiguity doing that job, **8** fires on 26% of 70 frames against 24's 29%, *and* recovers Weltenburg Abbey, whose stonework is faint under an overcast sky and which is lost above about 10. **A constant chosen to compensate for a different bug moves once that bug is fixed.**
>
> | levels | 2 | 4 | 6 | **8** | 12 | 16 | 24 | 32 |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | fires, votes counted anywhere | 97% | 96% | 93% | 84% | 53% | 34% | 29% | 27% |
> | fires, run required contiguous | 54% | 37% | 29% | **26%** | 20% | 16% | 13% | 11% |
>
> **⚠⚠ `detect_overlay` IS THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT ENDED THE GUESSWORK, AND IT IS KEPT.** It writes the plane `detect::verticals` actually consumes as a PNG with the chosen lines drawn on it, which separates two completely different bugs: *the lines are wrong* against *the lines are right and mapped wrongly*. **Two rounds of reasoning had gone to the wrong cause; one picture settled it in a minute.** `--refine` additionally draws a guide as drawn (amber) against refined (green). ⚠ Reach for it before theorising about detector behaviour.
>
> ⚠ **Two hypotheses were tested and REJECTED rather than assumed**, which is why they are worth recording: the offset mapping is **not** aspect-broken (every fixture was square 256×256 while the real plane is 512×342, and this project has recorded an aspect bug four times — but a vertical line on a wide frame comes back where it was painted), and the floor is **not** what excluded the colonnade (8, 12 and 24 give Walhalla the identical pair).
>
> **⚠⚠ A GUIDE'S TWO X VALUES ARE ITS POSITIONS AT THE Y IT WAS DRAWN BETWEEN — and reading them as the frame's top and bottom is a bug that is INVISIBLE on a full-height guide.** For a short one they describe a different line, with its lean understated by the ratio of the extents: tracing the top fifth of an edge leaning 8° read as **1.7°**, so a perfectly-placed guide was rejected on divergence outside where it was drawn. Reported in use as refinement taking only one of two guides *and* redrawing them full-height. The gap is measured at the **drawn endpoints** now, which is also simpler — the drawn line's x at those y *is* `from[0]` and `to[0]` — and the refined guide keeps the y it was drawn between.
>
> ⚠ `SNAP_RADIUS` is **0.03 and measured, not asserted**: guides traced 1–3% off the true edge moved 0.011–0.027 of frame width across both known frames, while the competing wrong edge — Walhalla's sky line against its building corner — sits **0.16 away, five times the radius**. ⚠⚠ The first measurement showed the abbey never snapping and **the fault was the measurement**: probing a 16°-leaning edge with a straight *vertical* guide leaves a large gap at one end however well placed the line is. `--refine` takes `top:bottom:y0:y1` for that reason.
>
> **⚠⚠ FOUR SABOTAGES PASSED WHILE PROVING NOTHING IN THIS MILESTONE, AND THREE WERE THE FIXTURE'S FAULT RATHER THAN THE GUARD'S.** (1) **My own change disarmed the one test that could see the direction gate** — `a_gradient_sky_casts_no_votes` carried 0.64 levels per row, far below the new floor, so the floor rejected every pixel before the gate saw one and deleting the gate outright left all 13 tests green; it is a repeating ramp now, ~25 levels per row.
