### M8.11 — a mask's coverage and blend on the GPU (2026-09-16)

**M8.11 — a mask's coverage and blend on the GPU (2026-09-16).** A whole mask is one `GpuStage`: seed, coverage, the sub-stages and the blend in one compute pass, with a composite folded into one coverage dispatch. 2497 → **2529 tests** (exactly the thirty-two added, plus one `#[ignore]`d probe); **63 goldens ran and none moved**, and `crates/pipeline/tests` is unmodified. ✅ **Merged fast-forward, its branch deleted. Not pushed.** ⚠⚠ **NOT YET CONFIRMED BY USE.** Spec `2026-09-15-mask-gpu-design.md`, plan `2026-09-15-mask-gpu.md`.

**⚠⚠ WHAT IT DELETES IS A ROUND TRIP IN THE MIDDLE OF EVERY ACCELERATED MASK, AND THE AGREED ORDER'S OWN NAME FOR THIS ITEM — "mask coverage + the blend" — MISSED THAT ENTIRELY.** Before it, `MaskStage::apply` ran its sub-stages through a `GpuChain` — uploading, running and **downloading the whole adjusted frame as floats** — and then blended on the CPU, reading `base` plus `adjusted` plus the coverage and writing a third image. ⚠ A mask also used to **end** a GPU run; `every_tail_stage_is_replaceable_or_a_mask` recorded that it was the last thing in the tail that could.

**⚠⚠ MEASURED BEFORE DESIGNING, AND THE MEASUREMENT REFRAMED THE MILESTONE.** `mask_breakdown` reports `cov=0.00` for a range mask — not because its coverage is free but because it is computed **inside the blend loop**, so that column means two different things by mask kind: **68.5–90.7 ms** for a colour range against **10.3–13** for a brush. That is why `cpu_cost` sums per component rather than carrying one constant, which would be wrong by about 7× one way or the other.

**⚠⚠ AND THE LUMINANCE RANGE'S COST WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN SCALED, WHICH A RATIO ARGUMENT WOULD HAVE MISSED BY 4×.** The tempting reasoning is that a luminance range is `color::luminance` plus an sRGB encode where a colour range is a full Oklab round trip plus `atan2` and `hypot`, so it must be a small fraction. Measured in one run at 6.5 Mpx: **45.6–48.1 ms against 97.5–111.6 — roughly 0.45×, not a tenth.** ⚠ That is the **sixth** time composing or scaling a measurement would have missed in this crate, after M8.3g (~2×), M8.3f (8× in attribution), M8.3o (~18%) and M8.10 (~12%). `GpuStage::cpu_cost` has no default precisely so adding a stage forces the measurement.

**⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE IS NOT THE SPEED-UP, IT IS THAT THE COMPOSITE FOLD REMOVES A REGRESSION.** A/B on one binary, the pre-fold decline restored for the "before" run. DSCF6274.RAF, rung 3200 (⚠ load **14–17**, a decidedly busy machine):

| | CPU | GPU | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **COMPOSITE: 3 colour ranges — before** | 219.72 ms | **305.15** | **0.72×** |
| **the same, after** | 195–222 | **47.9–51.1** | **~4.1×** |

Before the fold the twin declined, and **a declining mask ENDS a GPU run** — the tail split around it and paid two round trips plus the CPU mask, so with `gpu_tail` on that shape was **slower than leaving the GPU off**. The GPU column goes **305 → 48 ms, about 6×**.

⚠ **Only that row is quoted, and the reason is the M8.3k retraction's rule.** Its CPU columns agree across three runs (219.72 / 222.48 / 195.06). The mixed composite's moved **2.4×** between runs (271 / 643 / 217), so its before-figure is not sound and **no ratio is claimed for it**.

**⚠ The earlier A/B, for the single-component shapes** (same method, rung 3200): REAL SIDECAR 1 mask **116.70 → 62.93 ms (1.85×)**, 3 masked HSL **166.35 → 55.81 (2.98×)**, 1 masked HSL **76.31 → 44.00 (1.73×)**.

**⚠⚠ AND THE ROW THAT DOES NOT MOVE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A GAP: a GLOBAL slider drag over a masked photograph reads 1.00×.** Such a drag changes the base the auto-mask gate reads, so `MaskCoverageKey` misses on every frame; a gating brush then has no prebuilt map and the twin declines. The fix is a GPU-resident base for `GpuBrushRaster`, which is real work.

**⚠⚠ A GATING BRUSH IS ACCELERABLE ONLY THROUGH A MAP SOMEBODY ELSE ALREADY MADE, and that shaped the whole seam.** Such a brush reads the photograph to decide its coverage, and the photograph does not exist when the twin is built. `GpuBrushRaster` takes its base as **CPU memory**, so it cannot be called from inside `encode` either. So `PipelineStage` gained `prebuilt_coverage()` and `render_engine`'s existing cache supplies the map: on a hit the twin builds, on a miss it declines and the CPU stage rasterises and **deposits**, warming the cache for the next frame. ⚠ Measured trade: uploading the plane is ~2 ms at rung 3200 against **31.8–43.5 ms** to rasterise a gating brush on the GPU — cheaper by an order of magnitude, which is why the CPU-side cache was kept (user's call) and a GPU-side one backlogged.

**⚠ A brush is rasterised at ENCODE time, not at construction, and that is forced.** Coverage is defined over the FRAME, and without a region the frame's size is the buffer's — which does not exist until the pass is being encoded. Rasterising at construction would mean declining every whole-frame render, i.e. the entire fit rung.

**⚠⚠ `scratch_planes` IS `4 + max(sub.scratch_planes())`, AND THE SUM IS FORCED.** `GpuChain` lends the **same** planes to every stage — its own doc says "nothing written here survives the call" — so a base copy parked in shared planes would be clobbered by the first sub-stage wanting scratch. The **max** rather than the sum, because planes are transient within a stage. ⚠ `&scratch[4..]` is the single most dangerous expression in the stage: handing over the whole slice lets a sub-stage write `base_r/g/b` and `cov`, producing a plausible photograph blended against the wrong thing. **Its first sabotage went UNCAUGHT**, because the fixture's only sub-stage asks for zero planes; a **sharpening** sub-stage (4 planes) is what discriminates.

**⚠⚠ THE COMPOSITE FOLD: THE CHAIN IS UNROLLED INTO THE SHADER TEXT, AND ONLY THE NUMBERS TRAVEL.** Per-component parameters moved out of the uniform into a `Comp` storage array; the text is the program cache's key, so a composite of a given **shape** compiles once and is reused as its sliders move (M8.3d's rule). A loop over `comps` with a `kind` tag would compile once for the whole app and branch per pixel instead.
- **⚠⚠ The scene facts hoist above the chain, which is where the GPU does BETTER than the CPU rather than merely matching it.** `BaseFacts` memoises `lightness` and `hue_chroma` per pixel because a composite may hold several range components; here the chain is known when the shader is built, so the conversion is emitted **once** above it — and not at all for a mask that reads no pixel. **Three colour components cost one Oklab round trip**, the property `crates/pipeline`'s thread-local counter already asserts for the CPU.
- **⚠ Several painted components share ONE coverage binding**, concatenated, each carrying its own word offset — the binding count is fixed, so three brushes cannot have three bindings. `words_for` is the single definition of how much space a map takes, read by `pack` laying one down and by `comps` recording the next offset; two derivations is how a composite comes to read its neighbour's coverage.
- **⚠ The folds are `MaskOp::combine`'s three rules and must stay exactly those.** That function **is** the brush raster's algebra — `Add` is the across-strokes paint step and `Subtract` is `erase` — so a fourth spelling would make subtract-between-components disagree with erase-within-a-brush at every partial coverage. `min`/`max` agree at 0 and 1 and differ everywhere between.
- **⚠ One declining component declines the whole mask.** A composite is a single coverage plane; there is no half of it to accelerate.

**⚠⚠ THE ORDERING SABOTAGE IS OBSERVABLE AT LAST, AND THE STAGE'S OWN COMMENT HAD BEEN ASKING FOR THIS SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN.** The coverage dispatch is recorded *before* the sub-stages because it reads `img`, which is still the base. That was provably inert for painted and analytic masks — `painted_at` never touches `img`, and such a mask now emits no `img` read at all. Re-run once the range kinds and the composites landed, it **fails four tests**: both range masks and both composites containing one. A mask keyed on its own output chases its effect, which is what `Composite::at`'s `base_px` parameter exists to prevent.

**⚠⚠ THREE SABOTAGES WENT UNCAUGHT ACROSS THE MILESTONE AND EACH NAMED A REAL GAP — the step earning its place for the fourth milestone running.**
1. **The hoisted facts taken from the BASE alone.** All four composite tests stayed green, because every one of them mixed components of a **single kind** — so "the union over the chain" and "the base's own facts" agree on all of them. The discriminating fixtures are **a shape refined by a range** and **a luminance base refined by a colour range**.
2. **`cpu_cost` ignoring the refinements.** Wrong in the **safe** direction — the gate must fail toward the CPU — which is exactly why nothing saw it: the picture is identical and only the speed is lost. What it strands is a cheap base refined by an expensive range, the shape the fold exists for. ⚠ My first test asserted at the **gate** and its own fixture check failed: a mask's cost is **not** observable there, because `worth_a_chain` sums a whole run and every tail ends in `output_transform` at 28.6 ms, clearing the 27.0 bar by itself — M8.3h's finding arriving again.
3. **The frame aspect taken from the region, missed TWICE.** There was no region test for the mask at all, and every other fixture renders whole-image where the region's aspect **is** the frame's. Adding one modelled on `VignetteStage`'s own region test **still** did not catch it: the fixture was a 24×18 region inside a 64×48 frame, both exactly 4:3, so the two numbers were equal by coincidence. It is 30×12 now, with an assertion that the aspects differ. ⚠ Same family as an axis-aligned gradient hiding an aspect bug — **a fixture whose two quantities happen to be equal cannot tell them apart.**

**⚠⚠ AND THE HUE WRAP'S OWN TEST DID NOT CATCH `rem_euclid` BECOMING `%`.** The two differ by a multiple of 360 which **cancels** in `offset - span`, so only the `before` shoulder discriminates. Rewritten on band 200–260, where `%` gives 1.0 for every pixel against `rem_euclid`'s 0.028 / 0.697 / 0.997 / 1.000 / 0.000.

**⚠ A test asserted something FALSE about correct code**: an inverted colour range does **not** leave neutrals alone. `c = band * gate` is 0 for a neutral, so `1 - 0 = 1`. Renamed and its assertion inverted.

**⚠⚠ THREE FIXTURES LOST THEIR WEDGE, AND IT IS THE SEVENTH TIME A PROPERTY HERE BECAME UNCONSTRUCTIBLE BY BEING FIXED.** Substituting a mask for its twin means the CPU `MaskStage` is no longer in the accelerated pipeline, so every test inspecting a mask's **inner** structure needs one the twin declines. Six tests were re-aimed at a **gating brush** (permanent: no cached map, no acceleration), and the fold then retired a second wedge — two more tests used "carries a refinement" as their decline, which is now exactly what the fold accelerates. ⚠ The taker in `a_mask_that_deposits_nothing_never_takes_another_masks_plane` needed a gating brush whose box falls **below `MIN_GPU_BOX_PX`**, so the rasteriser refuses it and deposits nothing; a full-size one declines too and **deposits**, which is the one thing that fixture forbids. ⚠ `brush_mask` and `plain_brush_mask` both became dead and are **deleted with a note** — their death is the finding, and clippy caught both while every test was green.

**⚠ Divergence from the CPU, in 8-bit levels** (`probe_divergence`, kept and `#[ignore]`d, at 128×96): painted brush **0.00003**, linear **0.00003**, radial **0.00009**, luminance range **0.00024**, colour range **0.00040**, composite of three colour ranges **0.00036**, gradient ∩ colour range **0.00170**. Three orders of magnitude inside the equivalence tests' 1.0-level bound, and far more faithful than the crate's least-faithful stage (lens correction, 0.797).

**⚠ Two composite rows were added to `bench_gpu_tail`, because no existing row can see this milestone** — every other masked row carries a bare base, which the twin accelerated before the fold. That is the asymmetry M8.3j recorded when its own bench could only see fixtures.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **a global slider drag over a masked photo gains nothing**, structurally, and it is the case most likely to be reported as "the toggle does nothing here"; (2) **a gating brush with a cold cache declines**, so the first frame after any base change is unaccelerated; (3) **the coverage cache stays on the CPU** (user's call) — a GPU-side one is backlogged and wants re-measuring once this is in use; (4) **not bit-identical** — the blend is a multiply-add the GPU fuses, rounding once where the CPU rounds twice, so the GPU is the *more* accurate of the two; (5) the stage asks for **4 + max(sub)** scratch planes, 8 with a sharpening sub-stage; (6) ⚠ **M8.3j/k/l's inner-chain machinery is now reachable only on the decline path** — kept and pinned with the gating-brush wedge, and worth re-asking once a GPU-resident brush raster exists; (7) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), and the bench machine was **decidedly not quiet** (load 14–17); (8) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.

### M8.10 — a parallel batch export (2026-09-15)

**M8.10 — a parallel batch export (2026-09-15).** A batch decodes and renders `width` photos at a time, bounded by a `Settings` value defaulting to **4**, with every filename and collision settled **before anything decodes**. 2493 → **2497 tests** (exactly the four added: 2 for the setting's repair and its serde default, 1 for the up-front resolution, 1 carrier); **63 goldens ran and none moved**, and `crates/pipeline/tests` is unmodified — which is the proof this changed *when* work happens and never what it computes. ✅ **Merged fast-forward, its branch deleted, and CONFIRMED BY USE (2026-09-15)** — the batched export was exercised and reported working. **Not pushed.** ⚠ Read the confirmation narrowly: it establishes the **feature** — the progress line, the up-front collision prompts, a cancel — and **not** a measured speed-up, which is the bench's own 2.82–2.98× and stands on its own measurement. ⚠⚠ **The caveat most likely to come back is the memory**: ~4 GiB at width 4 on a 26 Mpx camera, and `Settings → Export at once` is the lever if that is too much. Spec `2026-09-15-parallel-export-design.md`, plan `2026-09-15-parallel-export.md`; the probe is `crates/app/examples/bench_batch_export.rs`, kept.

**⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE IS 2.82–2.98×, AND IT IS LOWER THAN THE 3.31× THAT MOTIVATED THE MILESTONE — WHICH THE SPEC PREDICTED AND DELIBERATELY DECLINED TO PROJECT.** `probe_decode_parallel` priced **decodes alone**; a real export also renders, encodes and writes, and the renders contend for the same rayon pool. Measured through the shipped `ExportWorker`, **each width in its own process**, X-T4, 8 distinct `.RAF` at the default `Better` tier, three runs each (⚠ load **5.1–6.2**, *not* a quiet machine):

| | wall clock | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| **width 1** | **66.02–66.15 s** (8.25 s/photo) | **1.32 GiB** |
| **width 4** | **22.17–23.37 s** (2.77 s/photo) | **4.01 GiB** |
| | **2.82–2.98×** | 3.04× |

⚠⚠ **Composing component measurements has now missed in this crate four times** — M8.3g over-predicted a frame by ~2×, M8.3f was right in magnitude and wrong by 8× in attribution, M8.3o was optimistic by ~18%, and this by ~12%. **It is the first where the miss was written down in advance**, which is the whole reason the plan made a real measurement its own task rather than quoting the sweep.

**⚠⚠ PEAK MEMORY READ 4.01 GiB AGAINST THE PLAN'S PREDICTED ~1.2, WHICH IS THE ONE FAILURE MODE THIS DESIGN CAN HAVE — AND IT IS NOT A LEAK.** That estimate priced the **decode buffers only** (4 × 313 MiB). Width 1 — *one* photo in flight — already peaks at **1.32 GiB**, so a photo costs its decode buffer **plus about a gigabyte of whole-buffer prefix render**; four of those at **3.04×** is **sub-linear**, because the process constants and the bundled lensfun database are shared.
- **⚠⚠ THE PROOF IT IS NOT A BUFFER HELD PAST ITS OWN PHOTO IS THAT WIDTH 1 DOES NOT GROW ACROSS ITS 8 PHOTOS.** A leak would climb with the count; 1.32 GiB is one photo's footprint and it stays there over 32 exports. ⚠ **Separating the two widths into their own processes is what makes that visible at all** — a single process running both reports only the larger, and cannot distinguish "four times a correct footprint" from "something held too long". The probe takes `BENCH_WIDTHS` for exactly that.
- **⚠ So the honest statement of the setting's meaning is stronger than the plan's: peak memory is `width` whole photos *including their renders*, ~1 GiB each on a 26 Mpx camera, not ~300 MiB each.** Four-wide is ~4 GiB; 8-wide would want ~8. That is what `export_width`'s ceiling of the core count is bounding, and it is the number to quote if anyone asks why the default is 4 rather than 8.

**⚠⚠ AND THE BYTE-IDENTITY CHECK CANNOT BE MET LITERALLY, FOR A REASON THAT PREDATES THIS MILESTONE ENTIRELY.** The plan's acceptance was *"the exported files must be identical to what width 1 produces"*. They are not — and neither are **two sequential runs of width 1**. On all 8 files, **exactly 2 bytes of 7,156,352 differ**, at offsets **72 and 74**: the **minute and second fields of the ICC profile's creation timestamp**, which `color::srgb_icc()` has lcms2 stamp into every profile it builds (year/month/day/hour matched, because the runs fell in one hour).
- **⚠⚠ That it differs between two *sequential* runs is what establishes it says nothing about concurrency.** Checking width 1 against itself was the discriminating measurement, and without it this would have been recorded as a concurrency bug.
- **⚠ What it does say is that an export is NOT byte-reproducible**, which matters to anyone checksumming, diffing or archiving one — and which nothing in this project had noticed. **The whole compressed image is byte-identical**, so the acceptance check holds in a stronger form than it was written: it names exactly which two bytes do not match, rather than asserting a match that was never true.

**⚠⚠ EVERY FILENAME AND COLLISION IS SETTLED UP FRONT, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE PARALLEL PHASE POSSIBLE AT ALL RATHER THAN BEING A TIDINESS.** `plan()` walks the jobs sequentially, resolves each destination and asks about every collision, **decoding nothing**; only then do N workers run. Otherwise a worker would block on a dialog while its neighbours ran — a stall, and a state nothing else here could see. ⚠ `no_photo_is_decoded_before_every_collision_is_answered` needs **both** collisions, because one alone passes against a loop that merely moved the prompt ahead of *its own* decode. ⚠⚠ Recorded honestly: **today that property is STRUCTURAL rather than guarded** — `plan` returns before `run` decodes anything, so no cheap sabotage can break the ordering without rebuilding the old interleaved loop; the test is for the *future* regression of folding the decode back in "to save a pass".

**⚠ The workers share an `AtomicUsize` cursor and each does a whole photo — decode, render, write.** Not decode-ahead-by-one: the spec priced that and it buys the decode's share of one photo for a channel, a buffer and a second place for a 298 MiB image to be alive, where this bounds peak memory at exactly the thing the setting names. ⚠ `thread::scope` rather than detached threads, so the workers borrow `planned`, `opts` and `decode` with no `Arc` around each.

**⚠ `Settings::export_width` REPAIRS rather than trusts** — `(self.export_concurrency as usize).clamp(1, cores)` — so a hand-edited `0` cannot produce a run with no workers and a hand-edited `64` cannot ask for 64 whole photos in memory. ⚠ The ceiling is the **core count**, because the decode is what is being overlapped and there is nothing to gain past it. ⚠ `DEFAULT_EXPORT_WIDTH` is 4 and the field carries the container-level `#[serde(default)]`, with its own test: a **field**-level one would give `u32`'s default of **0**, silently handing every existing user a run the clamp then repairs to one worker — the `write_xmp` trap, and the reason that test exists rather than being assumed.

**⚠⚠ `failed` IS NOW IN COMPLETION ORDER, WHICH IS NONDETERMINISTIC, AND `done` COUNTS COMPLETIONS RATHER THAN POSITIONS.** With several in flight the fourth photo can land before the second, so a *position* would jump about where a count only ever rises. The consequence is user-visible and is the feature rather than a defect: **the progress line names photos out of order**. ⚠ Any test comparing `failed` must sort or compare as a set.

**⚠ The post-decode cancel check now abandons up to `width` decodes rather than one** — ~30 s of background CPU on a four-wide run, spent and discarded. Inherent, and the same "abandon, don't abort" trade the sequential version already made for one: libraw cannot be interrupted, so the decode finishes and its result is thrown away.

**⚠⚠ THE CARRIER ASSERTS CONCURRENCY AS PEAK SIMULTANEOUS DECODES, NEVER BY WALL CLOCK**, and it needs both halves. A wide run and a sequential one produce the same files **by design**, so "the output is right" passes with the concurrency deleted, and "it ran concurrently" passes against a run that wrote the wrong files — the W5 failure mode. ⚠ The count lives in the **injected decode fn**, so no production observable is needed at all, and a timing assertion is the CI flake this project has three of on record.

**⚠⚠ FOUR SABOTAGES: TWO CAUGHT BY ASSERTION, ONE BY NON-TERMINATION, AND ONE RECORDED AS INERT RATHER THAN COUNTED.** Caught: **the width ignored** (the carrier alone) and **the post-decode cancel check dropped** (both cancel tests). ⚠ **The cursor never advancing** (`next.load` for `next.fetch_add`) is caught by the suite **hanging** rather than failing — every worker takes index 0 forever and `planned.get(0)` is always `Some`, so non-termination is *structurally certain* rather than timing-dependent, but it is a timeout and not an assertion. ⚠⚠ **Not caught: sending `ExportEvent::Item` BEFORE the work rather than after** — 46 passed, 0 failed. `every_photo_produces_a_jpeg` asserts the event *count*, which a moved send does not change, and the events are collected after the run so no test can observe an event against filesystem state. The consequence is a progress line optimistic by up to `width` photos, cosmetic rather than a wrong file; **a deadline-based test for it would be exactly the wall-clock assertion this project has three CI flakes from**, so it is stated rather than covered.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **peak memory is `width` whole photos including renders — ~4 GiB at width 4 on a 26 Mpx camera, not the ~1.2 the plan assumed**, and that is the caveat most likely to be reported as a problem; (2) **2.82–2.98×, not 3.31×** — the renders contend; (3) **the progress line names photos out of order**, deliberately; (4) **a cancel abandons up to `width` decodes**, ~30 s of discarded CPU four-wide; (5) **an export is not byte-reproducible**, by two bytes of ICC timestamp, and that predates this milestone; (6) the `Item`-ordering sabotage is uncaught and is recorded rather than covered; (7) **nothing here helps a single-photo export**, which is one photo either way; (8) one machine, one camera, 8 photos, and the bench machine was **not quiet** (load 5.1–6.2).

### M8.9 — lens correction on the GPU, and the export bug it uncovered (2026-09-15). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.9 — lens correction on the GPU, and the export bug it uncovered (2026-09-15). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works, confirmed by use, but I don't really notice it being that much faster with the gpu on"*, with **no defects found by using it**. ⚠ Read the confirmation narrowly: what it establishes is that **the export now matches the canvas**, which is the milestone's own acceptance check and the thing no test can make. The speed half is the reporter being right, and it is measured below.

**⚠⚠⚠ "NOT MUCH FASTER" IS CORRECT, AND THE REASON IS THE DECODE — WHICH THIS FILE ALREADY RECORDED AND WHICH THE MILESTONE DID NOT WEIGH AGAINST ITS OWN HEADLINE.** Measured on the reporter's machine, `DSCF6296.RAF` at 26.0 Mpx (⚠ load 5.4–7.6):

| | |
|---|---|
| the **decode** at his stored export tier, `Best` | **10.78 s** (9961 ms process + 820 unpack) |
| the decode at the default `Better` | 5.6–7.5 s |
| the decode at `Fast` | **2.82 s** |
| the whole **render**, corrected, CPU | 1.13–1.15 s |
| the whole **render**, corrected, GPU | **0.58–0.61 s** |

**So at his own setting the GPU saves ~550 ms of a ~11.4 s export — under 5%.** At the default tier it is ~9%. ⚠⚠ **That is not a defect and it is not fixable here**: ~93% of a full-resolution decode is libraw's demosaic, inside `dcraw_process`, **entirely upstream of every stage `wgpu` touches** — the M8.4 finding, arriving as the answer to a question it was not asked.

**⚠⚠ SO THE PORT'S REAL VALUE IS THAT IT PAID FOR THE FIX, NOT THAT IT MADE EXPORTS FAST — and that is how it should be reported.** Correcting the export costs **+715 ms a photo on the CPU**; with the seam it costs **+170**. Without the port, fixing the lens bug would have made every export visibly slower.

**⚠⚠ THE LEVER THE REPORTER WOULD ACTUALLY FEEL IS A DROPDOWN, AND IT SHOULD BE OFFERED BEFORE ANY FURTHER GPU WORK.** His `settings.json` holds `"demosaic": "Best"`, whose decode is **10.78 s** against `Fast`'s **2.82** — **~8 s a photo, fifteen times what this whole milestone saves.** ⚠ And M8.4's own validated comparison found `Better` and `Best` *"indistinguishable at 4× nearest-neighbour"*, so `Best` is buying a difference that milestone's crops could not show. ⚠ `Better` at 5.6–7.5 s is the middle option. **Say this before proposing another port.**

⚠ The second lever is **parallel export**: `batch_export` is sequential **by design**, to bound peak memory at roughly one 26 Mpx image. With ~90% of each photo being decode, overlapping the next photo's decode with this one's render would hide the render entirely — which is a memory trade, and is already on the M8.1 leftovers list.

⚠ **And nothing is expected in the PREVIEW**, which is accepted caveat (4) rather than a gap: the scoped path stays on the CPU by design, and on an unscoped fit render lens correction is a few milliseconds of a 1600 px frame. If the setting *felt* like it did something to the preview, that would be the surprise.

### M8.9 — lens correction on the GPU, and the export bug it uncovered (2026-09-15)

**M8.9 — lens correction on the GPU, and the export bug it uncovered (2026-09-15).** Two halves: `GpuLensCorrectionStage`, the third arm on `accelerate_prefix_stage`; and **lens correction reaching an export at all**, which it never had. 2479 → **2493 tests** (exactly the fourteen added: 3 grid, 2 weights, 7 shader, 2 export); `fmt` / `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` / `test --workspace` green together, **each exit code read from its own command** — `FMT=0`, `CLIPPY=0`, `TEST=0`; **63 goldens ran and none moved**, and `crates/pipeline/tests` is unmodified. **Not merged, not pushed.** ⚠⚠ **NOT YET CONFIRMED BY USE.** Spec `2026-09-15-lens-correction-gpu-design.md`, plans `2026-09-15-lens-correction-gpu-stage.md` and `2026-09-15-lens-correction-export.md`.

**⚠⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE IS A BUG, NOT THE PORT: THE GUI'S EXPORT APPLIED NO LENS CORRECTION AT ALL, AND NEVER HAD.** Found while reading `export_one` to plan the wiring, and **verified end to end rather than by reading**. It built through `pipeline::build_pipeline_spec`, which hardcodes `lens: None`, and `decode_for_export` discarded the metadata keeping only the white-balance baseline — so there was no `LensShot` in that path to pass even if it had.

| path | lens correction |
|---|---|
| the preview (`render_cached` → `build_prefix_steps(.., lens, ..)`) | **applied** |
| `rustroom render` (its own `build_pipeline_split_in_region_with_brush(.., lens, ..)`) | **applied** |
| **the GUI's Export dialog** | **not applied** |

Measured through the shipped CLI on `DSCF6296.RAF`, XF16-80 at **19.2 mm f/8 — a mild case**, since both corrections are worst at the wide end and wide open: corrected against uncorrected is **worst 187 of 255, mean 6.95, and 33.5% of samples differing by more than 4 levels.** ⚠ `lens_diff`'s radial bands read ~1.00 at that aperture, so most of it is **geometry**, which that probe structurally cannot see; the recorded worst displacement on this lens is **50.59 px**.

**⚠⚠ SO THE MILESTONE'S FRAMING CHANGED: you cannot accelerate a stage that does not run.** Plan 2 is "lens correction must reach export, and then cross the seam", and the two halves belong in one milestone because the port is what pays for the fix.

**⚠⚠ MEASURED — A WHOLE EXPORT AT 26.0 Mpx, THREE RUNS** (⚠ load average **5.00–10.80**, so **decidedly not a quiet machine**):

| | |
|---|---|
| no lens correction at all — **what shipped until today** | **400.6–425.5 ms** |
| lens correction on, CPU | **1077.5–1120.5 ms** |
| lens correction on, GPU | **585.3–594.0 ms** |

**So the fix costs ~+680 ms a photo and the port pays back ~490 of it, leaving ~+170–185 ms against the old, wrong behaviour — 1.82–1.89× on the corrected export.** ⚠⚠ **That excludes the DECODE**, which is ~2.9 s at `Fast` and dominates a real per-photo export — so as a share of what a batch actually waits for, the GPU saves roughly 490 ms of ~3.5 s, about 13%. Stated rather than glossed.

**⚠ And the stage alone, on the same frame, three runs:** CPU **729.6–736.3 ms** against **168.3–189.7 ms** across the seam — **3.88–4.37×**, with a worst divergence of **0.797 of an 8-bit level over 59.9% of samples**.

**⚠⚠ THE FIELD TRAVELS AS A COARSE DISPLACEMENT GRID, AND THAT WAS SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT.** The alternative was reimplementing lensfun's distortion model in WGSL — a second definition of the correction that can disagree with `Corrector::source`, made harder by `Modifier`'s normalisation fields being **private**. `pipeline::lens_grid` samples the field on a lattice and the shader interpolates: at step 8 that is **10.9 MiB against 695 MiB per-pixel** on a 298 MiB frame, and **4.8 ms to build against the full field's 38.3**.

**⚠⚠ IT STORES DISPLACEMENT RATHER THAN POSITION FOR PRECISION, NOT INTERPOLABILITY.** Bilinear interpolation is exact for the linear part either way — a grid of absolute source positions interpolates just as well. What differs is f32 resolution: a coordinate near 6246 resolves to ~0.0005 px, where a displacement near 50 resolves to ~4e-6.

**⚠⚠ THE FIRST EQUIVALENCE TEST DIVERGED BY 75 LEVELS AND NONE OF IT WAS THE SHADER.** Ablating the three corrections localised it in one run — **distortion 48.9 levels, TCA 0.004, vignetting 0.57** — which said immediately that the sampler was fine and the lattice was not. Running at **step 1**, where the lattice is exact at every integer pixel (`tx` and `ty` are both zero), settled it: **0.00009 of a level, on all four kernels including bilinear's separate branch.**
- ⚠⚠ **So the two questions are now tested separately**: the equivalence tests run at step 1 with a bound of **0.01** — not the 1.5 first written, which would have passed against a genuine half-pixel offset — and the lattice gets a sweep of its own.
- ⚠ That separation was **learned from a failure rather than designed in**, and `with_step` exists for it, the `Weights::with_table_size` precedent.

**⚠⚠ THE SWEEP MOVED `GRID_STEP` FROM 16 TO 8, AND THEN CORRECTED ITS OWN JUSTIFICATION.** On the synthetic torture chart the cost is **0.00009 / 2.57 / 7.68 / 28.4 / 94.7 / 221.0 levels at steps 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32** — quadratic, so the sweep measures the mechanism. That is **~1000 output levels per pixel of lattice error where the spec estimated ~250**: a hard 0.1/0.9 edge through a kernel that overshoots is far steeper than the 156 levels/px an edge naively suggests.
- ⚠⚠ **But on a REAL lens the two steps are nearly the same.** `probe_lens` reads **0.0015 / 0.0020 / 0.0027 / 0.0093 / 0.0348 px at steps 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64** — essentially **floored near 0.002 px below step 32**, because there the f32 precision of the field itself dominates the interpolation. So step 8 buys about **1.35× over 16 on this lens, not 4×**, and the end-to-end divergence at step 8 measures **0.797 of a level**.
- **It ships at 8 anyway, for a reason about the *next* lens rather than this one**: the XF16-80 at 19.2 mm is a mild correction, and on a fisheye or an ultrawide the quadratic term takes over sooner, where step 8 really is 4× better. 10.9 MiB against 2.74 on a 298 MiB frame, 4.8 ms against 1.4 on a 730 ms stage — nothing to trade.
- ⚠ **Third constant in this crate swept rather than chosen**, after `MIN_GPU_BOX_PX` (low by ~8×) and `MAX_TILE_DABS` (past an 8.7× occupancy cliff). The sweep disagreed with the reasoning all three times.

**⚠⚠ THREE SCRATCH PLANES, AND IT IS THE FIRST STAGE HERE THAT NEEDS THEM FOR CORRECTNESS RATHER THAN WORKING ROOM.** Every stage before this touched only its own pixel, which is what made the chain's one-image contract hold. **A gather cannot be in place** — an output pixel reads the source anywhere within the resampler's support, and those pixels may already have been overwritten. `seed` copies the image into the planes and `gather` reads from them, two dispatches in one pass on the in-pass barrier M8.3b measured. ⚠ The spec said "no scratch planes" and was **corrected in place**.

**⚠⚠ A SABOTAGE WENT UNCAUGHT AND FORCED A TEST THAT DID NOT EXIST.** Stepping `grid_at` by `1u` instead of by `STRIDE` — reading the next lattice point's `dx` where the gain belongs — left **all six tests green**, because at step 1 the interpolation's neighbour terms are multiplied by zero and are **unreachable**. `the_shaders_grid_read_agrees_with_the_cpus` drives the interpolation directly (vignetting alone at a coarse step, against `DisplacementGrid::at` through the same lattice) and fails on it alone. ⚠ Six of seven sabotages caught, each by exactly one test; the seventh — two passes rather than one — is **unreachable from inside `encode`**, which is handed a `&mut ComputePass`, and is recorded as such rather than counted.

**⚠ The resampler weights are the CPU's own LUT, uploaded** — `Weights::lut()`, the rule `ToneCurveStage::lut` already follows: substituted, never transcribed. ⚠⚠ **Bilinear's table is deliberately EMPTY**, because it is computed exactly (`1.0 - (1.0 - f)` is not `f` in f32), so the shader branches — and a shader that only read the table would agree on three kernels and render black on the fourth. That hazard has its own test, and its sabotage fails **that one kernel alone**.

**⚠ The seam gained TWO parameters, not one.** `accelerate_prefix_stage` could not build this stage: the **`LensShot`** is not in `Edits` (it comes from the file's metadata matched against the bundled database) and neither is the **`Resampler`** (a `RenderSpec` field). Both are in hand at both call sites. ⚠ `every_other_prefix_stage_is_left_alone` broke, which is what makes adding an arm deliberate; it now names the **two analytic resamplers**, and records that they are **not** a third instance of this mechanism — perspective is a homography and geometry a rotation, and M8.5 took both from ~160 ms to ~34 with rayon rather than a GPU.

**⚠ `gpu_tail` is threaded to export as a PARAMETER, on a written-down precedent.** `ExportRender { resampler, gpu_tail }` travels `start_export → spawn → run → export_one`, never an `ExportOptions` field — `spawn`'s own doc says why about `resampler`: in `ExportOptions` it would be saved into every export preset, so a preset could disagree with the preview about how the photograph is rendered. ⚠⚠ **The naming hazard was flagged and accepted (user's call):** that setting is named for the *tail* and now decides three things. The Settings hint carries the correction — **for the third time** — by describing the rule rather than enumerating what it reaches.

**⚠ The carrier tests are what stop either half shipping green and dead.** `a_lens_profile_reaches_the_exported_pixels` goes through `export_one` rather than through `pipeline`, because **nothing in `pipeline` could ever have seen the bug — the stage itself was never broken**; and `an_accelerated_export_really_uses_the_seam` counts steps that crossed, because an accelerated export and a CPU export produce the same photograph by design. ⚠ Its fixture drives **dehaze**, not lens correction, deliberately: dehaze is already ported and needs no profile, so it says something about the **wiring** independently of the shader.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **every exported RAW changes**, which is the fix rather than a side effect, and it is the thing most likely to be reported as "my exports look different"; (2) **a corrected export is ~170–185 ms slower than the old, wrong one** even on the GPU; (3) ⚠⚠ **the camera rendering still does not reach an export either** — `ProfileRendering::default()`, inherited from `build_pipeline_spec` and **deliberately not fixed here** because mixing two pixel-changing fixes makes the diff unattributable; it is in `docs/BACKLOG.md` with a measurement named as its first task; (4) **the scoped preview path stays on the CPU by design** — the seam's twins run whole-buffer, so the preview gains only on unscoped renders (the fit rung, the warm-behind, cold entries the area gate refuses); (5) **not bit-identical, and this is the least bit-faithful GPU stage in the crate** — per-pixel stages agree to about a hundredth of a level, this one to 0.797 at the shipped step; (6) at 26 Mpx it allocates **298 MiB in, 298 MiB out and 313 MiB of scratch**, degraded to the CPU by `GpuImage::new`'s ceiling rather than to a dead worker; (7) `gpu_tail` now governs three things under a name that says "tail"; (8) **still off by default**; (9) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), one lens profile, and the bench machine was **not quiet**.

### M8.8 — a region-scoped lens correction (2026-09-15)

**M8.8 — a region-scoped lens correction (2026-09-15).** `LensCorrectionStage` implements the `input_rect_for`/`apply_region` pair, so `region_plan` stops abandoning at **step 0** and a cold entry into 1:1 scopes the **whole** prefix chain. 2473 → **2479 tests** (exactly the six added); **63 goldens ran and none moved**, and `crates/pipeline/tests` is unmodified. **Not merged, not pushed.** ✅ **CONFIRMED BY USE (2026-09-15)** — *"much better now"*, with **no defects found by using it**; the measured session is in the next-action block, and the picture half (a band at the region's edge) is a separate judgement that is not claimed. Spec `2026-09-15-lens-correction-scoped-design.md`, plan `2026-09-15-lens-correction-scoped.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE MILESTONE IS NOT THE GPU PORT, AND MEASURING BEFORE DESIGNING IS WHY.** The agreed order named *"port lens correction to the GPU"* as item 3, on two facts that are both still true: it is **~75% of the resampling prefix** and **on by default for every RAW**. What changed is that M8.7 shipped a mechanism the GPU port cannot use. Its own retraction says it plainly — a cold entry into 1:1 is **2392–2528 ms and UNSCOPED**, because `lens_correction` is step 0 and has no `input_rect_for`, and **one decline anywhere abandons the whole plan**. Every downstream step already accepted a region and got nothing. So the two candidates are not alternatives on one axis: the port attacks one stage whole-buffer, the pair **unlocks the chain M8.7 already built**. The fork was put to the user rather than decided, and he chose scoping first with a re-measurement after.

**⚠⚠ THE FIELD IS 5–6% OF THE STAGE, AND THAT ONE NUMBER RESHAPED THE MILESTONE TWICE.** `probe_lens` (kept) was written **before the spec**, because this file's own recorded numbers for the stage do not compose — it holds *"400 ms field + 765 ms resampler"* from the per-pixel era beside a 309 ms whole resampling prefix after row batching, and both cannot describe the same stage. Measured on `DSCF6296.RAF`:

| | 6.5 Mpx (rung 3123) | **26.0 Mpx (1:1)** |
|---|---|---|
| the whole stage | 169.0 ms | **650.2–695.8 ms** |
| the displacement **field** | 10.0 ms | **35.6–36.1 ms** |
| the **resampling**, by difference | 150.7 ms | **597.5–646.8 ms** |

It says the GPU port would be attacking the 94% (a real target), **and** it says a scoped render pays almost nothing for computing the field over a wider row than it uses — which is what makes the bit-identity rule below affordable.

**⚠⚠ MEASURED THROUGH THE SHIPPED PATH, COLD, RESUMING AT STEP 0.** `build_prefix_steps` → `region_plan(steps, 0, ..)` → `run_region_plan`, six runs on the reporter's own chain `lens_correction → perspective → geometry → noise_reduction → dehaze` (⚠ load 4.3–7.7, **not a quiet machine**, which biases the whole-buffer column and so the ratio optimistically):

| the cold prefix | |
|---|---|
| whole-buffer, every step | **1689–1869 ms** |
| **region-scoped from step 0** | **218–225 ms** |
| | **7.5–8.5×** |

⚠ That is the **prefix alone, headless** — no tail, no pack, no decode — so it is **not** the app's 2392–2528 ms figure and must not be quoted as one. ⚠⚠ **And it is still not a session**: the row that decides this is a cold entry through `RUSTROOM_DEBUG_RENDER`, and *a bench prices a stage, not a session* has corrected two milestones' headlines already.

**⚠⚠ PER STEP, AND LENS CORRECTION IS STILL 54% OF THE SCOPED CHAIN.** `lens_correction` **118.1–118.6 ms** at 2210×1744, `perspective` 18.9–21.7 at 1868×1490, `geometry` 14.1–14.3 at 1792×1394, `noise_reduction` 34.2–35.7 at 1712×1314, `dehaze` 34.2–37.6 at 1432×1034. ⚠ It leads **because it is first**: every step below shrinks the rect, so the top of the chain carries the largest margined area — **3.9 Mpx against dehaze's 1.5**, and **14.8% of the frame** against `SCOPE_MAX_AREA_PCT`'s 50, so the gate has ample room.

**⚠⚠ THE MARGIN IS THE ONE REAL HAZARD, AND THE DESIGN'S OWN ARGUMENT FOR IT WAS TOO LOOSE — corrected in the spec in place during execution.** The spec said *"a radial map bows every edge, so a corner bound is unsound"*. The precise condition is sharper: ptlens is `r_d = r · (b·r² + (1 − b))`, so the radial factor **increases** with `r` for a **pincushion** correction (`b > 0`) — and then every extreme of a rect's image really does sit at a corner, so `PerspectiveStage`'s four-corner bound *would* be sound. It **decreases** for a **barrel** correction (`b < 0`), and the extreme then sits at an **edge midpoint** whenever the rect's span brackets the optical centre. Measured on a 400×300 fixture at `b = −0.05`: the corner box misses by **9.2 px**, against a Lanczos3 tap radius of 3. The bound that is sound either way is the **largest displacement anywhere in the frame** — no pixel can move further than the furthest-moving pixel, whatever shape the rect is. On the real lens that is **50.59 px**, so `margin = ceil(50.59) + 1 + radius`.

- **⚠⚠ AND THE BYTE-FOR-BYTE EQUIVALENCE TEST CANNOT SEE ANY OF IT.** Transplanting `PerspectiveStage`'s corner bound into `input_rect_for` **passes** `a_region_matches_the_same_part_of_the_whole` and fails `every_source_a_region_reads_lies_inside_the_rect_it_asked_for`, which is the whole reason that second test exists. ⚠ It sweeps **both signs of `b`** and uses rects that **bracket the centre in both axes**, because a pincushion-only fixture, or rects inside one quadrant, cannot witness the bulge however large the displacement.
- **⚠ `Corrector::margin(pad)` is ONE definition**, read by the stage and by the test that guarantees it. Two derivations of a margin is how a bound and the thing it bounds come to disagree — and here they disagree as a **band at the region's edge**, a plausible photograph rather than an error.
- **⚠⚠ `no_pixel_displaces_further_than_the_margin`'s `pad` RUNS FROM ZERO, and that is what makes it discriminating at all.** With a resampler's tap radius in the margin there are two free pixels for an under-estimate to hide behind: dropping the ceiling **and** the slack still **passes** at `pad = 2`, because truncation loses at most one pixel and the pad absorbs it. At `pad = 0` the same sabotage fails at *"a pixel displaced 135.65 px, past a margin of 135"*. **A test whose own parameter carries slack cannot see slack being removed.**
- **⚠ Two sabotages of `compute_max_displacement` are INERT and are recorded rather than counted.** Probing the frame's four corners alone passes, and never sampling the last row passes — because a lensfun distortion model is radial about a centre and monotone in radius at ordinary coefficients, so any border probe finds the maximum. The row sampling is **defence in depth** for a profile declaring a decentred optical axis (`center_x`/`center_y`, private in `Modifier`) or a non-monotone `poly5`; neither exists in this catalogue, so no test here can distinguish the two, and it costs ~2 ms on a 700 ms stage.

**⚠⚠ `apply` IS `apply_region` AT FULL EXTENT, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE TWO BIT-IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY COMPARISON.** `geometry::rotate`'s rule, for `geometry::rotate`'s reason: two implementations that must agree is how they come to disagree. The refactor landed as **its own commit**, and its acceptance was that the stage's own tests and all 63 goldens passed **unchanged** with `crates/pipeline/tests` unmodified.

**⚠⚠ THE FIELD STARTS AT x = 0 AND STOPS AT THE RECT'S RIGHT EDGE, AND THE TWO HALVES HAVE DIFFERENT REASONS.** It cannot **start** at the rect: `apply_geometry_distortion` computes each `x` as `(xu + ns * i as f64) as f32` — **from scratch per `i`, not incrementally** — so starting at `rect.x` re-associates an f64 addition, and f64 addition is not associative. The discrepancy is ~1e-16 against an f32 spacing of ~1.2e-7, so about **one pixel in 1e9** could round differently: a faint band that appears one pixel in a billion, which is precisely the class of thing this project has paid for. It *can* **stop** at the rect, because truncating the row changes **how many** `i` are computed and not **what any of them is**. ⚠ Measured at ~2 ms of a 120 ms step — within this machine's own spread at load 7.4 — so it is recorded as **free rather than as a win**.

**⚠⚠ THE CARRIER ASSERTS THE PLAN'S LENGTH, NOT MERELY THAT SCOPING HAPPENED.** A scoped render and a whole-buffer one produce the same picture by design, so every correctness test in the workspace — all 63 goldens included — passes with the pair deleted. That is the W5 failure mode. ⚠⚠ **And a test asking only *did it scope* would pass against M8.7**, the version that left a cold entry unscoped: there `region_plan` was only ever reached with `start >= 1`. `a_cold_chain_scopes_from_lens_correction` asserts `plan.out_rects.len() == steps.len()`, plus a fixture check that the margin really grew the request. ⚠ Sabotage: restoring the decline fails **exactly the three tests M8.8 adds** and leaves **487** others green.

- **⚠ `src.full`, never the slice in hand.** The corrector is built against the **frame** — its centre, its normalisation and its autoscale are all properties of the frame — so building it from `src.buf` corrects a different lens. M8.6's centre sabotage in this stage's costume; sabotaged and caught at `left: [0.874, ...] right: [0.100, ...]`.
- **⚠ `output_dims` keeps the trait's identity default**, because lens correction preserves dimensions. `PrefixStepKey` is untouched — a scoped output is never cached, so no key can go stale — and **the gate in `render_cached` needed no change at all**: it reads `plan.out_rects.first()`, which is simply lens correction's margined rect now.
- **⚠ `resample::sample_channel_region` is a fourth entry point**, the per-channel mirror of `sample_region`, and it exists for the reason that one does: TCA gives each channel its own source point.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ✅ **confirmed by use, but narrowly** — the session's own cold entries ran a **one-step** chain, so the headless five-step figure (7.5–8.5×) is corroborated by nothing but its own measurement, and the **picture** half is still a judgement nobody has made; (2) **nothing for a photo carrying spots** — `spot_removal` sits between perspective and geometry and still declines, so that chain cannot scope above `geometry`, and it is anchored to `GeometryStage`'s input so a patch survives a crop, which is worth more than the scoping; (3) **nothing for export or the fit rung**, both whole-buffer — and export is now where the GPU port's value lives; (4) **the settle still spends a whole-buffer render in the background**, M8.7's accepted caveat (4) rather than a new one; (5) **the margin is frame-global**, so it is coarser than a per-rect bound — 14.8% of the frame on the chain that matters, and it becomes expensive only for a lens whose worst displacement is a large fraction of the frame, which none in this catalogue is; (6) **lens correction is still 54% of the scoped chain**, so the GPU port is not retired by this — it is re-priced; (7) one machine, one photograph, one lens profile, and the bench machine was **not quiet** (load 4.3–7.7).

### The device-limit crash, and the vignette measured (2026-09-13) — both from ONE report, and neither was the…

**The device-limit crash, and the vignette measured (2026-09-13) — both from ONE report, and neither was the milestone it arrived against. ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works"*; 1:1 with a GPU prefix stage renders rather than killing the worker.** Reported as *"after zooming to 1:1, none of the edit sliders seem to change the image displayed, but the thumbnail changes. After moving to a different photo and back, it works again. Also, vignetting at full quality seems still quite slow with the gpu."* 2415 → **2417 tests** (exactly the two added); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, 0 GPU skips. No spec, no plan: one root-caused crash and one measurement.

**⚠⚠ THE FIRST HALF IS A DEAD RENDER WORKER, AND THE SYMPTOM NAMED IT PRECISELY.** Three facts and only one explanation fits: the **thumbnail kept updating**, so `Edits` was genuinely changing; the **canvas was frozen**, so nothing was rendering; and a **photo switch cured it**, which is exactly what builds a new `RenderEngine` and therefore a new worker thread. ⚠ The reporter's own sentence is the diagnosis — the third clause is what rules out a stale-cache or a stale-key theory, since a wrong key would still produce *a* frame. **The nineteenth time in this file that reading a report literally has out-diagnosed reasoning about it.**

- **⚠⚠ THE CAUSE: `DeviceDescriptor::default()` REQUESTS THE DOWNLEVEL FLOOR, AND THE CEILING IS THE `min` OF TWO LIMITS — taking one of them is how this was missed.** A resident image is allocated as a buffer **and** bound whole as a storage buffer, so `max_buffer_size` (256 MiB) and `max_storage_buffer_binding_size` (**128 MiB**) both apply and the *binding* is the tighter one. A full-resolution X-T4 frame is 6246 × 4170 RGB f32 = **298.1 MiB**, so it failed validation. ⚠ Measured on this machine: the M2 offers **9093 MiB** per buffer and **4096 MiB** per binding — **32× what we had opted into**, for nothing.
- **⚠⚠ AND WGPU REPORTS A VALIDATION FAILURE BY *PANICKING*, NOT BY RETURNING AN ERROR.** `create_buffer` aborts the calling thread through the uncaptured-error handler. The calling thread is the render worker, so one oversized frame ended rendering for the rest of the session. The log is unambiguous: `Buffer size 312549840 is greater than the maximum buffer size (268435456)` — and **312,549,840 = 6246 × 4170 × 3 × 4**, which is what identified the buffer exactly rather than by inference.
- **⚠⚠ IT NEEDED 1:1 *AND* A GPU-ACCELERATED PREFIX STAGE, WHICH IS WHY IT APPEARED ONLY NOW.** The **prefix always runs whole-buffer**; the tail at a native rung runs on a viewport-bounded **region**. So only a prefix stage can allocate a full-resolution image — and dehaze became the first one with a GPU twin at **M8.3o, yesterday**. ⚠ That is also why rung 3200 never showed it: 6.8 Mpx is 78.2 MiB, comfortably under even the old ceiling.
- **⚠ The fix is three parts and no one of them is sufficient.** (1) Request `adapter.limits()`, which cannot make `request_device` fail where the default succeeded, since those limits are by definition the adapter's own. (2) **Gate `GpuImage::new` on the device ceiling**, so a device that genuinely cannot take the frame degrades to the CPU twin rather than dying — every caller already handles `None`. (3) **`guarded`**, a `catch_unwind` around the GPU attempt **alone**, so any residual wgpu panic becomes a CPU fallback; scoped to the attempt so a panic in the *CPU* pipeline stays loud, and it prints once per occurrence so a performance cliff is not silent.
- **⚠⚠ THE TWO SABOTAGES BOTH DISCRIMINATED, AND THE FIRST ONE FAILED BY PANICKING RATHER THAN BY ASSERTING** — which is the point: a missing gate here does not return a wrong value, it aborts the thread. Deleting the ceiling check fails `an_image_past_the_devices_ceiling_is_refused_rather_than_allocated`; restoring `Limits::default()` fails `a_full_resolution_frame_fits_this_device` with *"needed 312549840 bytes, device allows 134217728"* — **the original crash, now as a clean assertion.**
- **⚠ `bench_preview` is NOT a reproduction of this, and believing it was would have shipped the fix unproven.** It ran clean on `DSCF6296.RAF` — because its buffer is **3123×2085 (6.5 Mpx, 74.5 MiB)**, the half-size preview decode, under even the old ceiling. The end-to-end proof is a real `GpuChain` over a **6246×4170** image, which now completes with `up=1 down=1`; a throwaway example did that and was deleted.
- **⚠ Clippy caught what 2417 passing tests did not, for at least the twenty-first time**, and it corrected a factual belief rather than a style: `max_storage_buffer_binding_size` is **`u64` in wgpu 29**, not the `u32` the `u64::from` assumed. The *value* was right and the type was not.

**⚠⚠ THE SECOND HALF IS THE MORE USEFUL FINDING: THE VIGNETTE IS NOT WHAT IS SLOW, AND IT CANNOT BE.** Measured through the real engine at rung 3200 — what a fitted photo renders at on a large HiDPI window with `drag_quality: Full`, which is this user's setting — on DSCF6291.RAF, load 4.82:

  | whole frame at rung 3200 (~6.5 Mpx) | CPU | GPU | |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **vignette −60, elliptical** | 48.60 ms | **28.70** | 1.69× |
  | **vignette −60, roundness −60** | 72.85 | **28.00** | 2.60× |
  | *unedited, colorimetric — the floor* | *43.09* | ***27.28*** | *1.58×* |
  | hsl only, for contrast | 121.75 | 27.27 | 4.46× |

- **⚠⚠ THE FLOOR ROW IS THE ANSWER. A GPU frame with an elliptical vignette is 28.70 ms and a frame with NO EDITS AT ALL is 27.28 — so the vignette itself costs 1.4 ms of a 28.7 ms frame.** What is being felt is the **frame floor at rung 3200**, which is ~27 ms ≈ **37 fps**, and every stage pays it. ⚠ The same reading explains the modest **1.69×**: the vignette is only **5.5 ms of CPU work**, so there is only 5.5 ms available to win — a cheap stage cannot produce a large ratio when both columns share a 27 ms floor. **The ratio is low because the stage is cheap, not because the shader is underperforming.** (The superellipse, which is 29.8 ms of CPU work, duly reads 2.60×.)
- **⚠ Decomposed rather than inferred** (`probe_breakdown`, 3200×2136, best of 5): staging memcpy **2.61 ms**, upload copy **6.29**, four dispatches **11.63**, byte-path download **4.88**. So a two-stage vignette chain is roughly **13.8 ms of pure transfer** before any arithmetic, and the rest of the floor is the CPU-side frame work the GPU never touches — the prefix clone, `downscale_to` and `pack`.
- **⚠⚠ THE LEVER THE USER ALREADY HAS IS A RUNG, AND IT IS WORTH 4×.** The identical frame at rung 1600 is **7.17 ms (139 fps)** against 28.70. `Settings → drag_quality: Faster` drops one rung during a gesture and restores full quality on release — which is the interactive-rung feature doing exactly what it was built for. ⚠ At `Full` there is deliberately no drop, so a fitted photo renders 6.5 Mpx on **every frame of every drag**.
- **⚠ The structural lever is the resident buffer across the prefix→tail seam** (`docs/BACKLOG.md`, head of `## Performance`), not the vignette shader. ⚠⚠ But it **does not help this case**: a vignette-only edit has no GPU prefix stage, so there is only one round trip to pay and nothing to share. It helps a *dehaze* drag, where the trip is paid twice.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **the frame floor at rung 3200 is unchanged by any of this** — nothing here made the vignette faster, it established that the vignette was not the cost; (2) the measurement is one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal) and the bench machine was **not quiet** (load 4.82), which biases the CPU column and so the ratios slightly optimistic; (3) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.

### M8.6 — a region-scoped prefix for the analytic resamplers (2026-09-13). ⚠⚠ ITS HEADLINE IS RETRACTED, AND O…

**M8.6 — a region-scoped prefix for the analytic resamplers (2026-09-13). ⚠⚠ ITS HEADLINE IS RETRACTED, AND ON THE REPORTER'S OWN PHOTOGRAPH THIS MILESTONE DOES NOTHING AT ALL — read the retraction below before anything else in this section.** During a Straighten or Perspective drag the prefix's last step produces only the sub-rect the tail is about to crop to. ~~A Straighten drag at 1:1 goes 145.3–154.9 → 11.2–12.2 ms, 12.5–13.3×~~ — that row prices a **stage** against a resume the app cannot perform. **Bit-identical**, which is the one claim of the three that held. 2428 → **2437 tests** (exactly the nine added); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, 0 GPU skips. **Not merged, not pushed.** Spec `2026-09-13-region-scoped-prefix-design.md`, plan `2026-09-13-region-scoped-prefix.md`.

### ⚠⚠ THE RETRACTION (2026-09-14), IN THREE PARTS

**⚠⚠ THE RETRACTION (2026-09-14), IN THREE PARTS.** Reported on first use as *"It's even slower now"* — the exact opposite of a 13× — and after the cache fix below as *"still on the same level as before, maybe slightly faster but still not acceptable"*.

- **⚠⚠ (1) THE GATE NEVER FIRED ONCE.** `scoped no` on all 22 instrumented frames. The reporter's chain is `lens_correction → perspective → geometry → noise_reduction → dehaze`, so geometry is **not** the last prefix step and `start + 1 == steps.len()` cannot engage. ⚠⚠ **That is accepted caveat (1) word for word** — written down, knowing NR and dehaze exist, and filed as an edge case rather than as *"this milestone is inert for the person who asked for it"*. **A caveat naming a configuration is worth checking against the configuration the reporter actually has**, and that check costs one sidecar read.

- **⚠⚠ (2) THE 13× IS A PROBE ROW, NOT A SESSION.** `probe_resamplers`' drag rows hold their checkpoints in a hand-built `Vec`, so `11.2–12.2 ms` is what the **stage** costs once every upstream checkpoint is warm *and valid* — a resume the app could not perform here for two independent reasons (the gate, and the cache bug below). ⚠ **This file already records the rule and it was reached for anyway**: the interactive rung's own section says *"a synthetic bench prices a stage, not a session"*, after a bench understated the app by 2.6× on 2026-09-07.

- **⚠ (3) AND THE SLOWDOWN WAS NOT M8.6's DOING** — it was a latent `PrefixCache` eviction bug that this milestone's instrumentation finally made visible. Its section is **"The prefix cache evicted the checkpoint a drag resumes from"** below.

**⚠⚠ WHAT THE RUNNING APP ACTUALLY COSTS**, `RUSTROOM_DEBUG_RENDER` on the reporter's machine at 1:1, after the cache fix:

```
prefix: ["lens_correction","perspective","geometry","noise_reduction","dehaze"]  resuming at 1 of 5
  [1] perspective      184.3 ms  -> 6246x4170 (26.0 Mpx)
  [2] geometry         178.4 ms
  [3] noise_reduction  287.3 ms
  [4] dehaze           360.6 ms
render: 1029.9 ms  rung 6246  frame 1502x1219 (1.8 Mpx)  prefix_ran 4  scoped no
```

**⚠⚠ NR AND DEHAZE ARE 648 OF THOSE 1030 ms — 63% — AND THEY RE-RUN AT 26 Mpx TO DISPLAY 1.8.** So scoping the whole prefix from the dragged step onward is not a refinement of M8.6; it is where the win is, and M8.6 is its seam.

**⚠⚠ AND "ONLY THE LAST STEP CAN EVER BE REGION-SCOPED" IS TOO STRONG — corrected here rather than in place, because the argument below is sound and its *conclusion* is not.** It reads: *"step n−1's region-scoped output cannot feed step n, because step n is a gather that reads anywhere in its source."* True **of two gathers in a row**, and this prefix is never that: its gathers (lens correction, perspective, geometry) all precede its locals (noise reduction, dehaze). Working backwards from the visible rect, each local needs only a **margin** — which is `tail_kernel_radius`'s existing job, already trusted for the tail — and the first scoped step is a gather reading a whole cached buffer, the case that is already sound. What is genuinely forbidden is a gather in the **middle**, which `build_prefix_steps` cannot produce. ⚠ At 1:1 the margin is roughly 110 px (dehaze's refine 60 + patch 20, NR's chroma up to 32), so a 1.8 Mpx region becomes ~2.3 against 26 — the win survives it comfortably.

**⚠ WHAT M8.6 IS WORTH, STATED PLAINLY: the seam, and nothing else today.** `OutRect`, `output_dims`, `apply_region`, the two `_region` gathers and the vignette-fixture acceptance test are a strict subset of what a prefix-wide version needs; only the **gate** changes. That is why it was kept rather than reverted — but it ships no user-visible win on the chain it was built for, and the sections below should be read with that in front of them.

**⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE IS THAT IT DISPLACES ITEM 3 RATHER THAN FOLLOWING IT, AND ONE PROBE ROW SAID SO BEFORE ANY DESIGN.** The next-action block named *"port lens correction"*, which is **~75% of the resampling prefix** and **on by default for every RAW** — both true. But a drag re-runs only its own prefix step and everything downstream, and **lens correction's checkpoint is keyed on edits a Straighten drag never touches, so it stays valid throughout and contributes EXACTLY ZERO to that gesture.** Item 3 is the right answer to a cold render and a rung change (the 967.8–1002.1 ms row); it is the wrong answer to *"the straighten drag is slow"*. ⚠ **That is M8.3q's lesson arriving a second time — the row that matters is a DRAG, not a stage** — and this file's own next-action block did not carry it either time.

  Measured on `DSCF6296.RAF`, Catmull-Rom, lens profile matched, 8 threads, three runs. ⚠ Load 5.2–7.1, so **not a quiet machine**.

  | what a drag actually costs | fitted rung (6.5 Mpx) | **1:1 (26.0 Mpx)** |
  |---|---|---|
  | `geometry` — the step Straighten invalidates | 33.4 ms | 138.2–188.5 |
  | **a Straighten drag frame, whole-buffer** | **40.6 ms / 25 fps** | **145.3–154.9 / ~6.6 fps** |
  | **the same drag, REGION-SCOPED** | *—, see caveat 5* | **11.2–12.2 / ~85 fps** |
  | *a `lens_correction` drag, for contrast* | *259.9* | *967.8–1002.1* |

- **⚠⚠ THE STRUCTURAL CAUSE: THE PREFIX RUNS WHOLE-BUFFER WHILE THE TAIL RENDERS A REGION.** `render_engine.rs` says it plainly — *"The prefix never depends on the region, so the whole chain is built and cached without one."* At 1:1 geometry therefore resamples all 26 Mpx to show a 1400×900 slice, **about 20× more pixels than are on screen**. ⚠⚠ That is **correct for caching** — keeping the region out of the key is what makes panning free — and **worth nothing during a drag**, because the dragged step is invalidated every frame by construction, so its whole-buffer output is computed and thrown away.

- **⚠⚠ IT BEAT ITS OWN PROJECTION (~26 ms) BECAUSE `apply_region` BORROWS WHERE `apply` CONSUMES.** The consuming signature — the ownership that keeps the GPU seam clean — makes the normal path clone the whole 26 Mpx checkpoint, **measured at 8.4 ms**, and that clone does not shrink with the region. A gather only *reads* its source, so the region path takes `&ImageBuf` and pays none of it. **The spec named this; the projection forgot to subtract it.**

- **⚠⚠ `rotate` IS `rotate_region` AT FULL EXTENT, WHICH MAKES THE TWO BIT-IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY COMPARISON.** One implementation, so there is nothing that can drift. `PerspectiveStage::apply` is `render` at full extent for the same reason. ⚠ The evidence the refactor moved nothing is that **all 17 pre-existing geometry tests and all 54 perspective tests passed unchanged** through it.

- **⚠⚠ AND THAT PROPERTY MADE THE CENTRE SABOTAGE INVISIBLE TO EVERY GOLDEN — the plan predicted they would fail and they did not.** Centring the rotation on the **sub-rect** instead of the frame is the one way to get this wrong, and it produces a plausible photograph of the wrong part of the frame. But at full extent `rect.x0 + (rect.w−1)/2` **is** `(w−1)/2`, so the whole-buffer path is bit-identical under it and the 63 goldens stay green. **The region test is the only thing in the workspace that can see it** — it failed at `sample 0 of 4992 differs`, and perspective's equivalent at `sample 0 of 1071`.

- **⚠ The gate is DERIVED, not a flag.** Engage when **exactly the last prefix step needs re-running** (`start + 1 == steps.len()`) and that step accepts a region. `render_cached` already knows both, so there is no drag signal to plumb and nothing that can disagree with anything else — the rule `Session::geometry_mode` was deleted for. ⚠ At the fitted rung the region is `None`, so it never engages there; it engages exactly at the native rungs, which is where the cost is.

- **⚠⚠ ONLY THE LAST STEP CAN EVER BE REGION-SCOPED, AND THAT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A v1 LIMIT.** Chaining two is impossible: step *n−1*'s region-scoped output cannot feed step *n*, because step *n* is a gather that reads **anywhere** in its source. Sound chaining needs pre-image analysis per stage, which is the whole thing this design avoids.

- **⚠ `None` is what makes every other stage decline BY CONSTRUCTION.** `apply_region` is a defaulted `PipelineStage` method — the fifth — returning `None`, so dehaze, noise reduction, spot removal and the masked capture corrections inherit the refusal rather than being name-checked out by the caller. The rule `GpuStage::cpu()` already follows: **fail toward the whole-buffer path**, where a wrong answer costs milliseconds and never pixels.

- **⚠⚠ THE SHARPEST HAZARD: THE FRAME'S DIMENSIONS MUST COME FROM THE PREDICTION, NEVER FROM THE BUFFER.** `(pw, ph)` feeds `CoverageSpec { fw, fh }` — what every brush mask's coverage is rasterised at — and the tail's `Region { full_w, full_h }`. On the region path that buffer **is** the region, so taking its size would rasterise every mask at the region's size and thrash the coverage cache on every pan. Hence the second defaulted method, `output_dims`, read *before* the step runs. ⚠ Its identity default is correct for every stage today and **silently wrong for a future dim-changing one**, which `every_prefix_stages_output_dims_match_what_it_produces` guards — total over the whole prefix, and it caught the sabotage with *"`geometry` predicted (37, 23) and produced (23, 37)"*.

- **⚠⚠ AND THE TEST FOR THAT HAZARD NEEDED A VIGNETTE IN ITS FIXTURE, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL FINDING OF THE MILESTONE.** The obvious observable — `frame.fit_size` — is **derived from the buffer and the geometry, not from `(pw, ph)`**, so a test asserting on it would have named the hazard and been unable to detect it. What *can* see it is a **position-dependent tail stage**: the vignette's falloff is measured against the frame, so wrong dimensions re-centre it and the bytes differ. `a_region_scoped_render_matches_the_whole_buffer_path_byte_for_byte` carries one, and sabotaging the dims fails **that test alone** — 64 passed, 1 failed.

- **⚠ The two paths are forced apart by the CACHE, not by a flag.** That acceptance test warms a final checkpoint so the gate *cannot* fire, renders the region through `img.crop`, then renders it again on a cold cache so the gate does, and compares byte for byte. Both halves assert their own fixture check first, or the comparison would be of one path against itself.

- **⚠⚠ THE REGION-SCOPED OUTPUT IS NEVER CACHED, and that is structural rather than guarded.** A region-scoped checkpoint served for a *different* region is the one failure here that shows as a plausible photograph rather than an error. The branch simply does not call `cache.insert`. ⚠ Its guard is that a second identical render must scope **again** — if a final had been stored it would resume there instead.

- **⚠ Clippy caught what 2437 passing tests did not, for at least the twenty-third time**, and it was the recorded trap rather than a style point: inserting the new test fixtures **separated `full_prefix`'s doc comment from its function**, so `empty_line_after_doc_comments` fired with `CLIPPY=101` against `TEST=0`. The same class as M8.3g's insertion silently reattaching an `#[allow]` to the wrong item. ⚠ The gate was re-run *after* the fix rather than the earlier green being quoted — M8.3n's lesson that **a gate run before the last fix describes a tree nobody shipped**.

- **⚠ `crop_bounds` was extracted first, as a pure refactor**, so `apply_crop` and `output_dims` read one rule. Two derivations of where the crop starts is how a predicted output size and the real one come to disagree. ⚠ Found in passing and deliberately **not** fixed: a `CropRect` with `left == 1.0` makes `clamp(x0 + 1, w)` panic, pre-existing and unreachable from the crop tool — fixing it inside a refactor whose acceptance is "no behaviour moved" would have hidden the change.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **a photo with dehaze or noise reduction active gets nothing**, since geometry is then not the last step — ⚠⚠ **RETRACTED 2026-09-14 — BOTH HALVES OF THAT SENTENCE ARE WRONG, AND THIS IS THE CAVEAT THAT DESCRIBES THE REPORTER'S OWN PHOTOGRAPH.** NR *and* dehaze can both be region-scoped behind a margin, which is exactly what their `tail_kernel_radius` machinery already computes for the tail; and dehaze's airlight is **not** re-estimated per region unless someone lets it be — it already runs on a **fixed 256 px downscale** (M8.3o, deliberately, *"so the estimate cannot vary with the render scale"*), so it is computed once from the whole checkpoint and passed in, the shape `GpuDehazeStage::new(image)` already has. ⚠⚠ **And note what this caveat was**: a one-clause aside that names the exact configuration the person who asked for the milestone was editing in, written down and filed as an edge case. See the retraction at the head of this section; (2) ⚠ **a Perspective drag qualifies only when geometry is inactive**, since geometry follows it and only the last step can be scoped — included anyway because it was the same fifteen lines, but most photographs carrying a perspective correction also carry a crop; (3) ⚠ **a photo turned 90° or mirrored gets nothing**, because `orient` runs whole-buffer inside `apply` and that case declines — uncommon, since a camera's portrait orientation is applied at decode through `sizes.flip` rather than through `Edits::orientation`; (4) **a tail slider after a straighten pays ~5 ms extra** at a native rung until a whole-buffer render rebuilds the final checkpoint, against 145 ms today; (5) **nothing at the fitted rung**, where the region is `None` — a fitted drag stays at 40.6 ms and `drag_quality: Faster` remains the lever there; (6) **nothing for a lens-correction drag**, the ~1 s row, which is item 3's territory and re-runs everything downstream of it; (7) one machine, one photograph, and the bench machine was **not quiet** (load 5.2–7.1).

### M8.7 plan 1 — the region-scoped prefix, headless (2026-09-14)

**M8.7 plan 1 — the region-scoped prefix, headless (2026-09-14).** Everything `pipeline` needs to
region-scope a CHAIN of prefix steps: one `Rect` type, `input_rect_for` on four stages, a chainable
`apply_region`, the `region_plan` backwards walk, `run_region_plan`, and a deterministic dehaze
airlight. 2439 → **2467 tests** (exactly the twenty-eight added); **63 goldens ran and none moved**.
Spec `2026-09-14-region-scoped-prefix-whole-design.md`, plan
`2026-09-14-region-scoped-prefix-headless.md`. ⚠⚠ **NOTHING CALLS `region_plan` YET** — plan 2 is
the wiring, and until it exists this is a capability with no user-visible effect, which is the W5
failure mode held deliberately.

**⚠⚠ THE SEAM IS A PAIR, AND A STAGE IMPLEMENTING ONE HALF IS A BUG.** `input_rect_for(out, in_w,
in_h) -> Option<Rect>` is the mirror of `apply_region`: given an output rect, what input does this
stage read? **`None` is the default, so lens correction, spot removal and the masked captures all
decline by construction** rather than being name-checked. ⚠ `GeometryStage` declines on a
non-identity orientation in *both* halves, and its test asserts that agreement directly — a plan
built from one half and executed by the other must never disagree about what is possible.

**⚠⚠ AND THE RECORDED ~110 px MARGIN WAS WRONG TWICE OVER.** A guided base reaches **2r**, which
this repo already wrote down in `local_contrast::kernel_reach`, so dehaze's refine reaches 120 and
not 60 → **140** with the patch. And **`CHROMA_PASSES` is 2**, so NR's chroma blur reaches
`passes × radius` → **64 at smoothness 100**, not 32. ⚠ The second of those was **my own
implementation repeating the first error one level down**, hours after writing the correction, and
it was invisible to review — only the byte-for-byte chain test caught it.

**⚠⚠ BYTE-FOR-BYTE IS ACHIEVABLE FOR GATHERS AND NOT FOR LOCALS, AND THE SPEC ASSERTED OTHERWISE.**
`box_blur` keeps a running sum, so it reaches each position by a different history of adds and
subtracts depending on where the row starts — the third CPU divergence class this file already
records, which shows up between two CPU runs too. Measured at **3.6e-7 absolute, one ulp, 0.00009 of
an 8-bit level**, scattered rather than banded. So there are two acceptance tests asserting the two
strongest **true** properties: `a_chain_of_gathers_is_byte_for_byte` and
`a_chain_with_a_local_agrees_to_within_a_rounding`. ⚠ A margin bug reads as a **band at one edge**
and blows the second bound by orders of magnitude, so it still catches what matters.

**⚠⚠ THE AIRLIGHT: THREE CANDIDATES MEASURED, AND THE INSTABILITY BELONGS TO THE ESTIMATOR.**
`airlight_shift` (kept) on three real frames, in 8-bit levels:

| candidate | vs today | drift under a drag |
|---|---|---|
| **256 px prefix replay** (shipped) | **5.6** | 0.009–24.3 |
| carry the last true value | 0 | **3.2 for ONE degree, 21.5 over five** |
| once from the source buffer | — | 0 by construction, but **25–95 off the truth** |

⚠⚠ **The source-buffer candidate is DEAD and CLAUDE.md's own warning understated it**: a *mild*
0.1–0.9 crop moves DSCF6291's true airlight 0.334 → 0.635, **65 levels**, because the crop removes
dark borders and the brightest 0.1% changes completely. ⚠⚠ **And the true airlight is itself unstable
— so today's app already wobbles up to 21 levels during a Straighten drag with dehaze active**,
because it recomputes every frame from the freshly-rotated buffer. "Match today exactly" means
matching something unstable. **Backlogged separately: a more robust estimator (a higher percentile,
or a larger sample) is its own change.**

- **⚠⚠ THE REPLAY RUNS FROM THE START OF THE PREFIX, NEVER FROM THE RESUME POINT.** Replaying from
  wherever a render resumes would make the airlight depend on **which slider was dragged** — the
  shape `render_max_dim`, `fit_image_size` and `Session::geometry_mode` were each deleted for. It is
  also what makes `PrefixKey` sound without carrying the airlight: the key already covers every edit
  the replay reads, and `the_replay_does_not_depend_on_where_a_render_resumes` asserts a tail edit
  cannot move it.
- **⚠⚠ `render_once` WAS A SECOND DEFINITION, AND THE MASTER INVARIANT CAUGHT IT.** It built through
  `RenderSpec::default()`, so it estimated from its input while `render_cached` replayed — and being
  **by construction the reference the cached path is tested against**,
  `every_cached_frame_matches_a_cold_render` failed at **one 8-bit level scattered across the
  frame**. ⚠ The whole point of the change is removing two definitions that can disagree, and making
  it introduced one. It takes a `lens` parameter rather than `None` because *"exact whenever the
  engine happens to be lens-less"* is a coincidence, not a guarantee.
- **⚠⚠ NO GOLDEN MOVES, AND THE 63 ARE STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO THIS.** Not inert — a wrong airlight
  fails `golden_dehaze_plus` and `golden_dehaze_minus` precisely. They do not move because **every
  chart's long edge is ≤ 256 and `AIRLIGHT_SAMPLE` is 256**, so `downscale_to` returns a clone and
  the replay reproduces today's value exactly. **The 5.6-level shift comes ENTIRELY from the
  downscale.** ⚠ So the goldens **cannot guard the airlight on real-sized images** — a future reader
  will assume they do. `airlight_shift` is the only instrument that can see it.

- **⚠⚠ `run_region_plan` IS IN `pipeline`, NOT THE ENGINE, AND THE PLAN HAD THAT WRONG.** Chain
  execution is **pure** — only the caching and the gate need an engine — so putting it here is what

  been added for noise reduction and dehaze and the forward half never was, so **the two stages
  carrying 76% of the win could not be region-scoped at all** — and every test passed, because
  nothing executed a chain.

- **⚠ Nine defects in the plan, found by executing it, none visible to the tests the plan
  specified.** `sed`'s `\b` (BSD has none, exit 0, nothing changed); a blanket field rename that

  a **private module**, so a reach and its caller cannot be separate commits; `input_rect_for`

  and `render_once`. ⚠ **A test on a concrete type cannot tell a trait method from an inherent one**,
  and the caller is `dyn` — `the_back_projections_are_reachable_through_the_trait_object` exists for
  that, and its sabotage reads `1 passed; 1 failed`, the concrete test passing under the bug.

- **⚠⚠ `clippy --all-targets` CAUGHT FOUR BREAKS THE TESTS COULD NOT, ACROSS FOUR TARGET KINDS** —
  two examples, `gpu-pipeline`'s test module and `app`'s. **`cargo build --workspace` and
  `cargo test -p <crate>` are both insufficient for a signature change**: neither builds examples,
  and `cargo test --workspace` does not build them either. ⚠ And enumerate every call site

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **nothing calls `region_plan`** — plan 2; (2) a photo with a masked NR or
  dehaze gets nothing, since those steps are last and one decline kills the chain — re-scanned
  2026-09-14, **40 sidecars, 1 mask, 0 masked capture corrections**; (3) spots block a Perspective
  drag from scoping above `geometry`; (4) the airlight shifts every dehazed export by up to 5.6
  levels, and the goldens cannot see it; (5) a chain with a local is not bit-identical, by one ulp;
  (6) `apply_region` on a local clones the **margined region** and runs the whole stage over it, so

would have rebuilt the entire prefix at ~2.4 s.

**⚠⚠ M8.6's "ONLY THE LAST STEP CAN EVER BE SCOPED" IS REPLACED, AND ITS ARGUMENT WAS SOUND ABOUT
