prefix is never that. Its gathers (lens correction, perspective, geometry) all precede its locals
(noise reduction, dehaze), so a local needs only a **margin** and the first scoped step is a gather
reading a whole cached buffer, the case that was already sound. ⚠ `region_plan` establishes that
**per chain** rather than by assertion, and one decline anywhere abandons the whole plan — so a
gather in the middle, which `build_prefix_steps` cannot produce today, would simply switch the
feature off rather than render wrongly.

**⚠⚠ THE GATE IS DERIVED, NEVER A DRAG FLAG.** It asks *is a region wanted, and does the chain from
the resume point accept one* — never *is the user dragging*. There is no drag signal to plumb and
therefore nothing that can disagree with anything else, the rule `Session::geometry_mode` was

| region (each axis) | margined share | scoped | whole-buffer | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10% | 2.9% | **8.7 ms** | 200.4 ms | **22.9×** |
| 30% | 13.8% | 34.5 | 204.8 | 5.94× |
| 50% | 32.7% | 78.6 | 222.4 | 2.83× |
| **60%** | **45.1%** | **109.4** | **213.1** | **1.95×** |
| 70% | 59.6% | 146.2 | 218.3 | 1.49× |
| 85% | 85.0% | 203.3 | 226.7 | 1.12× |
| 100% | 100.0% | 236.6 | 229.9 | **0.97×** |

⚠⚠ The scoped output is **never cached**, so a drag of *n* frames costs `n·scoped + whole` against
the whole-buffer path's `n·whole + tail` — and the break-even tightens as the gesture shortens. At
45.1% a **two-frame** gesture already wins (432 ms against 441); at 59.6% it **loses** (511 against
452) and pays off only past about five frames. **50 sits between those two rows**, so the gate
refuses exactly the band where a short gesture would be worse off. ⚠ The placeholder value turned
out to be right; what changed is that it is now defensible, and the table is in its doc comment so
the next reader can check it rather than trust it. ⚠ It is the **margined** share, not the visible
one: a local's reach is in full-resolution pixels, so 50% of each axis margins out to a third of the
frame.

**⚠⚠ WITHOUT THE WARM-BEHIND THE GESTURE INVERTS — fluid while dragging, then a stall the moment you
let go.** A scoped render is deliberately never cached, so no drag frame leaves a checkpoint and the
settled whole-buffer render builds the entire prefix from scratch: **~200 ms** on the sweep's chain.
The worker spends that in the background instead, ~150 ms after the requests stop.
- **⚠⚠ The settle is detected from the CHANNEL, not from a drag signal**, which is what keeps the
  whole mechanism inside the worker. A live gesture produces a request per UI frame, so silence for
  longer than a frame interval **is** the settle. A `dragging` flag threaded down from the canvas
  would be a second fact beside the derived gate, and the two could disagree.
- **⚠ A request arriving during the wait is TAKEN and carried forward**, never discarded — the wait
  has to take one out of the channel to learn the gesture is live, so dropping it is exactly how
  this could lose a frame, and a lost frame during a drag is the canvas silently showing a stale

- **⚠⚠ The warm render's frame is DISCARDED.** Sending it would replace the canvas texture with a

  local to one ulp — so neither acceptance test may be weakened to make this easier.

frame than M8.6 ever had it. ⚠ Sabotaged: reading them off the buffer fails both equivalence tests

**⚠⚠ THE CARRIER IS WHAT STOPS THIS SHIPPING DEAD, AND IT ASSERTS THE STEP COUNT RATHER THAN THE
FLAG.** A scoped render and a whole-buffer one produce the same picture **by design**, so every
correctness test in the workspace — all 63 goldens included — passes with the gate deleted. That is
precisely how creative LUTs (W5) shipped fully tested and 100% non-functional. ⚠ And a test asking

the reporter's chain; `a_chain_of_prefix_steps_renders_only_the_region` asserts `prefix_stages == 2`.
Sabotage: restoring `start + 1 == steps.len()` fails exactly the three new tests and **nothing
else** — 821 others green — so they are specific to what M8.7 adds rather than to scoping in general.

**⚠⚠ THE CHAINED FIXTURE CARRIES A VIGNETTE, AND TWO OF ITS PARAMETERS ARE LOAD-BEARING.** The
vignette is the only tail stage whose result depends on **where** a pixel sits in the frame, so it is
the only thing that can see wrong frame dimensions — M8.6 caught its version of that hazard with
exactly this stage and with nothing else. And `smoothness: 0.0`, not the default 50: the chroma
radius runs 8–32 full-resolution pixels and its reach is **two passes** of it, so a defaulted
smoothness margins a 24×18 region out to roughly the whole 128×96 fixture — **past
`SCOPE_MAX_AREA_PCT`, where the gate correctly refuses and the test goes green and blind**.

**⚠ Five sabotages beyond the gate deletion, every one caught by exactly the test named for it:**
frame dims off the buffer (135 levels); NR's chroma margin halved to one pass (**2 levels** — the
band at the region's edge, which is why a 1-level tolerance is tight enough to see it and a looser
one would not be); no warm-behind at all; warm behind *every* render; and the carried-forward request
dropped ("no frame produced").

**⚠ What the gesture test deliberately does NOT assert is that no warm render fires mid-gesture.**
That is held structurally by `recv_timeout`, because asserting it means asserting that six renders
finish inside 150 ms of wall clock — an assertion about **OS scheduling**, and this project has three
recorded CI flakes from exactly that.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **a COLD entry into 1:1 gets nothing** — lens correction is step 0 and

### The prefix cache evicted the checkpoint a drag resumes from (2026-09-14)

**The prefix cache evicted the checkpoint a drag resumes from (2026-09-14).** A root-caused bug fix, so no spec and no plan. Reported as *"it's even slower now"* against M8.6, and then — after this fix — as *"still on the same level as before, maybe slightly faster but still not acceptable"*. 2437 → **2439 tests** (exactly the two added); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, which is the proof this changed eviction order and no pixel; 0 GPU skips.

**⚠⚠ PLAIN LRU IS EXACTLY BACKWARDS FOR A DRAG, AND THE OLD COMMENT DEFENDED IT IN WRITING.** `PrefixCache`'s doc read: *"Retention is effectively deepest-first, and falls out of plain LRU rather than needing its own rule: within one render checkpoints are inserted shallow to deep, so the deepest is the most recently used and the shallowest is evicted first. That is the right order — the deeper checkpoint saves more upstream work."* **True of a cold render, false of the interaction the cache is paid for.** Dragging prefix step `g` invalidates every checkpoint *below* `g`, so the render resumes at `g` and then inserts `g+1 .. n` — every one of which its own next frame will miss. LRU reads checkpoint `g` (promoting it to the front), then pushes it to the back behind those doomed inserts and evicts it. **The one entry that was still usable is the one it throws away.**

### ⚠⚠ AND IT BIT ONLY AT FULL RESOLUTION, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED SINCE THE CHECKPOINTS LANDED (2026-08-12)

**⚠⚠ AND IT BIT ONLY AT FULL RESOLUTION, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED SINCE THE CHECKPOINTS LANDED (2026-08-12).** A checkpoint is ~74 MiB at rung 3123, so the 512 MB budget holds six and `MIDS_CAP` bound the tier before the byte budget ever chose. At rung 6246 one checkpoint is **298 MiB** and the budget holds **exactly one** — so a five-step prefix evicted its own upstream checkpoints *within a single render*, and every drag frame restarted from zero. Measured in the running app at **1730–2223 ms a frame with `prefix_ran 5`**, re-running lens correction each time.

**⚠⚠ EVICTION IS DEEPEST-FIRST NOW, AND IT IS A RULE OF ITS OWN RATHER THAN A CONSEQUENCE OF INSERTION ORDER.** `PrefixCache::evictable` takes the largest `PrefixKey::depth()`, ties broken toward least-recently-used — which is the behaviour the preview rungs already had and keep. ⚠ `max_by_key` returns the **last** maximum, so the key is the tuple `(depth, index)`: equal depths resolve to the larger index, i.e. further back, i.e. least recently used. Written as a tuple rather than left to that subtlety.

- **⚠ `PrefixKey::depth()` is DERIVED from the key, never carried beside it.** A cache storing a depth alongside a key is two facts that can disagree — the shape `render_max_dim` and `Session::geometry_mode` were each deleted for. It is `self.steps.len()`, three lines, and it is why this fix touched `pipeline` at all.

- **⚠⚠ THE EXISTING BUDGET TEST COULD NEVER HAVE SEEN THIS, AND ITS COMMENT CLAIMED IT COULD.** `the_mid_tier_is_bounded_by_bytes` was documented as *"insertion order within one render is shallow → deep, so the most recent insert is the deepest checkpoint; evicting the LRU is therefore evicting the shallowest."* But its `fake_key` varies only the `max_dim` tag, so **all three keys have the same depth** — the fixture could not exercise the story the comment told. The comment is rewritten to say what the test actually pins: the **tie-break**, at equal depth, which is still least-recently-used.

- **⚠⚠ THE DRAG TEST HAD TO DRAG NOISE REDUCTION, NOT GEOMETRY, AND THE REASON IS THE WHOLE POINT.** Geometry is the *first* prefix step in that fixture, so moving it invalidates everything and there is nothing to resume from whatever the policy — a test written that way passes against the bug. The bug is about a drag that **has** valid upstream work, which is every real one, since lens correction is on by default and runs first. `a_prefix_drag_resumes_when_the_budget_holds_one_checkpoint` asserts `prefix_stages < 3` after a cold render of 3, with a fixture check that the cold render really ran the whole prefix.

- **⚠ The unit test's budget is sized to hold exactly ONE checkpoint**, which is the full-resolution situation in miniature — 192-byte dummies against a 200-byte budget, and 3072-byte buffers against 4000. It asserts the **shallowest** survives. Under the old `pop()` it is the one that goes.

- **⚠⚠ `RUSTROOM_DEBUG_RENDER` NOW PRINTS THE PREFIX PER STEP, AND THAT IS WHAT MADE ANY OF THIS VISIBLE.** A whole-render figure says a drag is slow; only a decomposition says *which stage*. The render line gained `scoped {}` (M8.6's observable in the running app — the two paths produce the same picture by design, so a gate that never fires looks exactly like one that does, and it read `no` on all 22 frames), and `render_cached` now prints `prefix: [...]  resuming at N of M` followed by a timed line per step with its output dimensions. Kept permanently, the `RUSTROOM_DEBUG_MASK` and `RUSTROOM_DEBUG_BRUSH` precedent.

- **⚠ Found by instrumenting rather than by reasoning, for the twenty-somethingth time in this file.** The hypothesis in hand was *"lens correction re-runs every frame"*, which the log confirmed (`resuming at 0`, `prefix_ran 5`) and which reading the eviction code alone had not suggested — the old comment reads as correct, because it *is* correct about the case it describes.

- **⚠⚠ THE GATE FAILED ONCE WITH 17 FAILURES AND NONE OF THEM WERE THIS CHANGE SET — TWO GATE PROCESSES WERE RUNNING AT ONCE, AND THE RECORDED TEMP-DIRECTORY FAMILY BIT ACROSS *PROCESSES* RATHER THAN ACROSS THREADS.** A killed gate was still running when its re-run started, so two `cargo test --workspace` invocations overlapped. ⚠ **The tell was in the log rather than in the failures**: `test.log` held **two interleaved `failures:` blocks** with lines spliced mid-token (`----- batch_export::tests::keep_both_appends_it` and `test thumb_loader::… ok` on one line), which only two writers to one file descriptor can produce. ⚠ Established rather than assumed: the named tests pass **73/0 single-threaded**, five consecutive `-p app --lib` runs pass **824/0**, and running two `app` test binaries concurrently **reproduces it on demand** (one exits 101, the other 0). ⚠⚠ **The cause is that `TempDir::new` does `remove_dir_all` on a name with no `std::process::id()` in it, so one process deletes another's directory mid-test** — hence `os error 2` and a missing `good.jpg`. **11 of the 18 temp-dir sites in the workspace already carry the pid; 7 do not** — `batch_export.rs:657`, `presets.rs:237`, `presets.rs:391` (hardcoded), `sync.rs:83`, `settings.rs:1489`, `export_presets.rs:123` and `edit-model/src/lib.rs:2987` (hardcoded) — and the failures fell entirely in two of them, with the reproduction hitting a third. **Not fixed here**, because it is pre-existing, not blocking (the gate is reliable run alone) and touches seven test files across two crates. ⚠ **Never run two gates concurrently**, and when a gate fails in modules the change set cannot reach, read the log for interleaving before reading the assertions.

- **⚠ AND THE GATE'S OWN `gpu skips` ROW IS MEASURING THE WRONG THING.** It is `grep -ci "skip"` over the whole log, so it counts **test names** containing the word — `masking_zero_skips_the_gate_entirely`, `a_malformed_preset_is_skipped_not_fatal` and ten more, every one `... ok`. It read `12` on a run with **zero** skipped tests. The honest reading is the per-binary `test result:` lines summed: **2439 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored** — those three being the deliberately `#[ignore]`d `gpu-pipeline` probes. **Quote the summed result lines, never that row.**

- **⚠ One defect of my own, caught before the gate: adding `depth()` directly after `upto`'s doc comment ABSORBED it**, leaving `upto` undocumented. That is the recorded M8.6 clippy trap (`empty_line_after_doc_comments`) in a new costume — there an insertion *separated* a doc comment, here it *swallowed* one. **After any scripted insertion near a doc comment, read the surrounding lines back.**

- **⚠⚠ CONFIRMED IN THE RUNNING APP AT RUNG 6246 (2026-09-14), WHICH IS THE ONLY RUNG THAT CAN CONFIRM IT.** 13 consecutive drag frames, every one `resuming at 1 of N`, never `resuming at 0`: a Straighten drag `resuming at 1 of 4` / `prefix_ran 3` at 799.1–1217.6 ms, a Perspective drag `resuming at 1 of 5` / `prefix_ran 4` at 956.2–1111.3 ms — the latter reproducing the recorded post-fix reading (~1030 ms at 1.8 Mpx against ~980 at 2.2). ⚠ **A run at rung 3123 would have proved nothing**, because there a checkpoint is ~74 MiB, the budget holds six and `MIDS_CAP` binds the tier before the byte budget ever chooses — the *old* code reads `resuming at 1` there too. ⚠ The picture half is not confirmed and is a judgement rather than a measurement.

- **⚠⚠ AND THE SAME SESSION SHARPENS THE GENERALISATION'S TARGET FROM 63% TO 76%.** On a Straighten drag at 26 Mpx the per-step decomposition is `geometry` **206.2 ms**, `noise_reduction` **308.4**, `dehaze` **359.8** — so **NR and dehaze are 668.2 of 874.4 ms of prefix work, 76%**, against the 63% the five-step Perspective row gave. The shorter the prefix, the larger the two locals' share: there is no chain on which they are not the answer.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **this does not make the reporter's drag fast** — it takes it from 1730–2223 ms to **1029.9 ms**, which he reported as *"still not acceptable"*, and the remaining 648 ms of NR and dehaze is the region-scoped-prefix generalisation's territory rather than this fix's; (2) **the budget still holds one checkpoint at rung 6246**, so a five-step prefix keeps only its resume point and nothing else — raising `MID_BUDGET_BYTES` would buy more, at 298 MiB an entry, and is deliberately not done here; (3) deepest-first is the right rule for a *drag* and marginally the wrong one for an alternation between two unrelated deep states, which nothing does today; (4) not bit-identical to nothing — this changes no pixel at all, which is what the 63 unmoved goldens say.

### M8.5 — the sequential resamplers, in parallel (2026-09-13)

**M8.5 — the sequential resamplers, in parallel (2026-09-13).** `geometry::rotate` and `PerspectiveStage::apply` were single-threaded gathers on an eight-core machine. **The resampling prefix goes 544.4 → 287.5–296.0 ms, 1.84×, saving ~250 ms — with no GPU involved.** 2428 tests **unchanged**, 63 goldens **byte-identical**, which is the whole acceptance test. Spec `2026-09-13-parallel-resamplers-design.md`, plan `2026-09-13-parallel-resamplers.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE IS THAT ITEM 3 OF THE AGREED ORDER WAS WRONG IN BOTH HALVES, AND ONE PROBE FOUND IT BEFORE A LINE OF GPU CODE WAS WRITTEN.** That item read *"the three resamplers — geometry, perspective, lens correction — as ONE mechanism. Upload the displacement field as a two-channel texture."* Measured (`probe_resamplers`, kept; `DSCF6296.RAF`, native rung 3123×2085, Catmull-Rom, 8 threads, ⚠ load 3.0–4.0):

  | prefix step | before | after | |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `lens_correction` | 224.4 ms | 217.6–227.1 | unchanged — already rayon |
  | `perspective` | 158.3 | **34.3–35.0** | **4.5–4.6×** |
  | `geometry` | 161.8 | **34.5–35.8** | **4.5–4.7×** |
  | **all three** | **544.4** | **287.5–296.0** | **1.84×** |
  | *(a bare clone, in every row above)* | *2.0* | *2.1–2.2* | |

- **⚠⚠ THEY ARE ONE *KIND* OF PROBLEM AND NOT ONE MECHANISM.** Lens correction samples a displacement field lensfun computes, **per channel** — TCA gives R, G and B different source points, which is the entire reason `resample::sample_channel` exists — so its field is **six components per pixel, not two**. Perspective is an analytic **homography** and geometry an analytic **rotation**: a few arithmetic ops per pixel, wanting no texture at all. A design written from the two-channel phrasing would have been wrong about all three.
- **⚠⚠ AND TWO OF THE THREE DID NOT NEED THE GPU AT ALL — THEY NEEDED EIGHT CORES.** `perspective.rs` carried, in writing, *"Sequential, mirroring `geometry::rotate` … If this ever needs to be faster, both should move together."* It needed to, and they did. **After this, lens correction is ~75% of the resampling prefix**, so item 3 is now **"port lens correction"** rather than "port three resamplers".
- **⚠⚠ AND THAT COMMENT DEFENDED ITSELF WITH A NUMBER THAT HAD STOPPED BEING TRUE.** It read *"geometry's whole-buffer rotation measures 203 ms at full resolution and nobody has complained"* — at a native rung it is **158–162 ms**, and nobody had complained because nobody had looked. **A comment justifying a design decision with a stale measurement is how the decision outlives its reason.** Both stages now carry the band and the date.

- **⚠⚠ BIT-IDENTICAL, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE 63 GOLDENS THE ACCEPTANCE TEST RATHER THAN SOMETHING NEW.** Both are **gathers** — an output pixel reads the whole source and writes only itself — so no two threads write the same byte and none reads another's output, and the float operations are the same operations in the same order. `LensCorrectionStage`'s own rayon port records exactly this argument. ⚠ The check is **`git status` over `tests/`**, not a passing suite: a golden is rewritten only under `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`, so *an unmodified tree plus a green run* is what establishes byte-identity. Both stages were checked that way separately.
  - ⚠ It is also the guard on the **speed-up**: a 4.5× that came from doing *less* work would move a golden. None moved.

- **⚠ `rotate` ONLY, not "geometry".** `GeometryStage::apply` is orient → rotate → crop; `orient` is an index permutation and `apply_crop` a sub-rect copy. Neither is where the 161.8 ms was, so parallelising them would be machinery for nothing and would widen the diff the goldens have to cover.

- **⚠ The `stride == 0` guard rides along in both.** `par_chunks_exact_mut(0)` **panics**, and a zero-width image reaches `rotate`. Already recorded twice in this repo — `map_pixels_xy` and `LensCorrectionStage` — so this is a rule applied rather than discovered. ⚠ In `perspective` it is unreachable behind the existing `w < 2` guard and kept anyway, because that guard is about the identity case rather than about this.

- **⚠⚠ PERSPECTIVE'S RATIO WAS MEASURED DIRECTLY RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM GEOMETRY'S, AND THE PLAN MADE THAT ITS FIRST TASK FOR A REASON.** Reasoning by analogy from a sibling is what this crate has been wrong about three times (M8.3g by ~2×, M8.3f by 8× in attribution, M8.3o by ~18%). Measured before the change: geometry **160.5 → 33.1 ms, 4.85×**; perspective **158.8 → 30.2 ms, 5.26×**. They agree, which *confirms* the same-shape argument instead of assuming it.

- **⚠⚠ AND THE PROBE CARRIES ITS OWN CARRIER, WHICH IS WHAT PROVES THE CHANGE REACHED PRODUCTION.** Its `sequential vs rayon` rows compare the **real stage** against the probe's own parallel copy: before the change they read 4.85× and 5.26×, after it **1.04–1.19×**. A row still near 5× would mean the edit landed somewhere the probe does not look — the gap that let creative LUTs ship fully tested and 100% dead — and no pixel test could ever have seen it.

- **⚠ A plan error worth recording, because it anticipated the right hazard in the wrong place.** Its self-review flagged that `pipeline::perspective::Homography` might not be reachable from an example. It **is** public — **`PerspectiveStage` is not re-exported**, which is what actually failed to compile. The fix reaches the stage through `build_prefix_steps`, which is better than the constructor would have been: it measures the stage the prefix really builds.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **nothing for a photo with no straighten and no perspective** — both stages are skipped entirely when inactive, so this is paid only by photographs that use them; (2) **lens correction is untouched** at ~218–227 ms and is now ~75% of the resampling prefix, with the GPU its only remaining lever; (3) the prefix is still **whole-buffer**, so these costs are paid on every rung change and every prefix-slider drag as before; (4) three prefix stages now compete for the same rayon pool the tail uses — they run sequentially within one render, so this is a statement about a busy machine rather than a new race; (5) one machine, one photograph, and the bench machine was **not quiet** (load 3.0–4.0).

### M8.3q — noise reduction on the GPU (2026-09-13). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.3q — noise reduction on the GPU (2026-09-13). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works, confirmed by use"*, with **no defects found by using it**. ⚠ Read it narrowly: what that establishes is that **1:1 with a SECOND full-resolution GPU prefix stage renders rather than killing the worker** — 398 MiB of scratch on an X-T4 — and that an NR drag is visibly quicker with the picture unchanged. ⚠⚠ **The half a still frame cannot catch is the chroma blur's BORDER**, whose failure mode is a plausible photograph rather than a broken-looking one: `box_blur`'s window shrinks at an edge and the sum is divided by the count inside it, where the alternative reading darkens a margin by roughly half. It is M8.3n's hazard in a second stage, guarded by that milestone's `a_constant_plane_stays_uniform`, so treat a later report of *"a band of colour at the edge of the frame with Color up"* as that test's territory rather than as a new bug. The second acceleration outside the tail, and the cheaper case of the guided filter M8.3o shipped. 2417 → **2428 tests** (exactly the eleven added); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, 0 GPU skips. Spec `2026-09-13-noise-reduction-gpu-design.md`, plan `2026-09-13-noise-reduction-gpu.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE IS A DRAG, NOT A STAGE, AND THE NEXT-ACTION BLOCK DID NOT CARRY THE ROW THAT MATTERS.** That block quoted NR at *"~84 ms at a native rung"*, which is its cost **alone**. But noise reduction is the **first** prefix step, so moving its slider re-runs NR *and* dehaze *and* the tail — **205.9–209.3 ms, the most expensive drag anywhere in the prefix**, half again more than a Dehaze drag's ~126. Dehaze got the cheaper half of the seam it built. Measured on `DSCF6296.RAF` at a native rung (3123×2085, 6.5 Mpx), three runs (⚠ load 4.24–5.27, so **not a quiet machine** — that biases the CPU column and so the ratios slightly optimistic):

  | row | CPU | GPU | |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **NR DRAG — prefix steps AND tail** | **205.9–209.3 ms** | **140.9–144.4** | **1.45–1.46×** |
  | `noise_reduction` ALONE (whole buffer) | 81.9–82.8 | **54.8–57.7** | 1.44–1.51× |
  | `dehaze` ALONE, for contrast | 94.4–94.8 | 62.5–66.0 | 1.44–1.51× |

  **An NR drag goes ~207 → ~142 ms, saving ~65 ms a frame — 4.8 → 7.1 fps.** ⚠ It is *still* the most expensive drag in the prefix, because the dehaze step and the tail behind it are unchanged; what moved is the NR step itself.

- **⚠⚠ THE SPEC'S OWN 86.1 ms WAS A POINT READING THE BAND DOES NOT SUPPORT — 81.9–82.8 re-measured, and M8.3h had to retract a headline for exactly this.** That earlier figure was one best-of-5 taken at load **5.43** against this band's 4.24–5.27, and a busier machine biases the CPU column upward. ⚠ **Quote a band, not a figure**; `cpu_cost` therefore ships at **81.0** rather than the planned 86.0 — the band's floor rounded down, which is also the conservative direction, since a lower number makes a step *less* likely to chain and the gate must fail toward the CPU.

- **⚠ No prediction of the post-milestone figure was made, deliberately, and its agreeing with dehaze's is not evidence that one could have been.** Composing dehaze's 1.47× onto NR's cost is the error this crate has made three times — M8.3g over-predicted a whole frame by ~2×, M8.3f was right in magnitude and wrong by 8× in attribution, M8.3o was over-optimistic by ~18%. The bench's own row is the result.

- **⚠⚠ FOUR SCRATCH PLANES AGAINST DEHAZE'S SEVEN, AND THAT IS THE MILESTONE'S ONE REAL DESIGN CHOICE.** The prefix always runs whole-buffer, so this is the **second stage ever** to allocate at full resolution — 99.4 MiB a plane on an X-T4 — and the first one killed the render worker. Three layouts were priced at 26 Mpx: storing all six planes **795 MiB**, one seed pass **596**, and the shipped two-phase sequencing **398**. The luminance half finishes into `p1` *before* the chroma half starts, so the chroma channels take `p0` and `p2` back; `apply_nr` then **recomputes** `prophoto_to_oklab` from `img` rather than keeping three original planes. ⚠ That recompute is three `cbrt` and two matrices against 398 MiB, and it is **bit-identical by construction** — same bytes, same function, and `img` is not written until `apply_nr` itself.

- **⚠ `eps` is a UNIFORM where the box blur's radius is a LITERAL, and the asymmetry is deliberate.** The shader text is the program cache's key: `eps` moves with every step of the Detail slider, so a literal would compile a fresh program on every frame of a drag. The radii move only with Smoothness and the render scale — a handful of values — and `box_wgsl`'s own doc says a literal radius is what lets the compiler see a constant trip count.

- **⚠ Both radii sit far from M8.3n's crossover, in opposite directions.** `LUM_RADIUS_FULL = 6` is below `RUNNING_SUM_MIN_RADIUS = 7` at **every rung the app can reach**, so the guided filter always takes the **naive** body — its cheap case; the chroma radius is 8–32 and takes the **running** one. So the exact value of that constant is not load-bearing here either, only the side each lands on, which `each_radius_takes_the_body_the_sweep_chose` pins.

- **⚠⚠ THE FIXTURE WAS WRONG FIRST, AND ITS OWN CHECK IS WHAT SAID SO.** `no_sample_comes_back_negative` failed on its **fixture check**, not its assertion: two mid-tone colours drove the CPU stage to the zero clamp **zero times**, so the test would have passed against a shader with no clamp in it. The clamp needs **high chroma at low lightness**, which two mid-tones cannot produce. Swept four candidates: two mid-tone bands **0** clamped samples, red/near-black 785, green/near-black 3239, and **red / near-black / blue 5000** — which ships. The chroma blur carries the neighbours' large `a`/`b` into a region whose `L` is tiny, and that is outside ProPhoto's gamut. ⚠ **A fixture for a clamp must contain what reaches the clamp**, and the fourth property is now written into the fixture's doc with the measurement beside it.

- **⚠⚠ SEVEN OF EIGHT SABOTAGES CAUGHT; THE EIGHTH IS RECORDED AS NEAR-INERT RATHER THAN COUNTED, AND IT IS M8.3n's FINDING IN A SECOND STAGE.** Caught: `eps` interpolated arithmetically, both chroma passes collapsed to one, the lerp inverted, the radius scaling dropped, `eps` never written to the uniform, the seam arm removed, and the zero clamp removed. ⚠ **Not caught: dropping the variance clamp in `slope_offset`** — in the self-guided case `cov` and `var` are the **same expression in exact arithmetic**, so the only way `cov` goes negative is float cancellation on nearly-flat areas; M8.3n measured that at **4.7e-6, below the GPU/CPU baseline divergence of 1.05e-5** in the same regime. No test here can separate the two and one that appeared to would be measuring the baseline. Kept, and the shader says why.
  - **⚠⚠ THE RADIUS SABOTAGE WAS CAUGHT BY EXACTLY ONE TEST, AND THAT TEST EXISTS ONLY BECAUSE THE PLAN PREDICTED THE BLIND SPOT.** At `RenderScale::new(1.0)` the scaling is the **identity**, so every equivalence test is structurally blind to it being dropped — the two paths would agree perfectly while both used full-resolution radii at a fit rung, which is the rung the app spends most of its time at. `the_radii_follow_the_render_scale` is the only thing that fails.
  - ⚠ The zero-clamp sabotage fired on `no_sample_comes_back_negative` **alone**, exactly as designed: `compare` quantizes to 8-bit levels, where a negative sample and 0 are the same value, so the other nine stay green. The **seventh** recorded instance of that trap.

- **⚠⚠ THE FORCING FUNCTION M8.3o LEFT BEHIND FIRED EXACTLY AS WRITTEN.** `every_other_prefix_stage_is_left_alone` listed `"noise_reduction"` among the stages with no GPU twin and its doc said *"noise reduction is the one that will not, and naming it here is what makes adding it a deliberate act rather than a silent one."* Adding the arm broke it. It now names the **three resamplers**, and records that they are **one mechanism rather than three** — which is what the agreed order says and what a naive reading gets wrong.

- **⚠ `GpuNoiseReductionStage::new` takes NO image, where `GpuDehazeStage::new` must.** Noise reduction estimates nothing from the photograph, so every parameter comes from the `Edits` and the render scale; dehaze's airlight is a property of *this* frame. The seam hands the buffer over regardless, because one signature serves both.

- **⚠ TWO PROCESS FAILURES IN THE SABOTAGE STEP, BOTH MINE, AND THE SECOND DESTROYED A FILE.** (1) A sabotage editing `pipeline` was run **concurrently** with sabotages on `gpu-pipeline`, which builds against it — so one came back `DID NOT COMPILE` with errors naming a *different crate*, a reading that would have been recorded as a caught sabotage had the errors not been read. **A sabotage touching a crate others depend on must run serially.** (2) All the sabotages shared **one** `/tmp/sab.bak`, and a stale background job's restore fired long after I thought it had — copying the GPU shader over `crates/pipeline/src/stages/noise_reduction.rs`, 514 lines replacing 331. ⚠⚠ **The symptom was silence**: the benchmark's runs 2 and 3 simply printed nothing, and quoting run 1 as a band of three was one careless glance away. **Name the backup per file**, and `git checkout` was the right recovery here *only because that file was already committed*.
  - ⚠ **Clippy caught what three benchmark runs and a green suite did not, for at least the twenty-second time**: an unused binding in the new `NR DRAG` row. `cargo test --workspace` **does not build examples** and `cargo run --example` does not deny warnings, so only `clippy --all-targets` could see it. The commit was amended rather than followed by a fixup, so every commit on this branch is green.

- **⚠ `bench_preview` needed no edit to price the stage** — its loop already offers the seam to every prefix step and only special-cases the *absence* of a twin, so the `— \`noise_reduction\` has no GPU twin` line filled itself in. What was added is the **NR DRAG** row, which runs every prefix step from noise reduction onward through the seam (a step with no twin falls to the CPU exactly as it would in the app). ⚠ No existing row can see this milestone — the asymmetry M8.3j recorded when its bench could only see fixtures.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **only when you drag Luminance or Color** — the prefix is per-stage cached, so unlike a tail stage it costs nothing on any other slider, which is also why the ceiling is low; (2) **masked NR is untouched**, as masked dehaze still is — it runs through `capture_projection` in the same prefix and is item 4's territory; (3) **four scratch planes**, 104 MB at 6.5 Mpx and **398 MiB at full resolution**; (4) **not bit-identical** — NR inherits all three recorded divergence classes: subnormal flush-to-zero (M8.3a), FMA contraction in the lerp and in `combine_lum` (M8.3m), and the box blur's division (M8.3n); (5) **the prefix is still 4 of 6 stages on the CPU**, and the three resamplers are the largest number left anywhere — lens correction alone is ~210 ms and is on by default for every RAW; (6) **chaining NR with dehaze is still refused**, so a drag pays two round trips — M8.3o priced that and chose per-step to keep the post-NR checkpoint, and re-measuring the checkpoint's value is the condition it named; (7) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), and the bench machine was **not quiet** (load 4.24–5.27); (8) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.
