**⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE, AND FOR ONCE IT IS BIGGER THAN THE SPEC EXPECTED: THE CREATIVE LOOK IS THE LARGEST SINGLE-STAGE WIN THIS BENCH HAS EVER MEASURED.** Real engine, DSCF6291.RAF, rung 3200, three runs:

  | row | CPU | GPU | |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **creative look (sRGB display)** | 136.95–138.36 ms | **27.08–27.09** | **5.06–5.11×** |
  | **the WHOLE tail** | 183.06–185.72 | **43.20–43.46** | **4.24–4.28×** |
  | `vignette −60`, roundness −60 | 68.15–68.34 | **24.63–24.66** | **2.77×** |
  | `vignette −60`, elliptical | 41.04–41.73 | **24.35–24.66** | **1.66–1.71×** |

  ⚠ The existing rows are unchanged within noise — TYPICAL 2.37–2.54× against a recorded 2.47, `hsl only` 4.29–4.33 against 4.32 — which is what says nothing regressed. ⚠ Load 4.17–5.19, so **not a quiet machine**: that biases the CPU column and so the ratios slightly optimistic, the same caveat every bench in this section carries.

- **⚠⚠ THE SHAPER DOMINATES THE LOOK, NOT THE LOOKUP — and nobody expected that.** `probe_look` (kept, `#[ignore]`d) at 3200×2136: display-referred **96.48–99.96 ms**, `Linear` — which takes **no shaper at all** — **20.72–22.15**. Six `powf` per pixel against a trilinear sample of a table that fits in cache. ⚠⚠ **And the cube's SIZE is not the cost: 33³ and 65³ measure the same to within noise**, 0.43 MB of table against 3.30. Anyone reaching for a smaller LUT to make this cheaper would be optimising the wrong thing. ⚠ It is also why the GPU wins so hard here: a GPU has *hardware* special-function units where a CPU has polynomials — the argument M7.2's note made about a future port, arriving as a measurement.
- **⚠⚠ THE VIGNETTE'S TWO SHAPES ARE 5× APART ON THE CPU AND IDENTICAL ON THE GPU.** `probe_stages`, three runs: elliptical **8.57–9.05 ms**, superellipse **40.44–45.51** — a `sqrt` fast path against two `powf` and a reciprocal exponent. On the GPU both read **24.35–24.66 ms**, the same number. So the branch that dominates one column vanishes in the other.
  - ⚠ `cpu_cost` ships the **bottom of the elliptical band (8.5)**, under-reporting a negative-roundness vignette by ~4.7×. The conservative direction and the gate's own rule — a lower number makes a run less likely to chain, and the gate must fail toward the CPU. Branching would put the `roundness < 0.0` rule in a second place, and `Shape::new` is where it belongs. ⚠ **The creative look DOES branch**, on `LutSpace::is_the_rendering()` — which that type's own doc calls *"the one place this rule is written down"*, so the branch **reads** the rule rather than copying one. The asymmetry between the two is the difference between a published rule and a private one.
- **⚠⚠ `vignette_params` WAS EXTRACTED FIRST, SO THE CPU PATH *IS* THE REFERENCE RATHER THAN MERELY AGREEING WITH IT.** `R_MID`, `FEATHER`, the superellipse and the amount curve are derived in one function both paths read. Two derivations would disagree **invisibly** the first time any of them moved, because both answers are plausible photographs — the rule `white_balance_gains` already follows. ⚠ Its acceptance was that **regenerating all 63 goldens with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` produced byte-identical files**, which is stronger than "still green".
- **⚠⚠ THE VIGNETTE IS THE FIRST GPU STAGE WHOSE RESULT DEPENDS ON *WHERE* A PIXEL IS, so `Builder` had to learn the `Region`.** Its falloff is measured against the whole frame; a region rendered without the origin re-centres on whatever slice is on screen and **slides across the picture as you pan** — a plausible photograph, not an error. ⚠ The region is a parameter of its own rather than a field of `RenderSpec`, because `build_pipeline_split_in_region` takes it *beside* the spec and giving it two homes in one call is the two-facts-that-can-disagree shape this project has paid for three times.
  - ⚠⚠ **And the stage's own region test cannot see the row.** `a_region_is_shaded_as_that_part_of_the_whole` proves the **stage** honours a region; it says nothing about whether the table's row **passes** one. `the_vignette_row_carries_the_region` is the carrier, and sabotaging the row to `None` fails it **alone**.
- **⚠ `Builder` returns `Option`, so a builder may DECLINE.** `creative_look` is built from the profile's parsed `.cube`, and *"the tail and this call were handed the same profile"* is an invariant across two calls rather than something the types say. Declining leaves the CPU stage — the gate's own rule, fail toward the CPU — where an `expect` would panic on a render worker.
- **⚠⚠ TWO SHIPPED TESTS LOST THEIR WEDGE, AND IT IS THE FOURTH TIME A PROPERTY HERE HAS BECOME UNCONSTRUCTIBLE BY BEING FIXED.** `a_cpu_stage_between_two_gpu_stages_produces_two_chains` and `merging_preserves_order` need an unreplaceable stage between two replaceable ones. They used the **colour grade** until M8.3d and the **vignette** until today, and each stopped being a CPU stage the moment it was ported. The wedge is a **mask** now — the last thing the outer tail holds that `REPLACEABLE` cannot reach, since `accelerate` recurses *into* it and it keeps its name and position by design. Nothing else can play that part any more. (After M8.3e's *"a tail with nothing replaceable"*, M8.3h's *"a trailing run refused"* and M8.3n's *"a chain behind a CPU stage"*.)
- **⚠ `every_tail_stage_is_replaceable_or_a_mask` is the milestone's headline as a test**, over a tail carrying every stage the table can reach — and it asserts the **fixture** carries every `REPLACEABLE` name first, so a row added without a field here fails loudly rather than leaving the property asserted over a tail that never contained the new stage.
- **⚠⚠ A TEST THAT ASSERTED SOMETHING FALSE ABOUT CORRECT CODE, AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING.** `an_identity_cube_returns_the_input_in_every_space` failed at **31.3 levels** — because its fixture was hand-written *ProPhoto* triples, and ProPhoto's gamut is far wider than sRGB's: a plausible-looking `[0.1, 0.3, 0.5]` converts to a **negative** sRGB red, which the shaper legitimately clamps. Only a colour genuinely inside sRGB's gamut can round-trip, and the only honest way to get one is to **start there** — the fixture is derived through `srgb_to_prophoto` now.
- **⚠⚠ AND A SABOTAGE THAT PASSED BECAUSE THE *FIXTURE'S DOMAIN* WAS TOO EASY.** Clamping **before** the domain remap — `Cube::lookup`'s own recorded trap — left every test green against a declared range inside `[0, 1]`, where the two orders agree on every sample. It discriminates only when the domain's top is **above 1.0**, so the fixture now declares a real ACES LMT's `LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE 0.0927061729 1.0196260353`. **A guard against a mis-ordered clamp needs a fixture that can reach past the clamp.**
- **⚠ One sabotage recorded INERT rather than counted**: removing the blend-zero short-circuit fails nothing, and provably cannot. `a + (b − a) · t` is bit-exactly `a` at `t = 0` for any **finite** `b`; the residue the CPU stage's comment warns about belongs to the other spelling, `a(1−t) + bt`. The shaper's `pow` takes a clamped non-negative base, so a non-finite `b` is unreachable. Kept as defence in depth, with the reason written at the line.
- **⚠ Ten further sabotages, all caught**, each by the test named for it: the region origin, the lift's `max(1 − c, 0)` (**by the raw-float test alone** — `compare` quantises to 8-bit levels, where everything above 1.0 is 255 and the bug is invisible, M8.3e's clamp lesson in mirror form), the superellipse forced onto the `sqrt` path, x/y taken from the dispatch grid rather than the linear index, `Linear` taking a shaper, the domain remap dropped, Rec.709's transfer aliased to sRGB's, the matrix transpose dropped, and each of the two new table rows removed.
- **⚠ The bench's engine finally gets a real `looks_dir`** — without one the look row would render with **no look at all** and report a speed-up for a stage that never ran, which is the W5 failure mode as a benchmark. With no `.cube` installed the row is **skipped with a printed note** rather than silently reading zero.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **nothing for this catalogue's own sidecars** — 0 of 40 use the vignette and 0 use a creative look — though ⚠ the user has said plainly he **has not been using Rustroom yet**, so that scan describes the folders rather than what a photographer does, and this milestone was chosen structurally rather than from it; (2) `cpu_cost` under-reports a negative-roundness vignette by ~4.7×, deliberately and in the safe direction; (3) **a mask still splits the tail**, and is now the only thing that can — `LocalAdjustments` carries neither a vignette nor a look, so neither stage can appear inside one; (4) not bit-identical — the smoothstep and the lerp are multiply-adds the GPU fuses, and the shaper is six `pow` calls; (5) **the whole PREFIX is still 5/6 on the CPU**, which is where the remaining time is: measured at a native rung it is 238.6 ms against a 32.5 ms tail; (6) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), and the bench machine was **not quiet** (load 4.17–5.19); (7) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.

### M8.3o — dehaze on the GPU, and a seam for the prefix (2026-09-13). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.3o — dehaze on the GPU, and a seam for the prefix (2026-09-13). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works"*. ⚠⚠ **It shipped a live crash, fixed the same day**: it is the first GPU-accelerated *prefix* stage, and the prefix always runs whole-buffer, so at 1:1 it was the first thing ever to ask for a full-resolution GPU image — 298.1 MiB, past a ceiling nobody had noticed. Its section is **"The device-limit crash, and the vignette measured"** above. The first acceleration **outside the tail**. 2387 → **2401 tests** (exactly the fourteen added); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, 0 GPU skips. Spec `2026-09-13-dehaze-gpu-design.md`, plan `2026-09-13-dehaze-gpu.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE HONEST HEADLINE: 1.47×, WHERE THE SPEC PREDICTED 1.8× FROM COMPONENT MEASUREMENTS.** Measured whole-buffer at 3123×2085 (6.5 Mpx): **dehaze alone 96.8 ms on the CPU against 66.0 on the GPU**, so a Dehaze drag goes **129.8 → ~99 ms**, 7.7 → 10.1 fps. ⚠ Roughly **26 of those 66 ms is transfer**, so the arithmetic is ~2.4× and the round trip eats a third of the win. ⚠⚠ **That is the third time in this crate that composing component measurements has missed** — M8.3g over-predicted a whole frame by ~2×, M8.3f was right in magnitude and wrong by 8× in attribution, and this was over-optimistic by ~18%. **The plan's last task re-measures the real thing for exactly that reason, and it earned its place.**

- **⚠⚠ IT WAS CHOSEN BY RE-SCANNING THE CATALOGUE, AND THAT CORRECTED SOMETHING SAID OUT LOUD ONE MESSAGE EARLIER.** Across 40 sidecars / 40 copies: **dehaze 2** (at 70 and 100), noise reduction 1, local contrast 1, **vignette 0**, **creative look 0** — `null` in every sidecar. So dehaze is the most-used unported stage by a clear margin, and the claim that *"what is left that can still split the tail is the vignette and the creative look"* is structurally true and **worth nothing here**. ⚠ A first pass of that scan reported the creative look at **40 of 40** and was a detector bug; it was checked before being believed, which is the only reason it did not become a milestone.

- **⚠ And the user's own settings are what make it bite:** `drag_quality: Full` with `gpu_tail: true`, so a fitted photo on a large window renders at a **native rung** while dragging. The prefix also runs **whole-buffer whatever the zoom**, so there is no region to shrink it.

- **⚠⚠ THE PREFIX HAD NO SEAM, AND THE ONE BUILT HERE IS PER STEP AND AT APPLY TIME — a correction the plan did not anticipate.** The plan said *"substitute a step's stage by name"* over the whole list up front. **That is wrong**, because `dehaze::airlight` is estimated from the image the stage is **handed** — in the prefix that is the checkpoint *after* geometry and noise reduction, and geometry **crops**. An estimate taken from the raw buffer would key on pixels the crop has removed: a slightly different airlight, which is **a different photograph rather than an error**.

- **⚠⚠ IT RETURNS A STAGE, NEVER A STEP, WHICH MAKES A MUTATED KEY UNREPRESENTABLE RATHER THAN MERELY TESTED.** `PrefixStepKey` is derived from the **edits**, never from the stage, so a checkpoint written by the CPU path is a legitimate hit for the GPU path and the reverse — and `PrefixCache` needed **no change at all**. ⚠ `a_checkpoint_written_by_either_path_is_a_hit_for_the_other` renders once on the GPU and once on the CPU **through one cache** and asserts the second runs no prefix step; without it that is a claim.

- **⚠⚠ PER STEP, NEVER CHAINED, AND THE MEASUREMENT DECIDES IT.** Chaining the two prefix stages pays the transfer once — and destroys the **post-NR checkpoint**, which exists precisely so a Dehaze drag resumes after noise reduction. Priced at 6.5 Mpx: per-step gives a Dehaze drag ~99 ms against chaining's ~113, and a Dehaze drag is the case that matters (dehaze 2 of 40, NR 1). ⚠ **Chaining wins an NR drag** (~113 against ~139), recorded rather than hidden: it becomes right if NR is ported *and* the checkpoint's value is re-measured. ⚠ Worth knowing before anyone reopens it: even with the checkpoint lost, a chained GPU prefix still beats today's CPU — the question is *how much* to win, not whether.

- **⚠⚠ THE ONE NEW PRIMITIVE IS A MINIMUM, AND IT IS THE PLACE M8.3n's TRICK PROVABLY FAILS.** A sliding-window **minimum is not invertible**: `box_blur` slides by adding the entering sample and subtracting the leaving one, and a minimum cannot subtract — once the running minimum leaves the window there is nothing to recover it from. So there is only the naive O(r) gather, and it is affordable **purely because the radius is small**: `PATCH_RADIUS_FULL = 20` scales to **r=10**, measured at **4.49 ms**, where Clarity's r=40 cost 46.9 and lost to the CPU outright. ⚠ The CPU keeps an advantage the GPU cannot take here — `min_1d`'s monotonic deque *is* O(1) amortised — and it simply does not matter at this radius.
  - ⚠⚠ **It is BIT-IDENTICAL to `spatial::min_filter`, which nothing else ported in this crate can claim.** A minimum **selects an input sample** rather than computing one, so there is no sum to accumulate, no divide, and no multiply-add to fuse — none of the three divergence classes can reach it.

- **⚠ Two of dehaze's three primitives were already built.** The guided refinement is box blurs, which M8.3n shipped — ⚠ but it is **cross**-guided (`p` is the transmission map, `guide` is luma), so M8.3n's self-guided shortcut does **not** apply and all **six** statistic blurs are needed. Sabotage-verified: substituting `mean_guide` for `mean_p` fails the equivalence test. ⚠ `REFINE_RADIUS_FULL = 60` scales to **r=31**, above M8.3n's crossover, so it takes the running body.

- **⚠⚠ THE AIRLIGHT STAYS ON THE CPU AND ARRIVES AS THREE UNIFORMS, AND THAT IS A CORRECTNESS DECISION RATHER THAN AN ECONOMY.** It already runs on a **fixed 256 px downscale** — deliberately, so the estimate cannot vary with the render scale and the image does not shift on zoom — which makes it negligible to compute **and** makes both paths identical **by construction** rather than by comparison. `the_airlight_is_the_cpus_own` is the only test that can see a second estimate.

- **⚠ Seven scratch planes, the most any stage in this crate asks for** — the cross-guided filter needs four statistics where the self-guided form needs two. 190 MB at 6.5 Mpx, allocated per chain.

- **⚠⚠ SIX SABOTAGES: FIVE CAUGHT, ONE RECORDED AS NEAR-INERT FOR A REASON THAT IS A FEATURE.** Caught: the zero clamp (**only** the raw-float test, exactly as designed), `mean_p := mean_guide`, `OMEGA` transcribed as 1.0, the airlight replaced by a constant, the minimum's window unclamped, and the seam never firing. ⚠ **Not caught: lowering `T_MIN` from 0.1 to 0.0001.** The floor bites only where the refined transmission falls below 0.1 — and **M7.6's airlight tolerance RAISES `t` toward 1 for exactly those pixels**, because a transmission that low means the pixel is nearly the airlight's own colour, which is what the tolerance is for. The two guards overlap by construction and no photographic fixture reaches the floor. Kept, and the shader says why.
  - ⚠ Two sabotages first came back **DID NOT COMPILE** — removing a `{placeholder}` leaves the `format!` argument unused — which reads exactly like a pass. M8.3m records that trap; redone by changing the *value* rather than the placeholder.

- **⚠⚠ AND THE TEST COUNT CAUGHT A FACTUAL ERROR IN M8.3n's OWN RECORD.** 2386 + 14 should be 2400, and the gate reported 2401. Decomposed per crate, gpu-pipeline read 135 in that gate and 136 at the merged tip: **M8.3n's quoted gate was run one commit early**, before the accidentally-deleted `a_second_render_does_not_take_the_first_renders_plane` was restored. Corrected in place above. ⚠ **The lesson is not the arithmetic — a gate run before the last fix describes a tree nobody shipped, and only "the count moved by exactly N" catches it.**

- **⚠ `bench_preview`'s prefix labels were hardcoded and WRONG, in a kept instrument.** It printed three names — `geometry` / `NR` / `dehaze` — against a list whose length and order depend on the edits, so at a native rung it labelled a two-step list with three names and reported "geometry change" for a list containing no geometry. Derived from `step.stage.name()` now, the rule `EDIT_GROUP_NAMES` and the GPU hint string already follow.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **modest, and roughly a third of the win is eaten by the transfer** — 1.47×, a Dehaze drag 129.8 → ~99 ms; (2) **only when you drag Dehaze** — the prefix is per-stage cached, so unlike a tail stage it costs nothing on any other slider, which is also why the ceiling is low; (3) **noise reduction is not ported**, though the seam now serves it and it is the obvious follow-up (1 of 40 here against dehaze's 2); (4) **the masked dehaze is untouched** — it runs through `capture_projection` in the same prefix and would come along only once this is proven; (5) seven scratch planes, 190 MB at 6.5 Mpx; (6) not bit-identical — dehaze inherits both FMA contraction and the division class; (7) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), and the bench machine was **not quiet** (load 2.76); (8) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.

### M8.3n — local contrast on the GPU (2026-09-13). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.3n — local contrast on the GPU (2026-09-13). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works"*, with **no defects found by using it**. ⚠ Read that narrowly: what was exercised is Texture and Clarity as global sliders with the toggle on. ⚠⚠ **The half a still frame is least likely to catch is the BORDER, and it is the only thing here whose failure mode is a plausible picture rather than a wrong-looking one** — the box blur's window shrinks at an edge and the sum is divided by the count actually inside it, where the alternative reading darkens a margin by roughly half. It is guarded by `a_constant_plane_stays_uniform`, the only test in the workspace that can see it; treat a later report of "a band at the edge of the frame with Clarity up" as that test's territory rather than as a new bug. ⚠ The same hazard sits one level down at **1:1 while panning**, where local contrast runs on the cropped region and `tail_kernel_radius` is what keeps margin for its reach. ⚠⚠ And **the M8.3m mask fix below was NOT part of what was confirmed** — the check for it is a mask carrying white balance, contrast, a tone curve or saturation, and it is still owed. Texture and Clarity as compute shaders — the last unported mask sub-stage, so **a mask now carries 10 of 10** and nothing left in the tail can split a mask's chain. 2374 → **2387 tests**; 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, 0 GPU skips. ⚠ **Recorded as 2386 at first, and corrected at M8.3o by decomposing the count per crate.** The gate quoted here was run **one commit early** — before the accidentally-deleted `a_second_render_does_not_take_the_first_renders_plane` was restored — so it counted 135 gpu-pipeline tests where the merged tip has 136. ⚠ The lesson is not the arithmetic: **a gate run before the last fix is a gate that describes a tree nobody shipped**, and only "the count moved by exactly N" catches it. Spec `2026-09-13-local-contrast-gpu-design.md`, plan `2026-09-13-local-contrast-gpu.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE HONEST HEADLINE FIRST, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS M8.3m's: THIS DOES NOT MOVE THIS CATALOGUE.** Re-scanned at the end of the milestone rather than quoted from memory (M8.3j's lesson): of 40 sidecars and 40 copies, **0 use Texture, 1 uses Clarity (`DSCF6546.RAF.json`, `clarity: -5.0`), 0 use either in a mask.** What it buys is structural, and all three items were named in the milestone block before a line was written: it is the last stage that can **split a mask's sub-stage chain**, the last that can take the **leading position** and deny a mask M8.3l's shared upload, and the largest unported stage in the tail.

- **MEASURED, real engine, `bench_gpu_tail`'s three new rows at rung 3200** (⚠ load average 3.31, so not a quiet machine — the same caveat M8.3f and M8.3g carry, and it biases the CPU column and so the ratios slightly optimistic):

  | row | CPU | GPU | |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `texture -60` (the guided path) | 76.84 ms | **39.47** | **1.95×** |
  | `texture +60 + clarity 50` | 69.19 | **46.66** | **1.48×** |
  | **the head THROUGH local contrast** | 126.90 | **66.20** | **1.92×** |

  ⚠ The existing rows are unchanged (TYPICAL 2.47×, `hsl only` 4.32×), which is what says nothing regressed. ⚠ The three rows are **deliberately not catalogue rows** — no existing row can see this milestone, which is the asymmetry M8.3j recorded as the whole mechanism of its own wrong caveat.

- **⚠⚠ THE LOAD-BEARING RISK WAS PROBED BEFORE THE SPEC, AND THE OBVIOUS SHADER IS A REGRESSION.** `spatial::box_blur` keeps a running sum, so it is **O(1) in the radius** — 4.68 ms at r=40 against 4.63 at r=2, flat. A GPU thread has no running sum to keep, so the naive gather is **O(r)**: Clarity's 81-tap window × 2 passes × 3 iterations is **486 taps per pixel** against the CPU's five. Measured at 3200×2136 on an M2:

  | | naive O(r) | running sum O(1) | CPU | |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Clarity `wide_blur` r=40 ×3 | **46.9 ms** | **10.5** | 13.5 | naive **0.29× — a 3.4× REGRESSION** |
  | Texture guided r=2 ×4 | **5.6** | 13.7 | 18.5 | naive **3.29×** |

  **So there are two shader bodies chosen by radius**, and the crossover is **swept, not guessed** — two constants in this crate were reasoned about instead (`MIN_GPU_BOX_PX` low by ~8×, `MAX_TILE_DABS` sized by a *limit* and 5× slower than the CPU it replaced). The sweep crosses at **r=8**; `RUNNING_SUM_MIN_RADIUS` ships at **7**. ⚠ The four radii that occur — Texture 1 (fit) / 2 (native), Clarity 10 (fit) / 40 (native) — are far from it in both directions, so its exact value is not load-bearing; only the side each lands on is, and `each_band_gets_the_shader_the_sweep_chose` pins that.

- **⚠⚠ THE "THREE BLUR KINDS" FRAMING THAT SCOPED THIS OUT AT M8.3c OVERSTATED IT BY 3×.** This file has said since then that the stage *"needs three blur kinds (`box_blur`, `wide_blur`, the guided filter) where sharpening needed one"*. Not as a statement about **primitives**: `wide_blur` **is** three iterated `box_blur` passes, `guided_filter` **is** four-to-six of them, and `gaussian_blur` has been on the GPU since M8.3c. **`box_blur` was the only genuinely new primitive** — it needs its own shader only because its border rule differs (the **window shrinks** and the sum is divided by the count inside it, where `gaussian_blur` **replicates** the edge sample).

- **⚠⚠ A THIRD CPU/GPU DIVERGENCE CLASS: THE DIVISION.** The running body transliterates `blur_rows`/`blur_cols` exactly — same priming, same slide, same divisor — and **the spec predicted it would therefore be bit-identical**, since a running sum is adds and subtracts with no multiply-add to fuse. **It is not.** On a 20×12 structured plane at r=8, **36 of 240 samples differ, every one by exactly ONE ULP** (`0.41` against `0.41000003`). One rounding everywhere rather than error compounding along the row is what identifies it: consistent with Metal implementing `x / n` as `x * (1/n)`. ⚠ Stated as consistent-with rather than proven — WGSL exposes no division-mode control, so there is nothing to toggle and confirm against. After subnormal flush-to-zero (M8.3a) and FMA contraction (M8.3m), this is the third.

- **⚠⚠ AND IT FIXES A LIVE BUG M8.3m SHIPPED, FOUND BY WALKING INTO IT.** That milestone added `white_balance`, `contrast`, `tone_curve` and `saturation` to `REPLACEABLE` and left all four under *"deliberately not carried"* in `sub_edits`. The consequence inside a mask was silent and total: the builder read `Edits::default()`, so a masked white balance solved gains of `[1,1,1]`, a masked contrast a slope of 1, a masked tone curve an empty point list — **every one an identity**, while the CPU stage they replaced did the work. A slider that does nothing, with `gpu_tail` on, and no error anywhere.
  - ⚠⚠ **THE EXHAUSTIVE DESTRUCTURE CANNOT CATCH THIS, AND THAT IS THE GENERAL LESSON.** It catches a **new field**, because a new field has no arm. It cannot catch a field whose **status changed** — `_` stays a valid arm forever. **Anything added to `REPLACEABLE` must be carried by `sub_edits`**, and nothing in the build says so.
  - ⚠⚠ **AND THE TEST NAMED FOR THE PROPERTY ASSERTED THE BUG WAS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR.** `the_projection_carries_nothing_a_gpu_builder_does_not_read` used `contrast`, `saturation` and `vibrance` as its fixture — **the exact fields whose builders M8.3m had just added** — so it demanded that a projection *drop* three values a GPU builder now reads. It passed, loudly and wrongly. Rebuilt against the property that is actually stable: the only things a projection must never carry are the two stages that **cannot reach a mask's tail at all** (noise reduction and dehaze run in the prefix) and `masks`.
  - ⚠ **Its sibling guard had gone stale the same way.** `a_mask_carrying_every_ported_stage_renders_the_same_picture`'s doc read *"every one of the eight projected fields is non-default here"* — true when written, and the projected set grew to twelve without the fixture following. **A guard that enumerates a list stops guarding the moment the list grows**, for the second time in this file. It now asserts, field by field, that nothing reached the projection at its default.
  - ⚠ Nobody hit it: `gpu_tail` is off by default and 0 of 40 sidecars use those four. **That is luck, not a guard.**

- **⚠⚠ TEN OF TEN MASK SUB-STAGES, AND THE RESULT IS THAT A PROPERTY BECAME UNCONSTRUCTIBLE.** With `local_contrast` ported, a mask's sub-stages are contiguous and its chain **always lands at index 0** — so *"a chain behind a CPU stage"* can no longer be built from any `Edits`, and **M8.3l's shared upload reaches every mask shape rather than merely more of them.** That is the third time this crate has watched a property become unreachable by being fixed (M8.3e's *"a tail with nothing replaceable"*, M8.3h's *"a trailing run refused"*). ⚠ Three tests used `local_contrast` as their CPU wedge and were rebuilt rather than deleted: one drives `mark_shared`'s **whole truth table** directly (weaker in one way — it does not prove `walk` passes the right `is_first` — and stronger in another: it cannot go vacuous as a fixture drifts, which is exactly what happened to the test it replaces), and two swap the wedge for *a mask too cheap to chain*, which leaves a deposit unclaimed for a different reason.
  - ⚠ A fourth was **vacuous already**: `a_mask_carrying_the_whole_per_pixel_set_keeps_only_local_contrast_on_the_cpu` had **no `local_contrast` in its fixture**, so it asserted "with no local_contrast the whole set becomes one chain" over a fixture that had none by construction. Its `subs.len() > 1` check is far too weak — it holds for any two, so the one stage it was named for could go missing with nothing failing. It now names all ten.

- **⚠ A CPU WIN RIDES ALONG, AND IT IS A PREREQUISITE RATHER THAN A BONUS.** In the self-guided case (`p == guide`) `mean_p` **is** `mean_guide` and `cross` **is** `guide_sq`, so `guided_filter` computed **four** statistic box blurs where two suffice and built two whole-image temporaries it did not need. Removing them is **bit-identical** and **~30% faster** — 40.6 → 28.3 ms — which is visible in the stage's own cost: `texture_minus` read **50.4–66.8 ms** before and **38.8–39.2** after. It rode along because setting a `cpu_cost` against code with a known 30% of fat is **exactly the M8.3h staleness failure**. ⚠ Detected by **pointer identity**, which fails toward doing more work rather than toward doing the wrong work; noise reduction is self-guided and gains the same 30%, and **dehaze uses the general form and is untouched** — confirmed by a sabotage that took four dehaze tests and three goldens down with it.

- **⚠ Costs measured by `probe_stages` at 3200×2136, three runs, AFTER the slimming:** `texture_plus` **17.93–18.55** → ships 17.9; `texture_minus` **38.78–39.19** → 38.7; `clarity` **21.93–22.33** → 21.9. Each at the **bottom** of its band, the conservative direction. ⚠⚠ `cpu_cost` is the **max** of the two bands, never their sum: both together measured 32.77–33.66, which is *more* than either alone but *less* than both added (the luma extraction and the gain pass are shared), so a max is always an underestimate — the safe side.

- **⚠ Five scratch planes, and the sequence is what keeps it at five rather than seven.** A box blur is **in place at the plane level** (`box_h` writes `p2 → p4`, `box_v` writes `p4 → p2`), so a statistic never needs a destination of its own; and the guided base is **never materialised** — one kernel reads `p2`, `p3` and `l` and writes `delta += k_t · (l − (p2·l + p3))`. Texture finishes into `delta` before Clarity starts, so the two bands share `p2`–`p4`. **136 MB at 6.8 Mpx** against sharpening's 109, allocated per **chain** rather than per stage.

- **⚠⚠ FIVE SABOTAGES, FOUR CAUGHT, AND THE FIFTH IS RECORDED AS NEAR-INERT RATHER THAN COUNTED.** Caught: the border rule → `2r+1` (3 tests), the gain's zero floor (4), the halo suppressor (3), the threshold forced all-naive (4). ⚠ **Not caught: collapsing `cov` to `var` in `slope_offset`** — and the reason is structural. In the **self-guided** case the two are equal in exact arithmetic, so the only way `cov` goes negative is float cancellation on nearly-flat areas: measured at **4.7e-6**, which is **below the GPU/CPU baseline divergence of 1.05e-5** in the same regime. No test in this crate can separate them, and one that appeared to would be measuring the baseline. Kept anyway — it costs nothing, it mirrors the CPU line for line, and it becomes load-bearing the moment anything drives that shader cross-guided, which dehaze already does on the CPU side.

- **⚠⚠ THREE ASSERTIONS IN THIS MILESTONE WERE WRONG ABOUT CORRECT CODE, ALL CAUGHT BY RUNNING THEM.** (1) *"No sample comes back negative"* — false: the gain is a **scalar multiply**, so a scene-referred **negative input** stays negative however the gain is clamped (−0.05 comes back −0.2 under a gain of 4, on both paths). What the clamp prevents is a **negative gain**, whose signature is a sample whose **sign flips**. (2) *"The two bands are exactly additive"* — true only while the gain is unclamped, and the fixture deliberately drives it past `GAIN_MAX`; the test compares the GPU's residual against the **CPU's own**, which tests the shader rather than the model. (3) *"A constant plane stays exactly constant"* — `box_blur`'s own doc says that and it is true in **real** arithmetic, not f32: a running sum reaches each position by a different history of adds and subtracts, so the last bits wobble (0.36999995 against 0.36999992) **on the CPU too**. "Constant" means **uniform**, and the bound has to be `(w + h)` roundings because a separable blur drifts in both axes.

- **⚠ The kept instrument: `box_probe`'s `#[ignore]`d `probe_box`**, which drives `BoxProbe::forcing` so it times **both** bodies at one radius — the sweep in `box_wgsl`'s header is made of it, and a threshold nobody can re-measure is a threshold nobody can defend. ⚠ It was **deleted by accident** during a scripted rewrite of the test module and restored; the same rewrite silently removed `a_second_render_does_not_take_the_first_renders_plane`, an M8.3l guard, which **only a `git diff main` of the test-function names caught**. ⚠⚠ **Diff the test names and the `⚠` comments before committing a large test-module edit** — W0's rule, and it earned its place twice here.

- **⚠ Clippy caught what a green suite did not, again — `CLIPPY=101` against `TEST=0`.** An unused `Instant` import, which is what revealed the probe had been deleted. At least the twentieth recorded instance.

- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **nothing for this catalogue** — 0 of 40 sidecars use Texture and 1 uses Clarity at −5.0, so this is coverage plus an unlock rather than a speed-up anyone here will feel today; (2) **Clarity's blur is only ~1.3× the CPU's**, so `texture + clarity` is the weakest row at 1.48× — the running sum's cost is **coalescing** (on the horizontal pass adjacent threads walk adjacent *rows*, reading `w` floats apart), which is the ~10 ms floor visible at every radius in the sweep and the obvious next lever if it ever matters (a transpose, or a shared-memory tile); (3) **136 MB of scratch**, paid by every chain containing this stage; (4) bit-identity is off the table for this stage and now for the box blur too; (5) **the vignette and the creative look still split the tail** — after this they are the only two; (6) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), and the bench machine was **not quiet** (load 3.31); (7) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.

### M8.3m — the rest of the per-pixel tail (2026-09-13), i.e. M8.3e's plan 2 at last. ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.3m — the rest of the per-pixel tail (2026-09-13), i.e. M8.3e's plan 2 at last. ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works"*, with **no defects found by using it**. ⚠ Read that narrowly: what was exercised is the four sliders this milestone ports, with the toggle on. ⚠⚠ **The half a still frame is least likely to catch is the tone curve's clamp BELOW black** — it behaves differently there from every other table in this crate, deliberately, and its failure mode is a plausible shadow rather than a wrong-looking one. It is guarded by `a_negative_sample_takes_the_curves_bottom_entry`, the only test in the workspace that can see it; treat a later report of "the deep shadows look wrong with the GPU on" as that test's territory rather than as a new bug. White balance, contrast, the tone curve and saturation as compute shaders. **The per-pixel head is now contiguous**, and a mask carries **9 of 10** sub-stages on the GPU. 2358 → **2374 tests** (16 added: 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 across the four stages, plus 2 decision tests); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, 0 GPU skips. Spec `2026-09-13-per-pixel-tail-plan-2-design.md`, plan `2026-09-13-per-pixel-tail-plan-2.md`, `2026-09-13-tail-completion-gpu.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE HONEST HEADLINE FIRST: THIS DOES NOT MOVE THIS CATALOGUE, AND THE SPEC SAID SO BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN.** **0 of 40 sidecars use any of these four globally** — measured before M8.3k, and the reason plan 2 was deferred three times. No existing bench row moves. What it buys is three things, and only the third is why it was done *now*:

- **⚠⚠ TWO RUNS THAT WERE REFUSED BECOME ONE THAT PAYS, AND THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FOUR STAGES' OWN COST.** `contrast` and `tone_curve` sit **between** ported stages, so a photo using them split the per-pixel head into `[exposure]` at 1.3 ms and `[tone_regions]` at 18.0 — **each refused by the gate**. So **19.3 ms of already-ported work was stranded on the CPU by a 1 ms neighbour standing between it and the rest.** ⚠ That is why `contrast` is worth porting at a `cpu_cost` of 1.2, far under the transfer: **what a stage buys is not always its own cost.**
- **9 of 10 mask sub-stages**, leaving **`local_contrast` alone** — which turns "port the rest of a mask" from a list into one named item.
- **⚠⚠ AND IT IS WHAT MAKES M8.3l's SHARED UPLOAD REACHABLE FOR MORE THAN ONE MASK SHAPE.** That milestone shares the base plane **only with a mask whose sub-stages begin with a GPU-able stage**, because `MaskStage::apply` pipes the clone through them in order. A mask starting with white balance, contrast or the tone curve paid **both** uploads; three of these four are exactly those leading positions. **A caveat of one milestone became the case for the next.**

- **MEASURED, same machine, one session, `bench_gpu_tail`'s new `the whole per-pixel head` row at rung 3200:**

  | | CPU | GPU | |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **before** (7 `REPLACEABLE` rows) | 103.6–106.2 ms | 74.1–76.5 | 1.36–1.43× |
  | **after** (11 rows) | 104.5–106.3 | **41.0–42.5** | **2.46–2.55×** |

  A further **~33 ms**, which is the four stages' own **20.4 ms** plus the **19.3 ms** that was stranded. ⚠ The row is **deliberately not a catalogue row** — it prices the *shape*, and the existing rows cannot see this milestone at all.
- **⚠ Costs measured by `probe_stages` at 3200×2136, three runs:** wb **3.77–4.33** → ships 4.0; contrast **0.97–1.97** → 1.2; tone_curve **8.07–9.27** → 8.0; saturation **7.19–9.39** → 7.2. ⚠⚠ Each sits at the **bottom** of its band, which is the conservative direction for a `cpu_cost`: a lower number makes a run *less* likely to chain, and the gate must fail toward the CPU. `TRANSFER_COST` is rounded up from the top of its band for the mirror reason. ⚠ The same run re-measured the three existing constants — exposure 1.07–1.50 against a recorded 1.3 ✓, tone_regions 15.9–17.0 against **18.0**, display_rendering 23.3–24.9 against **25.7** — so the two older ones read slightly *less* conservative than they claim. **Recorded, not changed**; re-tuning a shipped constant is its own milestone and M8.3h is the precedent for how much care that takes.
- **⚠⚠ THE SECOND CPU/GPU DIVERGENCE CLASS THIS CRATE HAS FOUND: THE GPU FUSES THE MULTIPLY-ADD.** `PIVOT + (x − PIVOT) * slope` contracts to one `fma`, which rounds **once** where the CPU rounds twice — **so the GPU is the *more* accurate of the two.** Measured on contrast: 3 of 18 samples differ, every one by exactly **1 ulp**, worst **0.0** of an 8-bit level. Confirmed rather than assumed — every differing sample equals the CPU's own `mul_add` form **exactly**.
  - ⚠ It is why `white_balance` and `exposure` can claim **bit-identity** and the other three cannot: those are a pure multiply with **no add to fuse**. **Any future stage containing a multiply-add inherits this.**
  - ⚠ WGSL exposes no contraction control, and every algebraic form of the expression still contains a multiply-add — so it cannot be turned off or restructured away.
  - ⚠⚠ **The guard is therefore not a tolerance alone.** A tolerance passes against a genuinely wrong shader whose error happens to be small. `the_only_divergence_is_fused_multiply_add` asserts every sample equals the separate-rounding form **or** the fused one, with nothing in between — and accepts both, because contraction is the backend's choice.
- **⚠⚠ A CLAMP AT ZERO NEEDS A RAW-FLOAT ASSERTION, AND THIS MILESTONE HIT THAT FOUR TIMES IN ONE DAY.** `compare` quantizes to 8-bit levels, where **a negative sample and 0 are the same value** — so dropping a `max(.., 0.0)` floor is invisible to it. That is M8.3e's finding about the output transform's clamp, met again in `contrast`, in `tone_curve` and in `saturation`. **Every clamp-at-zero here now has a test that reads raw floats.**
- **⚠⚠ AND THE TONE CURVE'S CLAMP NEEDED TWO TESTS, BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS ONE IS INERT.** `sample` clamps its input to `[0,1]` *before* indexing — the **opposite** of the rule `ProfileHueSatMap`'s `v`, `ColorGradingStage`'s index and `tone_regions`' `l` each follow, where the *index* clamps and the *value* keeps its headroom. Above 1.0 the clamp is **redundant**, since `lo >= last` catches it anyway, so sabotaging it left `a_sample_above_one_takes_the_curves_top_entry` green. It is load-bearing only **below 0**, where `u32(floor(-511.5))` saturates to 0 on Metal and the interpolation then runs with `frac = -511.5`, extrapolating far off the bottom: measured **−0.93** where the curve's bottom is 0.
- **⚠⚠ EVERY CONSTANT IS SUBSTITUTED FROM THE CPU'S OWN DEFINITION, NEVER TRANSCRIBED.** `PIVOT` and `EPS` became `pub` for it, and saturation takes its luminance from `luma_wgsl`. A substituted constant **cannot disagree**; a transcribed one is merely checked for agreeing — the distinction `luma_wgsl`'s doc records as making it stronger than `oklab_wgsl`, and `color`'s doc records six copies of a Rec.709 triple that all went wrong on one day. Sabotage-verified: a transcribed Rec.709 luma in saturation fails at **43.7 levels**.
- **⚠ The tone curve uploads the CPU stage's own LUT** (`ToneCurveStage::lut()`), the rule `ColorGradingStage::lut` and `HueTable::entries` already follow. ⚠ And **`white_balance_gains` was extracted** from inside `adjustment_stages` *before* a GPU builder could recompute it — two derivations of "what as shot means" would disagree as a **wrong picture rather than an error**, and invisibly on any neutral fixture, since both land near `[1,1,1]`.
- **⚠⚠ SATURATION'S FIXTURE MUST BE COLOURED, AND THAT IS NOT A DETAIL.** A neutral pixel has chroma 0 and is untouched at **any** setting, so a grey fixture would pass against a shader that did nothing at all. A separate test asserts the CPU stage really moves the fixture before anything is compared against it.
- **⚠ Three process traps fired, all already in this file.** A commit went in with **`CLIPPY=101`** because the gate was sequenced with `;` — amended. A sabotage **did not compile** (removing `{eps}` leaves the named argument unused) and read exactly like a pass through a grep for `test result`; only the full output showed it. And `cargo test "a\|b"` matched **nothing** and printed `0 passed`, which reads as green — cargo takes a substring, not a regex.
- **⚠ A sabotage of my own that proved nothing until corrected:** the first floor sabotage hit saturation's **R** channel, which goes *positive* at high saturation. The negative one is **B**.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **nothing for this catalogue's globals** — 0 of 40 sidecars use these four, so no existing bench row moves and this is coverage plus an unlock rather than a speed-up anyone here will feel today; (2) **`local_contrast` still splits a mask**, and is now the only sub-stage that can — it needs three blur kinds, which is a different mechanism; (3) **the vignette and the creative look still split the tail**, for the same reason; (4) the GPU is bit-identical only for `white_balance` and `exposure`, the two with no multiply-add; (5) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal); (6) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.

### M8.3l — the mask's shared upload (2026-09-12). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.3l — the mask's shared upload (2026-09-12). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works"*, with **no defects found by using it**. ⚠ Read that narrowly: what it establishes is that a global slider drag on the masked photograph renders the same mask and is visibly quicker. ⚠⚠ **The failure this milestone could have had is a MASK LAGGING ONE FRAME BEHIND THE SLIDER, not a wrong-looking picture** — a plane taken wrongly renders the *previous* frame's pixels, which is a plausible photograph. That is what was watched for and it did not happen; treat a later report of "the mask trails the slider by a frame" as this milestone's territory rather than as a new bug, and the two guards it belongs to are `the_outer_tails_own_chain_never_takes_a_masks_leftover_plane` and `a_mask_that_deposits_nothing_never_takes_another_masks_plane`. A masked frame uploaded the same plane to the GPU **twice** — once as the auto-mask gate's base, once as the sub-stage chain's input. Now once. **The mask's `sub=` phase goes 23.6–29.8 → 16.0–22.0 ms, and a global drag over the catalogue's masked photograph 126.4–131.5 → 107.7–119.3 ms, 1.78–1.98× → 1.94–2.15×.** 2346 → **2358 tests** (12 added: 1 in `pipeline`, 6 `SharedPlane` unit tests, 5 end-to-end); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, 0 GPU skips. Spec `2026-09-12-mask-shared-upload-design.md`, plan `2026-09-12-mask-shared-upload.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE TWO SABOTAGES I PREDICTED WOULD BE INERT WERE THE INSTRUCTIVE ONES, AND BOTH NAMED A REAL HOLE.** This is the sabotage step earning its place more clearly than at any point in Phase 8 — neither gap was visible to review, and both would have shipped as a plausible photograph of the *wrong* photograph.

- **⚠⚠ Restricting the offer to a mask's sub-stages is NOT belt and braces.** `mark_shared` ignoring `share_input` looked harmless — the outer tail has no coverage rasteriser, so what deposit could its chain take? **The previous frame's.** A mask whose own chain sits behind a CPU stage leaves its deposit unclaimed, and the outer tail's chain runs *before* any mask — so on the next frame it finds that plane at matching dimensions on the same thread and renders it. ⚠ The guard needs **both halves at once** and neither alone can see it: a **global** hsl, which puts a chain at index 0 of the outer walk, and a mask whose chain is behind `local_contrast`, which is what leaves a deposit. It fails at **93.6% of samples differing**.
- **⚠⚠ And deleting `begin_mask`'s body was inert against the obvious test, for a reason worth keeping.** A test that renders one pipeline twice cannot see it: its chain **takes** the deposit every time, so the slot is already empty at the next apply and clearing is a no-op. The discriminating case is **two pipelines sharing one context** — one that *leaves* a deposit and one that *deposits nothing at all* (a plain brush needs no base) whose chain is at index 0 and would take whatever it finds. It fails at **worst 255 levels over 88% of samples**. ⚠ **A guard whose failure needs two different pipelines cannot be found by a test of one**, which is the same family as the seventeen "a test can name a bug it cannot detect" entries above, arriving from the composition side rather than the fixture side.
- **⚠⚠ THE PREMISE WAS VERIFIED ON BOTH SIDES BEFORE ANY DESIGN, because "the same bytes" is exactly the kind of claim that is usually almost true.** `MaskStage::apply` hands the gate `image.data()` and then hands `stages[0]` a clone of that same `image`; `GpuImage` is `w*h*3` f32 with `STORAGE | COPY_DST | COPY_SRC` — bit for bit `ImageBuf::data()`'s layout, and a **superset** of the usages the gate's base binding needs. No conversion stands between them, so the gate's own allocation is handed on rather than a second copy made.
- **⚠ Decomposed before designing, and the naive subtraction would have been wrong by ~40%.** The gap between a base and no-base rasterise is ~16 ms, and putting the device copy on its own submit showed the **gate's own per-pixel Oklab work is ~5–7 ms of it**. Only the upload half is recoverable. Measured warm at rung 3200, box 1510×2019, 78.1 MB base: host memcpy into staging **2.06–2.53 ms**, device `copy_buffer_to_buffer` **6.19–13.93**, compute+readback+poll 21.5–27.1, readback 1.36–1.61. ⚠ Round 0's staging take is **18.3–18.7 ms**, not ~2.1 — it allocates the pooled buffer — so every figure here is warm and round 0 is discarded.
- **⚠ The predicted 8–12 ms landed at ~8**, at the bottom of its own band. Said plainly rather than rounded up: the `sub=` phase is the directly instrumented measurement and it moves **~7.6–7.8 ms** consistently; the drag row's larger apparent gain carries the machine's own noise.
- **⚠⚠ THE SLOT LIVES ON `GpuContext` AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT PART OF `GpuCache`.** That cache's rule is *outlive the render*; this one's is the exact opposite — it must not outlive a single `MaskStage::apply`. Folding it in would invite the next reader to treat a stale plane as a cache hit, and a stale plane is the failure both sabotages above produced. It is on the context at all only because the two participants **never meet**: `accelerate` builds the rasteriser and the chain separately, and an `Arc<GpuContext>` is the one thing both hold.
- **⚠ Three guards, each answering a different way it could go wrong.** (1) **The chain must be `stages[0]`** — `MaskStage::apply` clones the image and pipes it through its sub-stages in order, so only the first receives the plane the gate was handed. Marked in `walk` **at the push**, where `out.is_empty()` still says the position: a finished `Vec<Box<dyn PipelineStage>>` cannot be asked which entry is a chain without downcasting. (2) **`begin_mask` clears the slot** at the top of every apply, above every early return. (3) **Dimensions plus a `ThreadId` stamp** — `shared()` is process-wide, so a preview render and an export render on two threads could otherwise trade planes; stamping makes that unrepresentable rather than unlikely.
- **⚠ `SharedPlane<T>` is generic over its payload so its rules are testable with NO GPU at all.** What it enforces is bookkeeping — one use, dimensions, ownership, clearing — and none of that is about wgpu; production instantiates it at `GpuImage`, the six unit tests at `u32`. ⚠ A **refused** deposit is also dropped rather than left for the next asker, which has its own test: it is stale by definition, and leaving it is the staleness the type exists to prevent.
- **⚠ Both `Default` and `Debug` are hand-written, and the derive is actively wrong in both cases** — `#[derive(Default)]` on a generic adds a `T: Default` bound a GPU buffer handle cannot satisfy (an empty slot needs no payload), and `Debug` would demand `T: Debug` of every payload. The first was caught by the compiler on the first build.
- **⚠⚠ THE OBSERVABLE IS A COUNTER ON A *PRIVATELY CONSTRUCTED* CONTEXT, and that second half is the part that matters.** A shared upload changes no pixel any test can read — the same bytes reach the same buffer by a different route — so every equivalence test in the workspace passes with the whole mechanism deleted. But reading the counters off `shared()` would report whatever the rest of the suite happened to be doing, which is **exactly the contamination that made `GpuChain`'s transfer counters per chain**. A second `GpuContext::new()` in a process that already has one is **259 µs** (M8.3a measured it), so a private context costs nothing.
- **⚠ Every end-to-end test asserts `deposits()` BEFORE `takes()`, because the fixture has two ways to be silently vacuous.** The brush must clear `MIN_GPU_BOX_PX` (512 Ki px) or the rasteriser declines and nothing runs on the GPU at all, **and** it must be auto-masked or no base is uploaded to share. A fixture missing either deposits nothing and every assertion below passes for the wrong reason.
- **⚠ Clippy caught `field_reassign_with_default` while the whole suite was green** — at least the nineteenth recorded instance, in a test written by someone who has now read that rule in this file a dozen times.
- **⚠ Found in passing and deliberately not fixed here:** `GpuBrushRaster::capacity`'s doc still reads *"the real brush averages 22 dabs per tile against a capacity of 4095"*. Both numbers are stale — M8.3k measured the busiest tile at **229** and set the capacity to **1024** — and that section already records the estimate as having been wrong by 10×. A comment, not a behaviour.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **only an auto-masked brush benefits** — the base is uploaded only when `plan.gating_rows` is `Some`, so a plain brush deposits nothing and its chain uploads as before; (2) ⚠ **only a mask whose sub-stages START with a replaceable stage** — one beginning with local contrast, saturation, white balance, contrast or the tone curve pays both uploads, which makes **M8.3e plan 2 worth a little more again**; (3) **nothing for the outer tail**, which has no deposit to take and is now guarded against taking one; (4) **the gate's own ~5–7 ms of per-pixel Oklab is untouched** and is real work; (5) **nothing for a mask rendering a region at a different size from its chain** — the dimension check refuses it, correctly, and that case does not arise today; (6) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), one rung, one photographer's single masked brush; (7) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.

The row was pricing the GPU tail *plus a whole rasterization the GPU never paid*.

Two explanations fit a drag frame that costs exactly what a cache-hit frame costs: coverage became free, or **the drag frame was a cache hit too**. The second is the mundane one and it was not checked. ⚠ Rule: **when an optimisation measures as *exactly* free, suspect the harness before believing the code** — free is the signature of work that never ran.

  ⚠ **What the fix is and how it is guarded:** the two configurations now walk **disjoint exposure ladders** (`+0.003` EV on the `on` frame — the same work, a distinct key). Reverting that one line is the sabotage, and it restores `cov=0.00` on every GPU render, so the row cannot silently regress to lying. Honest split on the drag frame: GPU coverage **31.8–43.5 ms** against the CPU's **61.4–66.2** — a real gain, about **1.8× on coverage itself**, not a disappearance.

What changed is its size: coverage went from ~64 ms to ~36 ms, not to zero. ⚠ The plain `REAL SIDECAR` row remains a genuine cache hit by design and still cannot show coverage on either side; the gap between it and the drag row (**91.2 → 126.4 ms on the GPU**) is now what the GPU rasteriser costs.

Swept:

  | capacity | GPU | vs CPU |
  |---|---|---|
  | 512 | 37.73 ms | 1.62× |
  | **1024** | **36.54** | **1.69×** |
  | 2048 | 36.66 | 1.68× |
  | 3584 | **320.20** | **0.20×** |

  **An 8.7× cliff between 2048 and 3584, not a gradient**, with correctness identical at every capacity — so it is purely occupancy. ⚠ And the headroom argument was an estimate wrong by **10×**: the comment claimed "22 dabs per tile" from average dab area, so an unconditional per-**workgroup** `atomicMax` now reports the truth — **the busiest tile holds 229**. 256 would have been under-provisioned on the very photograph this exists for. **An average is not a capacity.**
- **⚠⚠ AN `atomicAdd` COUNTER CANNOT PRODUCE AN ORDERED LIST, AND ASCENDING DAB INDEX *IS* STROKE ORDER.** The first shader appended through one atomic, so slots landed in whatever order 256 threads raced to claim them and the per-pixel walk composited strokes interleaved. **Invisible on one stroke and on any two that only paint; visible the moment one erases** — caught by three tests at once, worst 145 levels over 3,120 of 12,593 samples. The fix is a **two-pass scan over a CONTIGUOUS per-thread range with a prefix sum between them**: contiguous is what makes it sound, because each thread's range is ascending and disjoint, so concatenating blocks in thread order is globally ascending. ⚠ A **strided** assignment keeps each thread's own finds ascending and still interleaves them globally — the trap this replaced. Cost: 86.8 M bounding-box tests rather than 43.4 M, still three orders of magnitude below the 11.1 billion a per-pixel gather would need.
- **⚠⚠ PLAN 1 SHIPPED A REAL BUG THAT ITS ENTIRE SUITE WAS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO: the base plane was indexed without the region's origin.** `BaseView::at` takes **frame** coordinates and maps them into a region-local buffer with `saturating_sub` then a clamp; the shader did `base[(fy * img_w + fx) * 3]`. Correct **only** when `x0 == y0 == 0`, which is every fixture plan 1 wrote and the probe too. A region render at 1:1 would gate the auto-mask against pixels from somewhere else — a plausible mask, not an error. ⚠ Found by **reading `BaseView` while planning the wiring**, not by any test. The sabotage is the evidence: dropping the offset leaves **10 tests green and fails only the region one**, at worst 255 levels over 4,463 of 6,370 samples.
- **⚠ `MIN_GPU_BOX_PX` was swept too, and its starting value was low by ~8×.** It began at `SEQUENTIAL_FLOOR_PX`'s 64 Ki because that answers the same question on the CPU side; measured, at 126,504 px the GPU is **2.3× slower**. ⚠⚠ The GPU carries a **~1.6 ms floor whatever the box size** — M8.3g decomposed that as a 1.28 ms fixed download cost no size reduction touches — so below a few hundred thousand pixels the round trip cannot be repaid, and the curve is a floor rather than a slope. **512 Ki**, just above the 440,860 point where two runs straddled parity (0.80× and 1.50×). ⚠ Measured on a **non-gating** brush, the GPU's weakest case, so it is conservative for a gating one; a per-gating floor is a recorded follow-up.
- **⚠⚠ THE SEAM IS A SECOND INJECTED TRAIT, FOR M8.3j's REASON EXACTLY.** `MaskStage` cannot call `gpu-pipeline` — that crate depends on `pipeline` and its header records that nothing may depend on it — so `CoverageRasterizer` lives in `pipeline` and is handed over through a defaulted `PipelineStage::set_coverage_rasterizer`. ⚠ A second hook rather than a parameter on `accelerate_inner`: that one transforms a **stage list** and this hands over a **collaborator**. ⚠ Both are guarded by the same `inner.is_some()`, so the recursive call offers neither — sound for the same reason the depth bound is.
- **⚠ `plan_dabs` is called once and offered to both rasterisers**, so the GPU and the CPU cannot disagree about which dabs exist. ⚠ **Declining is always safe and every path fails toward the CPU**: no rasteriser offered, a plan that yields nothing, no adapter, a box below the floor — all fall through to `rasterize_in`, costing only the attempt. `a_rasterizer_that_declines_falls_back_to_the_cpu` asserts that is **byte-identical** to offering nothing, which is the guarantee the CLI, every export and all 63 goldens rely on by never offering one.
- **⚠⚠ NEITHER THE WIRING NOR THE OFFER CHANGES A PIXEL A TEST CAN READ, so both needed an observable.** The two rasterisers agree to within one level *by design*, so a `MaskStage` using the GPU renders the same picture and `sub_stage_names_of` cannot see a rasteriser because it is not a stage. **That is the W5 failure mode** — creative LUTs shipped fully tested and 100% dead. The guards are a **stub rasteriser that counts calls** (which also lets the wiring be tested in `pipeline`, with no GPU at all) and `Pipeline::mask_has_coverage_rasterizer`. Sabotage-verified: deleting the offer fails **only** the carrier, 96 passed 1 failed.
- **⚠ Equivalence is in 8-bit LEVELS, not bit-identity, and that is a deliberate change of standard from M8.3i.** Its guard is a frozen verbatim copy compared bit for bit; that cannot hold here because the gate needs `cbrt` and a matrix on the GPU and M8.3a established GPU/CPU float differs in the last bits. Coverage **is** a `u8`, so "within 1 level" is a statement about the stored value rather than a rendering of it. On the real brush: **worst 1 level, 10 of 3,048,690 samples (0.0003%)**.
- **⚠⚠ TWO SABOTAGES ARE RECORDED INERT RATHER THAN COUNTED, and one of them is inert BY CONSTRUCTION.** (1) Moving the gate above the short-circuit leaves every equivalence test green — it is *correct* and merely slower — which is why the dab-test counter exists and is the only thing that fails on it. (2) Substituting WGSL's `round` for `floor(x + 0.5)` passes, and provably must: coverage is scaled by **255, an odd number**, so `cover * 255 = k + 0.5` forces `cover = m/2^n` with `2^(n-1)` dividing `255m` — hence `n = 1`, and **`cover = 0.5` is the only constructible tie, where both rules give 128 because 128 is even**. Kept as defence in depth, and the comment says when it becomes live again: a 16-bit coverage map.
- **⚠ The counter's bound was swept, not guessed.** The first attempt asserted gate evaluations below a tenth of dab tests and **failed at 29.6%**. Measured both states — 29.6% with the short-circuit, **100.0% without, by construction** — so any bound in (0.30, 1.00) discriminates and 0.5 sits with ~1.7× margin below and 2× above. ⚠ A tenth was not a safer number, it was a **failing** one, and raising it without measuring the other state would have left a bound nobody could defend.
- **⚠⚠ THE GATE FIXTURE WAS WRONG TWICE, AND BOTH CORRECTIONS OUTLIVE THE TEST.** (1) It used a dark green against a bright magenta — different in both lightness and chroma, which *looked* stronger. The gate's ceiling at tolerance 25 is **0.095**, and those two are so far apart that **chroma alone already exceeds it**, so dropping the lightness term changed nothing and the sabotage passed. The discriminating fixture is the opposite of extreme: **two near-neutral greys**, chroma distance below the gate's `lo` of 0.0475, lightness far above the ceiling. *"Most different" is not "the content under test"* — the dehaze probe's lesson in a new place. (2) Even then the gate cut **nothing**, because the stroke ran *across* the boundary: each dab references the pixel under **its own centre**, dabs sit a quarter-radius apart, and the within-stroke combine is a `max`, so on the far side there is always a nearby dab whose reference matches. **The gate only bites where a stroke runs ALONG an edge**, which is what the feature is for. ⚠ The fixture check was rewritten too — counting samples `< 20` over the whole box is nearly vacuous, so it now rasterises the same brush with `auto_mask` off and asserts the gate **cuts coverage the positional raster lays down**.
- **⚠ An assert stopped a scripted edit from modifying the FROZEN REFERENCE copy of the old rasteriser.** The Task 1 split's patch matched `for stroke in &strokes` **twice** — once in production, once in the frozen copy the bit-identity test compares against. Editing that copy would have made it agree with the code under test forever, including against every future sabotage. `assert count == 1` failed and nothing was written.
- **⚠ `rasterize_in` is now `plan_dabs` + `rasterize_planned`, and the acceptance was "unchanged at 520", not "still green".** 63 goldens byte-identical and `the_rasterizer_is_bit_identical_to_its_reference` passing are what establish the extraction reordered no float operation. ⚠ One deliberate change, in a readout only: `t_lab` now brackets the Oklab conversion alone, where it used to include the `gating_rows` scan that moved into `plan_dabs`.
- **⚠ Clippy caught what a green suite did not, four more times** — the lib-crate dead-code trap twice (`sub_edits` in M8.3j, then `rasterize_counting`/`with_capacity` here, both `#[cfg(test)]` items with no test yet calling them, which is the bin-crate rule applying to a library), `field_reassign_with_default` on my own fixture against 6 passing tests, and a clamp-like pattern. ⚠ The rule those confirm: **a `#[cfg(test)]` item lands with its first test**, exactly as a `pub` item in a bin crate lands with its first caller.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **the shared upload is NOT taken**, and it is the largest lever left — plan 1 measured the rasteriser at **15.4 ms with no base against ~27 with one**, so ~12 ms is re-uploading a plane M8.3j already has resident; it needs `GpuChain` to accept a pre-resident buffer and is a recorded follow-up **with its number**; (2) **a CPU fallback plans the dabs twice**, since `rasterize_in` plans again internally — `rasterize_planned` is extracted and the fallback can call it directly if it ever matters; (3) **not bit-identical to the CPU rasteriser**, argued above; (4) the floor is measured on a non-gating brush and so refuses some gating brushes the GPU would win; (5) **nothing for a plain brush `BrushCache` already serves**, which pays nothing today; (6) nothing for the analytic masks, whose coverage is 0.00 ms; (7) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**; (8) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), one rung, one photographer's single masked brush.

### M8.3j — a mask's sub-stages on the GPU (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.3j — a mask's sub-stages on the GPU (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"it's smoother now"*, with **one defect found by using it, and it was a stale STRING rather than a wrong pixel** (below). ⚠ Read the confirmation narrowly: what was exercised is a mask carrying HSL with the toggle on, which is exactly what the milestone targets. `accelerate` recurses **one level** into `MaskStage`, so a mask carrying HSL runs its sub-stage chain on the GPU. **1 masked HSL at rung 3200: 116.3–121.5 → 57.4–59.8 ms, 1.99–2.03×** — against M8.3h's recorded **1.10×** for the same row. 2322 → **2331 tests** (nine added, which is exactly what this milestone adds rather than "still green"); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, 0 GPU skips. Spec `2026-09-11-mask-substages-gpu-design.md`, plan `2026-09-11-mask-substages-gpu.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE 63 GOLDENS ARE BLIND TO EVERY LINE THIS MILESTONE ADDS, AND THAT IS STATED UP FRONT RATHER THAN LEFT TO READ AS COVERAGE.** `grep -rln gpu tests` returns **nothing** — the goldens test the CPU pipeline only. What they prove here is the *other* half: that the defaulted no-op trait methods and the two re-added `MaskStage` fields changed no pixel. The new path is covered by the five guards below and by nothing else.

- **⚠⚠ THE ONE DEFECT FOUND BY USE WAS A SENTENCE, AND IT WAS REPORTED AS THE SETTING NOT EXISTING.** Asked to turn the toggle on, the user replied *"I dont see the option gpu tail on"* — **because there is no control called `gpu_tail`.** That is the `settings.json` key; the checkbox is **Settings → Rendering → "Use the GPU"**. ⚠ The handoff block named the key rather than the label, which is this file's own rule broken by the person who wrote it down: ***never describe a control without reading the dialog that would draw it***, recorded after `default_rendering` and `auto_lens_correction` shipped with no control at all. Here the control existed and the *description* was wrong, which reads identically from the user's side.
  - **⚠⚠ And looking for it exposed a genuinely false hint: it read *"Does not apply inside a mask"* — the exact thing this milestone made untrue.** It also enumerated *"the HSL, colour grading and sharpening stages"*, which stopped being true at **M8.3e** when the per-pixel tail took the ported set to seven. **Two stale clauses in one hint, from two different milestones, neither noticed until someone went looking for the checkbox.**
  - **⚠ The fix is to stop enumerating.** It now describes the *rule* — the per-pixel develop stages, inside a mask as well as outside, moved across only when the work saved is worth the transfer — rather than the membership. **A hint that lists a growing set is a hint that goes silently wrong**, which is the "Reset crop" hover text and the "Lens scale" label a third time, and the reason `EDIT_GROUP_NAMES` is derived rather than written out. ⚠ **Anything added to `REPLACEABLE` must not require editing that string**, which is now true by construction.
  - ⚠ **No test covers it and none is proposed.** `modals/settings.rs` needs an `eframe::Frame` to drive, which is not constructible in a test — the tier-2 gap this file already records. The guard is the rule above: a string that names no list cannot go stale as the list grows.

So 2.14× describes this mask's *own* sliders and a still view; a global drag on the same photo gains the same 77 ms on a larger total.

A `Box<Self>` receiver **is** object-safe but **cannot carry a default body**: returning `self` as `Box<dyn PipelineStage>` needs an unsize coercion, hence `Self: Sized`, which is exactly the bound that makes a method undispatchable on `dyn`. With ~30 implementors, a method every one of them had to write was not an option.
- **⚠⚠ `sub_stage_names` IS A SECOND DEFAULTED TRAIT METHOD, AND M8.3g REJECTED EXACTLY THAT SHAPE — so why this one is different is worth writing down.** That rejection was about the byte path: an **output-encoding** concern leaking into a seam deliberately free of them, `None` for every stage but one. This reports **composition**, which the trait already exposes a *mutator* for one method above. ⚠ And without it the milestone is untestable: an accelerated mask and a CPU one render the same picture **by design**, so every equivalence test passes against a hook that never fired — which is precisely how creative LUTs (W5) shipped fully tested and 100% dead. A trait you can change and cannot observe is worse than one carrying two views of one fact.
- **⚠⚠ THE PROJECTION IS AN EXHAUSTIVE DESTRUCTURING, SO A NEW `LocalAdjustments` FIELD IS A COMPILE ERROR.** Every `REPLACEABLE` builder reads the **global** `Edits` (`GpuHslStage::new(&e.hsl, ..)`), which is sound only because the tail's stages were built from those same `Edits`. Pointed at a mask it would apply the global HSL *inside* the mask — a plausible photograph, not an error. `sub_edits` carries the eight fields a GPU builder reads and names the eight it deliberately ignores. ⚠ **Verified by sabotage, not asserted**: adding a `sabotage_field` to `LocalAdjustments` fails `cargo check` with *"pattern does not mention field"*.
- **⚠ RECURSION DEPTH IS ONE, STRUCTURALLY.** The outer walk is handed an accelerator; the walk it starts is handed **`None`**. That is sound because `adjustment_stages` is exhaustive over `LocalAdjustments`, which has **no `masks` field** — a mask's sub-stages can never contain a mask. Pinned by `a_masks_sub_stages_never_contain_a_mask` rather than left as a comment, so a future `LocalAdjustments::masks` is caught by a test instead of by an infinite recursion at render time.
- **⚠ A MASK'S CHAIN IS NEVER TRAILING, so the byte path is unreachable there BY CONSTRUCTION.** `adjustment_stages` never places `output_transform`, so the inner walk's final `flush` can never see it and always returns `(Pipeline, None)`. A mask therefore always pays the **float** round trip, which is the one `TRANSFER_COST = 27.0` describes — no second rule to keep in step.
- **⚠ The hook is offered to EVERY stage the walk sees, before the `REPLACEABLE` lookup.** A replaceable stage has no inner list and inherits the empty default, so one rule covers both arms rather than one arm carrying an exception nobody would think to check.
- **⚠ Both constructors fill the new fields, and the CAPTURE one is not an oversight.** `accelerate` is only ever called on the tail, so the prefix's `MaskStage` never has its hook invoked — and if it ever were, `capture_stages` builds noise reduction and dehaze, neither in `REPLACEABLE`, so the list would come back unchanged. **Safe by construction in both directions**, which beats safe by one caller remembering. `accelerating_the_tail_leaves_the_prefixs_mask_alone` uses a mask carrying **both** halves so one `Edits` exercises both directions of the property.
- **⚠ `MaskStage` re-acquires a field it had deliberately dropped**, and the old comment said so. It was right until a GPU builder needed the *parameters* a CPU stage does not expose: a `Box<dyn PipelineStage>` reports only `name` and `apply`, so the only alternative was downcasting every stage in the workspace. The scale comes with it because `GpuSharpenStage`'s sigma is in **full-resolution** pixels.

- **⚠ A plan error worth recording, because it is a trap this file already names:** the plan's own verification command was `cargo test -p pipeline name_a name_b`, and **cargo takes one TESTNAME, not a list** — it exits with `unexpected argument`. Filters go after `--`. That is the cargo-substring trap in a new costume, caught on the first run.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **five of ten sub-stages ported**, so a mask carrying white balance, contrast, a tone curve, local contrast or saturation keeps those on the CPU and splits its run around them — **M8.3e plan 2 is now worth more than its own row suggests**, since each of those four is also a mask sub-stage; (2) **`image.clone()` (~2 ms) is wasted** when the whole sub-stage run becomes one chain — uploaded and immediately discarded, ~2 ms of ~35, deliberately not reclaimed; (3) **N masks means N round trips**, un-batchable because each mask's sub-stages run on a clone of the *current* image and each blend is CPU and sequential; (4) **nothing for a colour range's 59.9–60.0 ms blend** (re-measured today), nothing for brush coverage, nothing for a gradient's 10.6 ms blend; (5) ~~**no gain on the catalogue's only masked photograph**, by design~~ — **overtaken within the hour: it saves 77 ms a frame there**, see the bullet above, and the retraction is worth more than the caveat was; (6) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), one rung, and the machine was **58–74% idle rather than quiet**, which biases the CPU column and so the ratios slightly optimistic — the same caveat M8.3f and M8.3g carry; (7) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.

### M8.3i — the parallel brush rasterizer (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.3i — the parallel brush rasterizer (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works, confirmed by use"*, with **no defects found by using it**. ⚠ Read that narrowly: what was exercised is a **global slider on the one masked photograph**, which is exactly what the milestone targets and the one case the coverage cache cannot help. The brush coverage rasteriser runs across rows: the Oklab conversion its auto-mask gate needs, and the per-stroke dab splat, which became a **gather**. 2321 → **2322 tests**; 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, which together with a frozen sequential copy is the proof no pixel changed. Spec `2026-09-11-parallel-brush-rasterizer-design.md`, plan `2026-09-11-parallel-brush-rasterizer.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE MILESTONE WAS SCOPED AS "THE MASK LOOP ON THE GPU" AND THE MEASUREMENT MOVED THAT WORK OUT OF IT ENTIRELY.** `CLAUDE.md`'s own rule — measure before theorising — was applied first, by instrumenting `MaskStage::apply` and `rasterize_in`. **Per mask, rung 3200, 3123×2085 (6.5 Mpx), Apple M2, best of 5:**

| mask | coverage | clone | sub-stages | blend | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| exposure, gradient | 0.00 | 2.06 | 3.8 | **11.1** | 17.0 |
| **HSL, gradient** | 0.00 | 2.06 | **68.8** | 11.1 | 82.0 |
| exposure+contrast+HSL, gradient | 0.00 | 2.1 | 67.5 | 11.5 | 81.2 |
| exposure, small radial | 0.00 | 2.2 | 4.0 | 15.3 | 21.5 |
| exposure, colour range | 0.00 | 2.3 | 4.0 | **61–120** | 67–128 |
| exposure, brush (plain, uncached) | 26.6 | 2.3 | 4.0 | 9.3 | 42.4 |
| **the catalogue's one real mask** | **228** | 2.1 | **3.8** | 9.7 | **236** |

⚠⚠ **THERE IS NO DOMINANT PHASE — which one leads depends entirely on the mask kind and what it carries.** HSL → sub-stages (84%); colour range → the blend (91%); auto-masked brush → coverage (97%); exposure under a gradient → the blend (65%). **So "port the mask loop" was never one thing.** ⚠ And on the only masked photo this catalogue has, **the sub-stages — the thing the milestone was scoped to port — are 3.8 ms of a 296.8 ms frame, 1.3%.** ⚠ The clone is never above 12% and is ~2 ms flat, so the scope note's worry about a full-RGB GPU scratch copy was aimed at nothing.

- **⚠ SUPERSEDED 2026-09-12: that sidecar was edited during M8.3j's confirmation check and now carries `exposure: -0.3` plus a fully saturated HSL.** The reading below was accurate when taken; see M8.3j's section for why a catalogue measurement has a shelf life. **⚠⚠ THIS FILE'S RECORD OF THAT SIDECAR WAS WRONG, AND IT IS CORRECTED IN PLACE BELOW.** The M8.3h next-action block said the mask carries *"noise reduction, exposure, sharpening and grading"*. Read directly from `DSCF6274.RAF.json`, **every field is neutral except `exposure: -3.6`** — NR is `luminance: 0, color: 0` (detail 50 / smoothness 50 are the *defaults*, and `is_active` is amount-only), sharpening amount 0, all four grade wheels 0, all eight HSL bands 0. **A sidecar summarised from memory rather than read.**
- **⚠ The brush is 36 strokes and 1,387 points, 22 of them auto-masked**, so `BrushCache` declines it and it rasterises from scratch on every render the auto-mask coverage cache misses — a **global** slider (which changes the base the gate reads) or a pan. Those are the frames that paid 236 ms, and they are what this milestone targets. ⚠ It does **not** help this mask's own sliders, which were already a cache hit.
- **MEASURED, real engine, DSCF6274.RAF, rung 3200, machine 82.8% idle, three runs:**

  | | before | after | |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **the whole frame** | 294.3 ms | **140.2–143.3** | **2.07×** |
  | the mask's own cost | +234.3 | **+79.9 to +82.1** | **2.9×** |
  | Oklab conversion (`lab`) | 54.2 | **9.6–10.3** | **5.5×** |
  | dab splat (`dabs_ms`) | 162.3 | **53.1–56.0** | **2.9×** |

- **⚠⚠ THE DAB LOOP BECAME A GATHER, AND THAT IS WHAT MADE IT PARALLELISABLE AT ALL.** Per stroke it was three passes over the sub-rect — clear a reused `layer`, **scatter** every dab into it with `max`, composite `layer` into `cov` — and a scatter cannot be split over dabs because dabs overlap. Now each **row** walks the dabs that touch it, keeps its own running max in a row-local scratch, and composites straight into its own row of `cov`. `layer` and the clear pass are gone: three passes become one, and rows are independent.
- **⚠⚠ THE SHORT-CIRCUIT BEFORE THE GATE IS LOAD-BEARING AND A NAIVE REWRITE DESTROYS IT.** `if a <= *slot { continue; }` sits *above* the gate, and is sound because the gate can only ever **reduce** an alpha — so a dab whose positional alpha already loses the running max cannot change the pixel however its gate resolves. Dabs are laid `SPACING` (a quarter radius) apart and overlap heavily, so most of them lose. **A gather that evaluated the gate for every dab touching a pixel would be correct and dramatically slower**, and every test would still pass.
- **⚠⚠ TWO OF THE PLAN'S OWN SABOTAGES WERE PROVABLY INERT, AND FINDING OUT WHY IS THE SHARPEST RESULT HERE.** The plan predicted that reversing the dab order, and replacing `*slot = slot.max(a)` with `*slot = a`, would each fail. **Both passed.** The reason is one property: the within-stroke combine is a `max`, and the skip only ever drops a dab already below it, so the result is exactly `max_d gated_alpha(d)` — **order-independent**, and at the assignment `a > *slot` already holds so the `max` is redundant there. ⚠ **Stroke order therefore matters for the skip's EFFECTIVENESS, not for the value.** A third predicted sabotage (drop each dab's last row) was also inert: at `y = dy1 - 1` the distance exceeds the radius, so `dab_alpha` is already 0. **Three "obvious" sabotages, all no-ops — recorded rather than counted.**
- **⚠⚠ AND THE BIT-IDENTITY TEST WAS BLIND TO THE PARALLEL PATH, WHICH ONLY A SABOTAGE REVEALED.** `SEQUENTIAL_FLOOR_PX` is 64 Ki, so an 80×60 fixture never leaves the sequential branch — the guard written for this milestone could not see the code this milestone added. Caught when a sabotage failed an *unrelated* test (`a_brush_mask_in_a_region_matches_the_same_part_of_the_whole`) while the named guard stayed green. It now runs at **both** 80×60 and 900×700 and **asserts which branch each took**, through a thread-local event counter — the twenty-third instance of a test naming something it could not detect.
- **⚠ `PARALLEL_STROKES` is a `#[cfg(test)]` thread-local COUNTER, not a flag**, because the two branches produce identical pixels by design and nothing in the output can distinguish them — the reason `Ran { bytes }` and the Oklab conversion counter exist. ⚠ **A counter, because an observable describing the current state cannot see its own absence**; ⚠ **thread-local**, because libtest runs in parallel; ⚠ and **incremented on the calling thread, outside the rayon closure**, or it would land on a worker's copy and the test would never see it.
