- **⚠⚠ THE REFERENCE IS A FROZEN VERBATIM COPY OF THE OLD `rasterize_in`, LIVING IN THE TEST MODULE.** The plan's first draft had it *call* `rasterize_in` and read the map back — which would have compared the function under test against itself and passed forever, including against every later sabotage. **Caught in the plan's own self-review, before execution.** Its doc comment says it must never be updated to match: if the two disagree, that is the finding.
- **⚠⚠ THE CHUNK SWEEP INVERTS THE 8-BIT PACK'S FINDING.** There, per-item rayon measured *slower than not threading at all* and coarse blocks were the fix. Here the opposite holds — median `dabs_ms`: **1 → 55.6, 2 → 55.5, 4 → 56.4, 8 → 56.4, 16 → 57.8, 64 → 70.4, 256 → 121.3**. The cause is **load imbalance, not dispatch**: rows differ enormously in how many dabs touch them, so a 256-row task holds a large share of the stroke while every other thread waits. A task here is one row of up to 1510 px against the pack's four bytes. **`CHUNK_ROWS = 4`**, mid-plateau, and it amortises the per-task scratch allocation four ways.
- **⚠ `SEQUENTIAL_FLOOR_PX` was swept too and it earns its place**: `pipeline`'s lib suite reads **0.86–0.98 s at a floor of 0** against **0.74–0.79 at 64 Ki**, with 256 Ki and never-parallel indistinguishable from it. 64 Ki is the *smallest* value at that plateau, which keeps the parallel path reachable for the largest share of real strokes.
- **⚠ Converting only the gating strokes' rows buys NOTHING MEASURABLE HERE, and the mechanism says why.** `gate_rows=1718` of 2019 — **85% of the box gates**, because the 22 auto-masked strokes are spread across the whole painted area. So it saves ~15% of a ~10 ms phase, real and below the noise floor. Kept because it is free at runtime and a brush with one localised gating stroke would gain far more; the `gate_rows` readout makes that visible rather than needing re-derivation. **Measured the mechanism, not only the outcome.**
- **⚠ Six `⚠` findings were nearly lost in the rewrite** — the two-level max-then-composite rule, the gate's placement before the `max`, the no-base positional degradation, `MaskOp`'s shared algebra, the bit-identity of the composite, and the product-algebra argument. Caught by W0's own rule: `grep "⚠" | sort` then `comm` against `HEAD`, **before** committing. All six restored to production rather than surviving only inside the frozen test copy.
- **⚠ Four process traps fired, every one already recorded in this file.** A scripted edit matched nothing and the test then "passed" meaninglessly (caught by the `assert`, twice); `cargo fmt` reflowed an anchor between reading and patching it; and **a `///` doc comment on a `thread_local!` invocation is `unused_doc_comments`**, which `-D warnings` rejects — the exact trap M7.1c recorded, walked into anyway and caught by clippy while 2322 tests passed. At least the seventeenth time clippy has seen what a green suite did not.
- **`RUSTROOM_DEBUG_MASK` is kept permanently** — four phase timers in `MaskStage::apply` (coverage / clone / sub-stages / blend) and three fields in `rasterize_in` (`gate_rows` / `lab` / `dabs_ms`) — the `RUSTROOM_DEBUG_BRUSH` precedent. It is what reframed this milestone. So is `crates/app/examples/mask_breakdown.rs`, the only thing in the repo that prices a mask as a photographer actually has one, real sidecar included.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ~~**nothing for masked HSL's 68.8 ms of sub-stages** — that is M8.3j, and it is the case actually reported in use as slow~~ ✅ **CLOSED 2026-09-11 by M8.3j**, which took that row from 1.10× to 1.99–2.03×; (2) **nothing for a colour range's 61–120 ms blend**, which is already rayon-parallel through `map_pixels_xy` and simply expensive — the range-mask coverage cache in `docs/BACKLOG.md` is the lever there; (3) **coverage still dominates the real photo** at ~64 ms of a ~140 ms frame; (4) **an auto-masked brush is still uncacheable across a global slider**, a property of the gate reading base pixels and unchanged here; (5) the frozen reference will drift out of resemblance and is deliberately not maintained; (6) one machine, one rung, one photographer's single masked photo.

### M8.3h — the cost gate re-tuned (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE (2026-09-13)

**M8.3h — the cost gate re-tuned (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE (2026-09-13).** `TRANSFER_COST` **34.0 → 27.0**. 2318 → **2321 tests** (three added: the decision test, the behaviour test, the frame-equivalence test); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**. Spec `2026-09-11-cost-gate-retune-design.md`, plan `2026-09-11-cost-gate-retune.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE FINDING IS A MAINTENANCE FAILURE, NOT A DESIGN ONE, AND IT IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: A CONSTANT THAT DESCRIBES A MEASURED COST GOES STALE WHEN SOMETHING ELSE IMPROVES THAT COST, AND NOTHING IN THE BUILD SAYS SO.** `TRANSFER_COST` was measured at **M8.3e** and describes one GPU round trip. **M8.3f** then recovered 9.46 ms per render and **M8.3g** took the download from 13.20 ms to 4.78 — each of them making the very quantity the constant describes cheaper, and neither re-measuring it. For two milestones the gate refused runs that would have paid, and every bench table in this file recorded the symptom as *"unedited, colorimetric 1.00×"* without anyone reading it as one.

- **⚠⚠ QUOTE A BAND, NOT A FIGURE — AND THIS SLICE HAD TO RETRACT ITS OWN HEADLINE TO LEARN IT.** Seven `probe_rt` runs at 3200×2136 on a quiet machine: **float 23.0–26.8 ms**, **byte 15.7–21.0**. The first readings taken were 26.80 and 21.02 — **both the top of their bands**. ⚠⚠ On the strength of that single byte reading the spec claimed *"deriving it by subtraction would have been wrong by 45%"*, since M8.3g's components predict 18.4. **Retracted: 18.4 sits comfortably inside 15.7–21.0, so the components composed perfectly well.** The "error" was a point prediction compared against one sample — precisely what M8.3g's control row exists to expose, committed *while citing M8.3g as the reason for measuring*. The measurement was still right to do; it produced the range, and the range is what makes the constant defensible. It simply did not catch the failure it was credited with.
- **⚠ 27.0 is rounded up from the TOP of the float band**, which is what makes it conservative rather than central. `output_transform` at 28.6 clears even the worst reading.
- **⚠⚠ EXACTLY ONE DECISION CHANGES, AND THE FULL TABLE IS WHAT ESTABLISHES THAT** — `exposure` 1.3, `tone_regions` 18.0, `display_rendering` 25.7, `output_transform` 28.6, `color_grading` 48.0, `sharpening` 54.0, `hsl` 60.0. Only **a lone trailing `output_transform`** crosses from refused to accepted. Everything else sits far from the threshold on one side or the other, which is why a re-tune of this size is a one-case change rather than a general loosening.
- **⚠⚠ THE CHAIN-COUNT PROBE CORRECTED THE GOING-IN ASSUMPTION ABOUT MASKS.** The expectation was that a mask **splits** a run and pays two round trips. **It does not.** A mask ends the run, and then neither piece clears the gate: a temporary probe printing each tail and its chain count showed `["mask", "output_transform"]` → **`chains: 0 (+0 trailing)`**. So the GPU toggle was **inert on a masked photograph**, not merely unhelpful — right direction, wrong mechanism, settled by measuring rather than by reading the code.
- **⚠ One conservative constant, not two.** The byte figure is recorded and deliberately unused: a lone `display_rendering` run (25.7) **can** occur — `CreativeLookStage` sits between it and `output_transform`, so a creative look makes it a run of its own — and **that run is never trailing, so it can never take the byte path**. ⚠ Stated honestly and weaker than the spec first claimed: 25.7 is *inside* the float band, so refusing it is not an arithmetic certainty but an application of the gate's own rule — **fail toward the CPU, because a wrong number costs milliseconds and never pixels**. Revisit when a ported stage's cost lands clearly between the bands.
- **⚠⚠ THREE PRE-EXISTING TESTS FAILED AND EVERY FAILURE WAS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR THEIR PREMISES DID NOT ANTICIPATE — the M8.3e pattern exactly.** All three assumed a run containing `output_transform` was unaffordable, which was load-bearing without being stated anywhere.
  - ⚠⚠ **`exposure_alone_is_not_worth_a_chain` WAS PASSING FOR THE WRONG REASON.** Its tail is `[exposure, output_transform]` — one run of 29.9 ms — so it measured *the pair* being refused and **never measured exposure alone**, which is what it is named for. Its name became true for the first time when the fixture was hand-built.
  - **`a_tail_the_cost_gate_refused_hands_nothing_back`** used a colorimetric tail, which is precisely the tail that now chains. ⚠ And since `output_transform` ends every tail and alone clears the bar, **a trailing run can no longer be refused through any real `Edits`** — the property is reachable only by construction now, the same shape M8.3e hit when `output_transform` made "a tail with nothing replaceable" unbuildable.
  - **`a_tail_too_cheap_to_be_worth_a_chain_is_returned_unchanged` fired its OWN fixture check**, because that check hardcoded `28.6` instead of reading it off the stage. **The guard working exactly as designed, and the reason a cost must never be written twice.**
- **⚠ The decision test reads each stage's own `cpu_cost` rather than repeating a literal.** `worth_a_chain(&[28.6])` would write the same number twice and pass against any pair that happened to agree; reading it off the real `GpuOutputTransformStage` and `GpuDisplayRenderingStage` means it still describes the truth if a cost is ever re-measured. ⚠ The `display_rendering` half is not symmetry — it is what pins the one-constant argument.
- **⚠ Sabotage-verified:** putting `34.0` back fails both new tests, with a `test result:` line present so it is a real failure rather than a compile error reading as a pass. ⚠ `a_colorimetric_frame_renders_the_same_picture_on_the_gpu` **passes** under that sabotage and is recorded as inert for it rather than counted — with no chain built the accelerated pipeline *is* the CPU one, so the two agree trivially. ⚠ The three repaired tests also pass under it, which is the point: rebuilt on hand-built tails, they no longer depend on the constant's exact value.
- **MEASURED, real engine, DSCF6291.RAF, rung 3200, machine 74% idle:**

  | case | before | after | saved |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **unedited, colorimetric** | 1.00× (−0.04 ms) | **1.53–1.64×** | **+12.8 to +14.6 ms** |
  | **1 masked exposure (gradient)** | 0.97× (−1.39) | **1.35×** | **+14.44** |
  | **1 masked HSL (gradient)** | 1.00× (+0.07) | **1.10×** | **+10.62** |
  | TYPICAL of this catalogue | 2.33× | 2.15–2.42× | unchanged within noise |
  | hsl only | 4.16× | 4.22–4.36× | unchanged within noise |

  ⚠ **~11–15 ms, above the 8–13 ms predicted**, and reproducible across three runs — which matters because the predicted band was only ~2–3× the ±4 ms noise floor. ⚠ The masked rows were **measured rather than inferred from "the trailing run is the same"**; that mechanism reasoning has been wrong three times in this project, and this time it happened to hold.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **one case and modest** — frames whose tail ends in a lone `output_transform`; (2) ⚠⚠ **this does NOT make the mask loop unnecessary** — a masked photograph gains ~11–14 ms and remains fundamentally unaccelerated at 120 ms (1 masked HSL) and 290 ms (3 masked HSL), which is M8.3i; (3) **the gate still ignores GPU execution entirely**, comparing CPU work against the transfer and saying nothing about the dispatches; (4) one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), two rungs — the constant has been machine-specific since M8.3e; (5) **a lone `display_rendering` run stays on the CPU** at 25.7 ms, correctly per the argument above but real work left unaccelerated whenever a creative look is active; (6) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**.

### M8.3g — the 8-bit readback (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE (2026-09-13)

**M8.3g — the 8-bit readback (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE (2026-09-13).** When the accelerated tail ends in a GPU chain and nothing downstream needs the float, the chain quantizes on the GPU and downloads **RGBA8 — 27 MB instead of 82** at rung 3200. 2306 → **2318 tests**; 63 goldens ran and **none moved**. Spec `2026-09-11-eight-bit-readback-design.md`, plan `2026-09-11-eight-bit-readback.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE PROJECTION MISSED, AND BY A FACTOR OF TWO.** The spec assembled **10.6 ms** from component measurements — 8.4 ms of download plus `pack`'s ~2.2 ms quantize. Measured on the real engine, **A/B on one binary and one machine state**, the GPU column at rung 3200:

| case | float path | **byte path** | saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TYPICAL of this catalogue** | 44.31 ms | **37.28** | **7.03** |
| unedited, camera rendering | 38.16 | **32.74** | 5.42 |
| hsl only | 34.75 | **29.46** | 5.29 |
| hsl + grade + sharpening | 51.14 | **46.81** | 4.33 |
| *unedited, colorimetric* — **the control** | *36.87* | *40.94* | *−4.07* |

⚠⚠ **THE CONTROL ROW IS THE MOST USEFUL LINE IN THE TABLE.** A colorimetric frame runs **no chain at all** in either build — the cost gate declines it — so its −4.07 ms is **pure run-to-run noise**, measured rather than assumed. The noise floor on this machine is therefore about **±4 ms**, which is comparable to the effect: the saving is **~5–7 ms and cannot honestly be stated more precisely than that**. Four of four chained rows improved in both comparisons, so the effect is real; the *number* is soft. ⚠ **Adding up component measurements over-predicted a whole frame by ~2×** — the same class of error as M8.3e's "~10 ms of per-encode overhead", arriving from the opposite direction, and the third time in three milestones that a decomposition has failed to compose.

- **Against M8.3f's recorded figures** (different machine load, so read the deltas as approximate): TYPICAL **42.32 → 37.28 ms, 1.88× → 2.20×**; camera rendering 1.55× → 1.84×; hsl only 3.19× → 3.74×; hsl+grade+sharpening 3.20× → 3.85×. Rung 1600 TYPICAL reads **2.25×**. ⚠ The CPU column moved 79.75 → 81.91 between those runs by itself, which is the reason the A/B above exists.
- **⚠⚠ THE DOWNLOAD DOES NOT SCALE 4×, AND `CLAUDE.md`'s OWN NEXT ACTION SAID IT DID.** Decomposed with `probe_breakdown` (kept, `#[ignore]`d in `chain.rs`), at 3200×2136 with each step on its own submit:

  | readback | copy+map | `to_vec` | total |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 82 MB (f32) | 6.33 | 6.87 | **13.20** |
  | **27 MB (RGBA8)** | 2.59 | 2.19 | **4.78** |
  | 6.8 MB | 1.32 | 0.57 | 1.89 |
  | ~256 B | 1.28 | 0.00 | **1.28 — the fixed cost** |

  **2.8×, not 4×**, because a download carries a fixed cost no size reduction touches. ⚠ The same probe retires a question M8.3a left open: the **upload half is 9.8 ms and cannot shrink at all** — the input is scene-referred f32, and WebGPU forbids `MAP_WRITE | STORAGE`, so there is no zero-copy path to find. ⚠ And the **four dispatches are 11.61 ms**, now the largest single item and untouched by any of this.
- **⚠⚠ WGSL's `round` BREAKS TIES TO THE *EVEN* WHOLE NUMBER; RUST'S `f32::round` BREAKS THEM *AWAY FROM ZERO*.** `ImageBuf::quantize` is `(v.clamp(0,1) * 255.0).round()`, and `v * 255` lands on exact halves routinely — so a transliterated `round()` in the shader is correct on every ordinary value and **off by one level on every tie**. The shader uses `floor(v * 255.0 + 0.5)`. ⚠⚠ **A fixture that never lands on a half cannot see this**, which is why the test's fixture carries every tie `(2k+1)/510` — and the sabotage's failure is exactly that signature: GPU 0 against CPU 1 at the `0.5` tie and 2 against 3 at `2.5`, **while `1.5` matches because 2 is already even**. Confirmed empirically rather than read out of the spec. ⚠ `pack4x8unorm` specifies the same `floor(0.5 + 255·clamp(..))` and was still not used: writing the rule out is what lets a reader check it against `quantize` without consulting the WGSL spec.
- **⚠ NaN must reach 0, and `clamp` is not what does it.** On the CPU that happens through the saturating `as u8` cast — `f32::clamp` returns NaN for NaN — so the shader tests `v != v` explicitly.
- **⚠⚠ THE GATE IS FOUR CONDITIONS ACROSS TWO CRATES, WHICH IS THE SHAPE THIS FILE RECORDS AS GOING WRONG SILENTLY — so each half is answered where it is provable.** Three things downstream need the float: a **non-sRGB display space** (`pack` converts from the float deliberately, because an 8-bit → 8-bit conversion "costs roughly 0.8 bits and shows as banding on a smooth sky" — its own comment), **Visualize Spots** (the edge view is computed from it) and **soft proofing** (the ProPhoto run is decoded back to the working space). Those are derived **once** in `render_cached` and passed down. The fourth — *is this chain last, and does it end in `output_transform`* — is answered **by construction inside `accelerate`**, which is the only code that knows how the tail was regrouped; a caller holding the finished `Pipeline` could only recognise a chain by downcasting. ⚠ The **grade range view** is a fourth float consumer needing no work at all: it bypasses `accelerate` entirely, which was checked rather than assumed.
- **⚠ `accelerate` returns `(Pipeline, Option<GpuChain>)`**, and `rejoin` puts it back for the paths wanting one plain pipeline. ⚠ The alternative — a method on `PipelineStage` — was rejected because it leaks an output-encoding concern into the seam trait this file keeps deliberately free of them, giving every stage in the workspace a method that is `None` for all but one. ⚠ And *expand the bytes back to f32 inside the chain*, the only option needing no API change, gives back most of what it saves: `pack`'s quantize stays **and** a 27 MB → 82 MB expand pass is added.
- **⚠ `pack`'s `Rgba8` arm carries no `ImageBuf` at all**, which is what keeps it small: the histogram already came from the quantized bytes — deliberately, so it describes the image rather than the monitor — and `srgb` and `rgba` become **one shared allocation**, precisely the existing sRGB branch. The three float-only features are **unrepresentable** on that arm rather than guarded against.
- **⚠⚠ WHICH TEST EXERCISES THE `output_transform` NAME GUARD IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE, and the plan predicted the guard would be unreachable.** A *trailing CPU stage* does **not** reach it — there the final flush is empty and `None` comes back whether or not the name is checked. Only a chain that genuinely **is** last while ending in something else does, which no `Edits` can produce (that stage ends every tail and is itself replaceable), so the fixture is hand-built. The guard is therefore exercised rather than recorded as inert — better than the plan asked for.
- **⚠ `Ran { prefix_stages, bytes }` is the observable, returned and discarded in production.** The byte path and the float path produce **identical frames by design**, so nothing in the output can distinguish them and only an explicit counter can — the same reason `prefix_stages` exists, since the correctness tests would all pass with the prefix cache deleted. ⚠ **Per render rather than a process-wide static**: `cargo test` runs in parallel and a global counter reading someone else's renders is a contaminated observable this project has already paid for once, in `GpuChain`'s transfer counts. ⚠ `bytes` is **derived** from what was produced (`matches!(out, Packed::Rgba8 { .. })`) rather than tracked alongside it — two facts that can disagree is the shape `render_max_dim` and `Session::geometry_mode` were each fixed for.
- **⚠ Sabotage-verified in both directions**, which is what the fourth gate test exists for: forcing the gate **open** fails the three condition tests; forcing it **shut** fails the byte test *and* the carrier's own fixture check. Three "does not take the byte path" tests alone would pass against an implementation that never takes it at all.
- **⚠⚠ THREE SCRIPTED-EDIT FAILURES ON ONE BRANCH, EACH CAUGHT BY A DIFFERENT GUARD, AND ONE OF THEM REACHED A COMMIT.** (1) A `python` edit splicing by a **computed index** (`s.index('    }\n}\n')`) matched the *end of the file* and **deleted ten tests**, including the barrier test — and `git add -A` committed it. Caught by reading `git show --stat` afterwards, which is one commit too late; repaired and the commit amended to a pure addition. (2) **Two sabotages silently failed to apply** because `cargo fmt` had reflowed the target expression onto two lines, and the tests then "passed" against correct code — caught by the `assert`, which is exactly why that rule exists. (3) An insertion **separated `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` from the function it was written for**, silently reattaching it to the new struct — caught **only by clippy**, while 2318 tests passed. ⚠ One root: *trusting that a scripted edit landed where it was aimed*. **Read `git diff --stat` and `git diff | grep '^-'` BEFORE committing, not after.**
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **no win with a non-sRGB display space, under Visualize Spots, or while soft proofing** — the gate, and on Linux/Windows the first of those is a real setting rather than a hypothetical; (2) **the measured saving is ~5–7 ms against a ±4 ms noise floor**, so the ratio improvements above are directionally solid and numerically soft; (3) ⚠ **the bench machine was not quiet** — WindowServer ~36% and Firefox ~30% — which biases the CPU column and so the ratios optimistically, the same caveat M8.3f carried; (4) **the dispatches (11.6 ms) and the upload (9.8 ms) are untouched**, and the upload *cannot* be improved; (5) nothing helps **export**; (6) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**; (7) measured on one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), at one rung.

### M8.3f — a GPU resource cache (2026-09-11)

**M8.3f — a GPU resource cache (2026-09-11).** The wgpu objects a render builds now survive it: per shader, the module, the layout and its pipelines; plus a small pool of staging buffers. 2306 tests (2299 → 2303 → 2306); 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, which is the proof a caching change changed no pixel. Spec `2026-09-11-gpu-resource-cache-design.md`, plan `2026-09-11-gpu-resource-cache.md`.

**⚠⚠ THIS FILE'S OWN ~10 ms ACCOUNTING WAS RIGHT IN MAGNITUDE AND WRONG BY ~8× IN ATTRIBUTION, AND MEASURING BEFORE DESIGNING IS THE ONLY REASON THAT WAS CAUGHT.** M8.3e recorded the gap between its 1.54× and its projected ~1.9–2.1× as *"the shader module, the pipeline and every uniform and LUT buffer being recreated on every encode"* — and flagged it, correctly, as **a consistent explanation rather than a measured one**. Instrumented (`Dispatch::encode` and `GpuChain::run`, temporarily) at 3200×2136, TYPICAL four-stage chain, warm:

| item | ms |
|---|---|
| **staging buffer allocation** | **7.2** |
| GPU wait — 82 MB in, 4 dispatches, 82 MB out | 21.5 |
| readback `to_vec` of 82 MB | 6.5 |
| memcpy into the staging buffer | 2.6 |
| **encode: modules + pipelines + layouts + bind groups + every LUT, ×4 stages** | **1.2** |
| image buffer + readback buffer allocation | 0.07 |
| submit | 0.07 |

**So the pipeline and shader cache — the thing the note named and the thing that was asked for — is worth 1.2 ms of ~39, about 3%.** Metal already caches compiled shaders by source, so warm module creation is 0.10–0.12 ms per stage and pipeline creation 0.04–0.08; only the first render pays real compilation (round 0 reads 1.41 ms for one pipeline). ⚠ The ~10 ms was nonetheless real — the milestone recovered **9.46 ms** — which is the useful shape of the correction: **a total can be right while every word of its explanation is wrong.**

- **⚠⚠ THE 7.2 ms IS ONE BUFFER, AND THE REASON IS `mapped_at_creation: true` RATHER THAN THE ALLOCATION.** The 82 MB *image* buffer costs **0.05 ms** and the 82 MB *readback* buffer **0.02** — same size, same device, both cheap. It is the **mapping** that is expensive. "Recreated on every encode" was the right diagnosis aimed at the wrong object.
- **⚠⚠ THE DESIGN'S CENTRAL RISK WAS PROBED BEFORE THE SPEC WAS WRITTEN, NOT AFTER.** Reuse means `map_async(Write)` instead of `mapped_at_creation`; if that cost what the allocation did there was no feature. Measured on a 78.2 MiB buffer: **8.3–9.8 ms to allocate against 0.00–0.01 ms to map**, and the write itself is faster on warm pages (2.4–3.5 against 3.8–5.5). ⚠ Safe **only because `GpuChain::run` is synchronous** — it blocks on `poll(Wait)` until readback completes, so the GPU is idle by the next map. An asynchronous chain would need a ring and that reasoning would not survive it.
- **⚠⚠ ONE SHARED STAGING BUFFER WAS WRONG, AND THE PARALLEL TEST SUITE FOUND IT AS 28 FAILURES WITHIN A MINUTE OF SHIPPING IT.** `Buffer is already mapped`, plus **wrong pixels** in `a_subnormal_result_is_flushed_to_zero_on_the_gpu`. ⚠ **Not a test artefact — a real corruption bug in Compare**: the cache is process-wide while rendering is not, and each Compare pane owns a `RenderEngine` on its own thread with the full-resolution worker a third. It is a `Vec` pool now (`MAX_STAGING = 4`), taken before the upload and **returned only after `poll(Wait)` confirms the submission finished**, since the GPU reads it during the submit. ⚠ The user's "one buffer, grown to the largest seen" survives inside it: a buffer too small for the render asking is dropped rather than kept. **A design measured carefully, specced and planned was still wrong about concurrency, and only running the suite in parallel showed it.**
- **⚠⚠ `GpuExposureStage` HAD NEVER BEEN A `Dispatch` CLIENT, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE TO THE PROBE.** Written at M8.3a *before* `Dispatch` existed; M8.3e's `ee75477` made it **replaceable** without folding it in. So it carried its own ~90-line copy of the layout/bind/pipeline dance, printed no per-stage probe line, and **by subtraction was ~0.6 ms of the 1.17 ms encode — half of it, for one stage of four.** Folded in here: `exposure.rs` 366 → 279 lines, shader text, params and grid all unchanged, and **its bit-exactness tests passing unchanged is the proof the fold moved no behaviour**.
- **⚠⚠ THE CACHE LIVES ON `GpuContext` BECAUSE NOTHING SHORTER-LIVED WOULD WORK — a placement that is forced rather than chosen.** `accelerate` rebuilds `GpuChain` and every `GpuStage` box on **every render**, so a cache owned by a chain or a stage is discarded each frame and buys exactly nothing.
- **⚠⚠ KEYED ON THE SHADER TEXT, NEVER THE LABEL.** Every shader here is a constant prelude plus a constant body — `luma_wgsl()` and sharpen's `.replace(..)` substitute *compile-time* constants — so **a label key works today** and breaks silently the first time a stage bakes a parameter into its WGSL, serving a stale pipeline and a plausible-but-wrong picture. Hashing 2–4 KB is ~1 µs against the 0.10 ms it removes. `PrefixKey`'s rule: fail toward a miss.
- **⚠ Sharpen is the largest single beneficiary and is not a `Dispatch` client** — it builds one module and **up to eight pipelines** per encode, more program objects than every other stage combined. It encodes eight dispatches over shared scratch planes, a different shape wearing a similar name, so it calls the cache directly; `sharpen.rs` now creates no wgpu program object at all.
- **⚠ What is deliberately NOT cached, with the numbers:** the image buffer (0.05 ms), the readback buffer (0.02), the uniforms (~0.01/stage), the LUTs (~0.02/stage), the bind groups (~0.00). Each references this render's buffers or this render's **edits**, so caching them would add an invalidation risk whose failure mode is a wrong picture rather than a slow one.
- **⚠⚠ TWO OF MY OWN TESTS NAMED A BUG THEY COULD NOT DETECT — the twenty-first and twenty-second instances, both found by the sabotage step and neither by review.** (1) **The miss counter was written as `1` on every insert**, so a cache recompiling on *every* call still reported 1 and the delta assertion read 0 either way — the "never consult the cache" sabotage **passed**. ⚠ **An observable that describes the current state cannot see its own absence; it has to count events.** (2) **`two_renders_in_flight_never_share_a_buffer` never put a buffer back**, so both takes hit the *empty-pool* branch and the take-from-pool path — the one a sharing bug lives in — was never reached; it passed while 26 other tests failed. ⚠ **A fixture must contain the thing a wrong implementation would be attracted to**, the same correction `spot_source`'s four blind tests needed.
- **⚠ Five sabotages, and one PREDICTION CORRECTED.** Label key → 3 tests. Never consult the cache → 2 (after the counter fix). `slice(..)` for `slice(..bytes)` → 14. One shared buffer → 26, plus its named guard after the fixture fix. ⚠ **Skipping the map wait was predicted to be inert and is not** — 14 tests fail.
- **⚠ A process trap, twice in one session: a scripted patch silently did not apply because `cargo fmt` had reflowed its target**, and the shell carried on so the sabotage re-run "passed" meaninglessly. The `assert` caught it; the retry prints `PATCH LANDED` / `SABOTAGE APPLIED` explicitly. **Assert the edit landed, and print it.**
- **MEASURED, real engine, DSCF6291.RAF — the number this is judged by** (`bench_gpu_tail`; `gpu_run_bench`'s synthetic TYPICAL went **1.68× → 2.38×**, 41.70 → 31.03 ms):

  | rung 3200, ~6.5 Mpx | CPU | GPU M8.3e | GPU M8.3f | was | now |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | **TYPICAL of this catalogue** | 79.75 ms | 51.78 | **42.32** | 1.54× | **1.88×** |
  | unedited, camera rendering | 57.43 | 45.89 | **37.16** | 1.26× | **1.55×** |
  | unedited, colorimetric | 38.66 | 36.98 | 36.77 | 1.00× | 1.05× |
  | hsl only | 104.18 | 43.29 | **32.65** | 2.53× | **3.19×** |
  | hsl + grade + sharpening | 176.63 | 64.75 | **55.15** | 2.81× | **3.20×** |

  ⚠ **1.88× lands in M8.3e's own projected 1.9–2.1× band**, which is the projection arriving — from a different object than the one it named. ⚠ The fit rung (1600, ~1.7 Mpx) reads TYPICAL **1.84×** and `hsl + grade + sharpening` **3.29×**; M8.3e's table had no fit-rung rows. ⚠ The colorimetric row runs **no chain at all** — the cost gate still declines it — so its 1.05× is noise on one code path, not a win.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **up to four 82 MB staging buffers can be held resident** once you render at rung 3200 with the tail on, and nothing releases them — the pool is bounded by concurrency, so one thread means one buffer; (2) **nothing helps export**, since `batch_export` never calls `accelerate` and ~93% of an export is libraw's demosaic upstream of everything wgpu touches; (3) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**; (4) **the first render still compiles shaders** (~150 ms) — `wgpu::PipelineCache`, a driver-level compilation cache persistable to disk, is the answer to that and is **not** taken: it addresses only the cold start, nothing for the 0.10 ms warm module creation and nothing for the buffer, and is backend-limited; (5) ⚠⚠ **the two larger levers are untouched — 21.5 ms of GPU wait and 6.5 ms of readback copy — and the 8-bit readback is still worth more than this whole milestone**; (6) the reuse argument depends on `run()` being synchronous; (7) measured on one machine, one adapter (Apple M2, Metal), at one buffer size, and ⚠ **not on a perfectly quiet machine** — SkyLight, Firefox and the editor were live, which biases the CPU column and so the ratios slightly optimistic.

### M8.3e — the per-pixel tail on the GPU (2026-09-11)

**M8.3e — the per-pixel tail on the GPU (2026-09-11).** Four more stages run as compute shaders, so on an ordinary photograph the **entire tail** is one chain and one round trip. 2278 → **2299 tests**; 63 goldens ran and **none moved**. Spec `2026-09-11-per-pixel-tail-design.md`, plan `2026-09-11-per-pixel-tail.md`.

**⚠⚠ THE MILESTONE I PROPOSED WAS MEASURED WRONG, AND MEASURING BEFORE DESIGNING IS THE ONLY REASON IT DID NOT SHIP.** After M8.3d I recommended porting `display_rendering` next on one number: it is active on **100% of this catalogue's 40 sidecars**, where `hsl` is on 0%, `color_grading` 5% and `sharpening` 2.5%. Right diagnosis, wrong prescription:

| at 3200×2136 (6.8 Mpx, 82 MB) | |
|---|---|
| `display_rendering` on the CPU | **22.2 ms** |
| one GPU round trip (a one-stage chain) | **34.0 ms** |

**Porting it alone would have made the typical photograph ~10 ms per frame SLOWER.** M8.3a's finding arriving exactly where it was predicted — *the transfer is everything* — and it means **stage popularity is the wrong selection criterion on its own. The criterion is how much CPU work a contiguous run can put across one bridge.**

- **⚠⚠ THE STRUCTURAL FACT THE WHOLE DESIGN RESTS ON: an inactive stage is not a neutral stage in the list, it is ABSENT.** `build_pipeline_split_in_region` pushes a stage only when `is_active()`, so printed for real edits (`probe_tail`): neutral is `["output_transform"]`, neutral+rendering is `["display_rendering", "output_transform"]`, and **typical is `["exposure", "tone_regions", "display_rendering", "output_transform"]`**. ⚠ The eleven stages this catalogue never touches are not obstacles in the middle of the tail — so porting the per-pixel set does not add a stage to a chain, it makes the ordinary photograph's **whole tail** one chain, which is the case M8.3c's run-merging was built for and had never been able to serve.
- **⚠⚠ MEASURED ON THE REAL ENGINE, AND THE TYPICAL ROW WENT FROM NOTHING TO 1.54×.** Rung 3200, DSCF6291.RAF:

  | case | CPU | GPU | | saved |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | **TYPICAL of this catalogue** | 79.58 ms | 51.78 ms | **1.54×** | **+27.8 ms** |
  | unedited, camera rendering | 58.03 | 45.89 | 1.26× | +12.1 |
  | unedited, colorimetric | 36.88 | 36.98 | **1.00×** | −0.09 |
  | hsl only | 109.47 | 43.29 | 2.53× | +66.2 |
  | hsl + grade + sharpening | 181.76 | 64.75 | **2.81×** | +117.0 |

  ⚠ That first row read **0.97×** before this milestone. ⚠ The last two improved (2.18 → 2.81×) **without being touched**, because `output_transform` now joins their chain.
- **⚠⚠ 1.54× IS BELOW THE ~1.9–2.1× THE SPEC PROJECTED, AND THE GAP IS NOT NOISE — it is ~10 ms of per-encode overhead, which is caveat 4 arriving with a number.** Accounting at rung 3200: the colorimetric frame is 36.88 ms of which the tail is ~27, so non-tail frame cost is ~10 ms; TYPICAL's tail is then ~70 ms on the CPU against ~42 on the GPU, of which the round trip is ~32. **The residual ~10 ms is the shader module, the pipeline and every uniform and LUT buffer being recreated on every single encode** — now four times per frame rather than three. ⚠ A pipeline cache is the standing answer and it now has a price tag; ⚠ this is a *consistent* explanation rather than a measured one, and the way to settle it is to cache and re-run.
- **⚠⚠ `output_transform` IS THE SECOND MOST EXPENSIVE STAGE IN THE TAIL, WHICH I HAD ASSUMED WAS TRIVIAL.** 28.63 ms at 6.8 Mpx — three `powf` per pixel, twenty million transcendentals. Leaving it on the CPU caps the typical win at **1.2×** instead of 2.2×. ⚠ It is also on **every** photograph, which is what forced the cost gate.
- **⚠⚠ THE COST GATE, AND IT IS WORK RATHER THAN A STAGE COUNT.** `GpuStage::cpu_cost()` in ms per 6.8 Mpx; a run is chained only when its total exceeds `TRANSFER_COST = 34.0`. Without it a neutral frame would build a one-stage chain and pay 34 ms for 28.6 ms of work — **a regression where there is none today**, felt exactly while browsing. ⚠ A count is the wrong gate: one expensive stage pays easily (`hsl` alone is 2.53×) where three cheap ones do not. ⚠⚠ **The comparison is SCALE-FREE, which is what makes it one constant per stage rather than a table per rung** — both sides are linear in pixel count, confirmed rather than assumed at 4× the pixels giving **3.9×** the round trip. ⚠ It fails toward the CPU, so a wrong number costs milliseconds and never pixels — the distinction from the cost heuristic `PrefixCache` deliberately refused, where a wrong guess would have changed what was *rendered*. ⚠ Verified end to end: the colorimetric case reports **0 chains** and **0 of 5,126,400 samples differing**.
- **⚠⚠ AND IT RESHAPED `accelerate`, WHICH THE PLAN CAUGHT AND THE COMPILER WOULD NOT HAVE.** The run held `Box<dyn GpuStage>` and had already **dropped** the CPU stage — so a refused run had nothing to put back, and `GpuStage::cpu()` hands out a *borrow* that cannot be pushed into the output. The run carries **both halves** now and `flush` chooses.
- **⚠⚠ TWO OF THE FOUR STAGES ARE NOT BUILT FROM `Edits` AT ALL**, which the plan did not anticipate. `display_rendering`'s curve and baseline come from the **camera profile**, which `pipeline` never loads; `output_transform`'s space is a property of the *render* (sRGB for the preview, ProPhoto for a soft proof). `accelerate` and `Builder` now carry a `ProfileRendering` **and** a `RenderSpec` — the whole spec rather than just the space, because it also holds the white-balance baseline plan 2 needs, so that is one signature change instead of two.
- **⚠⚠ AND THE CPU TAIL FILTERS OUT AN IDENTITY PROFILE CURVE BEFORE BUILDING THE STAGE.** Skipping that in the GPU builder would render every camera whose profile declares one differently from the CPU — **which is most of them, the X-T4 included**. It is `pipeline::effective_profile_curve` now, called by both rather than remembered twice.
- **⚠⚠ A SABOTAGE WENT UNCAUGHT, AND THE REPLACEMENT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE STAGE — the twentieth instance of the standing lesson.** Deleting `clamp(v, 0, 1)` before `pow` in the output transform left **all five tests green, including the one written for it**. Two blindnesses compounded: **sRGB's toe branch catches a negative before `pow` ever sees it** (`c <= 0.0031308` is true of every negative), so the NaN never happens in the one space that test used — it happens in Adobe RGB, which reaches `pow` directly; and the output is then **negative rather than 0**, while `compare` converts to **8-bit levels**, where a negative sample and 0 quantize identically. ⚠ The guard is now the property the stage really has — **no space may emit a sample outside [0,1]**, on raw floats, across all four — which catches the negative leak *and* the NaN in every mode rather than naming one trap and probing where it is inert. It fails with `Srgb emitted -7.46`.
- **⚠⚠ THE OUTPUT MATRIX IS EXTRACTED FROM `OutputSpace::from_working` BY ITS BASIS VECTORS, NEVER COPIED.** It is a linear map, so its columns *are* the images of the basis vectors — which means no second copy of any matrix can go stale, ProPhoto's identity included. ⚠ This repo has already shipped a **row-swapped P3 matrix that passed every test using a neutral fixture**, which is why the equivalence test's fixture is coloured.
- **⚠ The WGSL luminance prelude substitutes `color::PROPHOTO_LUMA` rather than transcribing it**, which is strictly stronger than `oklab_wgsl` — that one carries its matrices as literals and is guarded *behaviourally*, because parsing digits out of a shader string breaks on reformatting. Here the constant is three numbers, so the two **cannot** disagree rather than being checked for agreeing. ⚠ `color`'s own doc records six copies of a Rec.709 triple all becoming wrong on one day; this is the seventh place it is needed and the first that cannot go stale.
- **⚠⚠ `tone_regions` IS THE ONE STAGE WHOSE LUT DID NOT ALREADY EXIST, so building it introduces a quantization the CPU does not have** — and `LUT_SIZE` was **swept rather than chosen**: 1024 passes at only **1.4× margin and was rejected**; 2048 gives **5.1×** for 8 KB; 4096 gives 21×. ⚠ The worst case sits at luminance **0.0034** in every row, because the table is linear in luminance while the weights are shaped on the **display encoding** of it — the same reason `DisplayRenderingStage` needed 4096. ⚠ `LUT_TOP` is exactly **1.0 and that is a fact rather than a safe bound**: `gain_for_luma` clamps its own input, so the last entry is the *exact* answer for every scene-referred highlight, which has its own test.
- **⚠ `display_rendering` is the one tonal stage that deliberately does NOT preserve hue** — curving the three channels independently is where a camera rendering's shadow saturation comes from. A shader that "fixed" that would be a different stage wearing the same name, and **only the saturated-pixel test can see it**; a neutral fixture cannot. Sabotage-verified.
- **⚠ `exposure` cost one table row.** `GpuExposureStage` had existed since M8.3a as the seam's proof and was never reachable. ⚠ A pre-existing **fixture check fired on it**: the test asserting a tail with nothing replaceable is returned unchanged had been *using exposure as its example of an unreplaceable stage*. It said so loudly rather than going vacuous.
- **⚠⚠ FOUR PRE-EXISTING TESTS FAILED AND EVERY FAILURE WAS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR THEIR PREMISES DID NOT ANTICIPATE.** `output_transform` is in **every** tail, so *"a tail with nothing replaceable"* can no longer be constructed at all — that test now exercises the **cost gate** end to end instead, which is a better test than the one it replaced. And the merge tests' `after.len() == before.len() - N` arithmetic encodes *how many* stages merged, which changes every time a stage is ported; it is `no_replaceable_survives` now, which is what they meant.
- **⚠ The wgpu boilerplate was extracted FIRST, alone, as a pure refactor** — `hsl` and `grading` carried the same ~120 lines and four more stages of that shape were coming. ⚠ Its acceptance was that the gpu-pipeline count was **44 before and after, unchanged**, not "still green". ⚠ `sharpen` is deliberately not a client: it encodes eight dispatches over scratch planes.
- **⚠ A commit went in with clippy at 101 and was amended** — the gate was sequenced with `&&`, so the commit ran because `tail` succeeded. At least the sixteenth recorded instance, by someone who had just written the rule into the plan. ⚠ And the `cargo fmt` reflow trap fired twice more, making two scripted edits match nothing; both were caught by asserting the edit landed.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **a colorimetric unedited frame is deliberately not accelerated** — the gate keeps it on the CPU rather than losing ~5 ms, and it reads 1.00×; (2) **~10 ms per frame of per-encode overhead at rung 3200**, which is the gap between 1.54× and the projection and the clearest lever left; (3) **nothing here helps export** — `batch_export` never calls `accelerate`, and ~93% of an export is libraw's demosaic upstream of everything `wgpu` touches; (4) **`gpu_tail` is still off by default**; (5) **the 8-bit readback is deliberately not taken** — with `output_transform` ending the chain the result is display-referred `[0,1]` and could download as RGBA8, **4× less readback and the larger half of the transfer**, but it changes `GpuChain`'s contract and `pack`'s role; (6) the cost constants are measured on one machine at one buffer size, as a *ratio* against a transfer measured the same way; (7) **the bench was taken alongside an unrelated `julia` job holding one of eight cores for 203 hours**, which biases the CPU column pessimistic and so the ratios slightly optimistic; (8) **local contrast, the vignette and the creative LUT are still not ported** — spatial, position-dependent and a 3-D table respectively, each a different mechanism; (9) **plan 2 is outstanding**: white balance, contrast, tone curve and saturation, which change the typical row by nothing and are coverage.

### M8.3d — colour grading on the GPU (2026-09-11)

**M8.3d — colour grading on the GPU (2026-09-11).** The stage that was splitting the merged run now runs on it, so `hsl + grade + sharpening` is **one chain of three**. 2270 → **2278 tests**; 63 goldens ran and **none moved**. Spec `2026-09-11-gpu-grading-design.md`, plan `2026-09-11-gpu-grading.md`.

⚠⚠ **THIS TAKES THE M8.3d SLOT AND RENUMBERS WHAT WAS THERE**, because M8.3c's own measurement moved it ahead: **the mask loop is now M8.3e** and **the prefix M8.3f**. Any older text in this file or `docs/BACKLOG.md` saying *"M8.3d — the mask loop"* is stale.

- **⚠⚠ THE ACCEPTANCE ROW WENT 1.04× → 2.05×, AND IT IS NOW THE BEST RATIO IN THE BENCH.** X-T4, 1600×1068 (19.6 MB), release, best of 4 warm rounds:

  | tail | CPU | GPU | | |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | hsl only | 25.70 ms | 16.42 ms | 1.56× | 1 chain |
  | hsl + sharpening | 39.35 ms | 25.75 ms | 1.53× | 1 chain |
  | **hsl + grade + sharpening** | **51.40 ms** | **25.12 ms** | **2.05×** | **1 chain** (was 1.04× across 2) |

  ⚠⚠ **The GPU column barely moves — 25.75 → 25.12 ms — while the CPU column climbs 39.35 → 51.40.** So the grade costs the CPU ~12 ms and the GPU **nothing measurable once the buffer is already resident**, which is the clearest statement of the whole GPU-tail thesis anywhere in this project: the transfer is the cost, and a stage added to a run that already pays it is close to free.
- **⚠ It was cheap because the stage was ALREADY a LUT, and that was its own founding decision rather than anything this slice did.** `ColorGradingStage` collapses all three wheels plus Global into a **256-entry table on Oklab L**, built once per render — so per pixel the shader is an Oklab round trip, one lookup with a lerp, and three adds. **No `atan2`, no `cos`/`sin`, no band weighting, no branch**: strictly simpler than `HslStage`, which needed the rotation identity and two Taylor polynomials.
- **⚠ The table is the CPU stage's own, uploaded** — `ColorGradingStage::lut()`, mirroring `HueTable::entries`. Two constructions of one table is how they come to disagree about Blending and Balance, and **nothing in the rendered image would announce it** because both answers are plausible photographs.
- **⚠⚠ ONE SHARED WGSL OKLAB PRELUDE, AND ITS GUARD IS BEHAVIOURAL RATHER THAN TEXTUAL.** `cbrt_signed` and both matrices moved into `oklab_wgsl::OKLAB_WGSL`, concatenated into both shaders — a second copy is the shape this file records at its worst, **six copies of a Rec.709 luma triple all becoming wrong the day the working space changed**, and WGSL has no compiler checking these against `color::oklab`. ⚠ The first design said *parse the constants out of the shader string*; checking `color::oklab` killed that — **the matrices are literals inside the two functions, not public constants**, so parsing compares digits to digits and breaks on any reformatting. Instead: **a neutral grade has an all-zero LUT, so the shader reduces to exactly `oklab_to_prophoto(prophoto_to_oklab(rgb))`** — a pure round trip that `the_wgsl_prelude_agrees_with_color_oklab` compares against `color::oklab`'s own, through the real stage and with no extra machinery. The shape `the_profile_agrees_with_our_own_maths` already uses against lcms2.
- **⚠ The extraction's verification is that `hsl`'s OWN equivalence test passed unchanged.** It is behaviour-preserving or it is not, and one wrong digit fails it — sabotage-verified, three hsl tests fell.
- **⚠⚠ THE INDEX IS CLAMPED, NEVER THE PIXEL'S LIGHTNESS.** `grade_at` clamps the table index; a scene-referred value above white has `L > 1`, and clamping the **value** drags every highlight back toward white. ⚠ Invisible on an in-gamut fixture, and still a plausible photograph when it happens — the identical trap `ProfileHueSatMap`'s `v` is documented for. ⚠ Honestly: the equivalence tests catch it too, because the fixture deliberately carries an above-white sample; the named test adds the **diagnosis** and a floor under that fixture ever being narrowed.
- **⚠⚠ AND THE BENCH FOUND A GAP IN THE CARRIER TEST — the most useful thing in the slice.** The bench reported **0.01153 levels** of divergence on the three-stage chain while `a_three_stage_run_renders_the_same_picture`, asserting **< 0.01**, passed. The cause: `ramp()` never exceeds 1.0 and the bench's ramp reaches **1.2×**, so the test was blind to the regime being measured. ⚠⚠ **The fix was the fixture, not the number** — its own `scene_ramp()` reaching 1.2 — and then an honest bound of **0.02**, which is a *measured property of composition*: hsl alone is 0.00104 and sharpening 0.00905, and **three transcendental stages each under 0.01 do not compose to under 0.01**. The per-stage bound catches a wrong stage; this one catches a wrong chain. ⚠ A test whose bound holds only while its fixture stays easy is the family this file records eighteen times over.
- **⚠ Substitution really was one line**, which is what M8.3c's table was for — and **the at-most-once guard needed no edit at all**, because that slice had already generalised it to loop the whole table rather than name `"hsl"`. *A guard that enumerates a list stops guarding the moment the list grows*, applied in advance and paying off one milestone later.
- **⚠ Two existing tests were RE-AIMED at the vignette**, because the colour grade stopped being a CPU stage and could no longer play the thing that splits a run. ⚠ The rule is unchanged and only its example moved — and their **fixture checks would have failed loudly** rather than the tests going quietly vacuous, which is why those checks are written.
- **⚠ Clippy caught `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` while 42 tests passed** — at least the fifteenth recorded instance of clippy seeing what a green suite did not, and the commit was held until both exit codes read 0.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **nothing inside a mask is accelerated**, so masked HSL — still the case actually reported as slow — is M8.3e's; (2) **local contrast is still not ported**, and it is adjacent to nothing accelerated, so porting it alone buys a third round trip rather than joining the run; (3) the shader and pipelines are still rebuilt on **every encode**, which the bench's round-0 column shows; (4) the three-stage chain diverges by ~0.0115 levels against ~0.001 for one stage — accumulation, invisible, and now bounded by a test that can see it; (5) `gpu_tail` is still **off by default**, so a fresh install sees no change.

### M8.3c — spatial stages on the GPU, and run-merging (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.3c — spatial stages on the GPU, and run-merging (2026-09-11). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works, confirmed by use, I can now use the full quality while dragging and it remains snappy"*, with **no defects found by using it**. Sharpening runs as compute shaders, consecutive GPU stages share **one** round trip, and the setting is `gpu_tail` rather than `gpu_hsl`. 2257 → **2270 tests**; 63 goldens ran and **none moved**, which is the proof no pixel path was touched. Spec `2026-09-10-spatial-gpu-design.md`, plan `2026-09-10-spatial-gpu.md`; the bench is `crates/gpu-pipeline/examples/gpu_run_bench.rs`.

- **⚠⚠ THE REPORT CARRIES A RESULT THE MEASUREMENTS DID NOT PREDICT, AND IT IS THE INTERACTIVE RUNG'S OWN PREDICTION COMING TRUE.** Reported: *"I can now use the full quality while dragging and it remains snappy."* Every number here is **ms per render**; nobody measured whether an accelerated tail makes `DragQuality::Full` usable, and it evidently does on this machine. ⚠⚠ That is exactly what the interactive rung's section wrote down in advance — *"`Full` is zero, so when the GPU port lands the feature is switched off from Settings rather than removed from the code"* — and it is why that setting exists at all rather than the rung drop being unconditional. **A deliberate off-switch, designed a milestone early, turned out to be the right shape.**
- **⚠ Read the scope of that narrowly, because it is one report on one machine.** It says the *fitted, whole-image* case — the interactive rung's own 137.9 ms measurement — is now fast enough at full rung with `gpu_tail` on. It says nothing about a **zoomed native rung**, where the region is small and the rung drop was already worth almost nothing, and nothing about a photo with an **active colour grade**, where the run splits and the win falls to 1.04×. ⚠ Nobody has measured a drag frame at `Full` with the GPU on; `RUSTROOM_DEBUG_RENDER` is the instrument, and doing so is what would turn this from a report into a number.
- **⚠⚠ THE MERGE IS THE FEATURE, AND IT WAS PRICED DIRECTLY RATHER THAN BY SUBTRACTION.** X-T4, 1600×1068 (19.6 MB), release, best of 4 warm rounds:

  | tail | CPU | GPU | |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | hsl only (M8.3b's case) | 27.71 ms | 17.99 ms | 1.54× |
  | **hsl + sharpening, one chain** | 37.67 ms | **24.78 ms** | **1.52×** |
  | hsl + **grade** + sharpening, split | 47.95 ms | 45.93 ms | **1.04×** |

  And the merge itself, by running the same two stages as **two** chains — the shape `accelerate` had before this slice: **merged 21.84 ms against split 32.01 ms, so the merge saves 10.17 ms.** ⚠⚠ **Without it a second GPU stage would have been worth 1.18×, i.e. very nearly nothing** — so run-merging is not an optimisation on top of the port, it is what makes the second stage pay at all. ⚠ Measured directly rather than by subtracting the third row from the second, which would have confounded the merge with the grade's own cost — the arithmetic this project has already been misled by twice.
- **⚠⚠ AND THE THIRD ROW IS THE CAVEAT AS A NUMBER: AN ACTIVE COLOUR GRADE TAKES THE WIN FROM 1.52× TO 1.04×.** Grading sits between `hsl` and `sharpening` in the tail and is not accelerated, so it **splits the run** and the same edits pay two round trips. That is a real limit of this design rather than noise, and it is the thing most likely to be reported as "the GPU setting does nothing on this photo".
- **⚠⚠ SCRATCH PLANES, NOT CHAIN-LEVEL PING-PONG — and `CLAUDE.md`'s own M8.3b note predicted the wrong shape.** That note said *"a spatial stage reads neighbours, so `GpuImage` needs a second buffer"*, which is true and led to the wrong design: ping-pong makes *"which buffer is the front"* a fact every stage must agree about. Instead `GpuStage::scratch_planes()` returns a count, the chain allocates the **max** once and lends the same planes to every stage, and a separable blur goes `front → scratch → front` — so the result lands back where it started and the chain's contract is **unchanged from M8.3b**. The wrong question is unrepresentable rather than answered.
- **⚠ The MAX, not the sum, and nothing is allocated when nothing asks.** Planes are transient *within* a stage, so two stages wanting two each share the same two; summing would double the memory for nothing. And an HSL-only chain still allocates zero, so M8.3b's case costs exactly what it did. ⚠ The carrier is a test stage that asserts on **what it was actually lent** — `scratch_needed` can be right while `run` hands over the wrong slice, and only a stage that looks can see that.
- **⚠⚠ WGSL INDICES ARE UNSIGNED, WHICH IS THE ONE TRAP IN THE WHOLE PORT.** The CPU replicates edges with `(x + i).saturating_sub(r).min(w - 1)`; transliterated, `x + j - r` **wraps to a huge number** whenever `x < r` and then clamps to `w - 1` instead of `0`. The symptom is a fringe down the **left and top edges only**, every interior pixel correct. One `clampi` helper writes the rule once so no pass can get it wrong on its own. ⚠ Honestly: the whole-image equivalence tests catch it too, because their fixture includes its own edges — verified by sabotage, three fail together. The edge test earns its place on **diagnosis**, failing with a coordinate rather than a worst-case level.
- **⚠⚠ THE KERNEL IS THE CPU'S OWN, UPLOADED RATHER THAN RECOMPUTED**, which is why `spatial::gaussian_kernel` is now `pub`. Two implementations of a Gaussian is how the two come to disagree about a σ nobody re-derives — the rule `HueTable::entries` already follows. Sabotaged with a box kernel of the same length: three tests fail.
- **⚠ Eight dispatches, five with masking off, in ONE compute pass** — luma → blur_h → blur_v → difference → [magnitude → mask_h → mask_v] → apply. Four scratch planes: luma, blurred, difference, mask. The mask passes sit where they do because `apply` reads the mask and `magnitude` reads the difference; the order **is** the data dependency. ⚠ Masking 0 skips all three, matching the CPU's `Option<Vec<f32>>` — both the cheap path and what avoids `smoothstep(0, 0, ..)` being degenerate.
- **⚠⚠ THE EQUIVALENCE TESTS WOULD ALL PASS AGAINST A STAGE THAT DID NOTHING**, because they compare GPU against CPU and a sabotage deleting both would agree perfectly. `the_stage_really_sharpens_rather_than_copying` is what says the fixture is one the stage moves — the same shape as the "a masked capture correction really changes the chart" guard, and it exists because the goldens cannot see this crate at all.
- **⚠⚠ THE NEGATIVE MERGE TEST IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.** *A CPU stage between two GPU stages must produce **two** chains* — an implementation merging every replaceable stage regardless of position passes the positive test and runs the intervening stage's work in the wrong order, producing a plausible photograph rather than an error. Sabotaged, **five** tests fail including both carriers, so the bug is a wrong picture and not merely a wrong shape.
- **⚠ A substitution TABLE replaces the if-chain, and it is still not the fix.** `REPLACEABLE: &[(&str, Builder)]` is still name-matching and still stringly-typed; M8.3b's `StageAccelerator` hook remains the right answer once a dozen stages are accelerated, and still loses because `RenderSpec` is `Copy + PartialEq` and an `Arc<dyn Trait>` is neither. ⚠ The at-most-once guard now runs over **the whole table** rather than over `"hsl"` alone — *a guard that enumerates a list stops guarding the moment the list grows*, the sharpest finding the masked-grade milestone left behind, applied here in advance.
- **⚠ `accelerate` gained a `RenderScale`**, found by the plan's own self-review rather than by the compiler: `SharpenStage`'s sigma is in **full-resolution pixels**, so a builder without the rung cannot be written at all. A signature change with two call sites, not a typo.
- **⚠⚠ `gpu_hsl` → `gpu_tail` IS A MIGRATION, NOT A RENAME.** `Settings` carries a container-level `#[serde(default)]`, so without `alias = "gpu_hsl"` an existing file holding `"gpu_hsl": true` would silently fall back to `false` — the user's choice discarded with nothing to notice it. The `EditGroups::effects` → `vignette` precedent, and its test asserts **both** names work: an alias that *replaced* the field name rather than adding to it would pass the first assertion and break every current file. ⚠ The old name governed more than HSL the moment sharpening joined it, which is the class the `Effects` edit group and the "Reset crop" hover text were each corrected for.
- **⚠⚠ AND THE BLANKET RENAME ATE THE ALIAS STRING ITSELF.** A `replace('gpu_hsl', 'gpu_tail')` over the crate rewrote `alias = "gpu_hsl"` into `alias = "gpu_tail"`, silently destroying the migration it had just been written for — the file would have loaded, the test would have been the only thing to fail, and a scripted edit that matches **too much** is the mirror of the `sed`-matched-nothing trap this file already records. Caught by reading the diff. **After a blanket rename, grep for the old name and check every place it legitimately survives.**
- **⚠⚠ THE PLAN'S TASK ORDER WAS WRONG AND EXECUTING IT SHOWED WHY.** Run-merging was Task 2 and `GpuSharpenStage` Task 3 — but the merge tests need **two adjacent replaceable stages**, and until the sharpen stage exists the only one is `hsl`, of which a tail contains exactly one (asserted by M8.3b's own test). Run-merging was structurally untestable before the stage it merges with. Swapped; recorded in the plan in place.
- **⚠ The first bench run was contaminated and was discarded rather than quoted.** Taken while `cargo test --workspace` saturated the cores, it read **49.55 ms of CPU for less work than a later 37.97 ms** — visible only because the column was internally inconsistent. Re-measured on a quiet machine. The same contention trap this file already records against the debug adapter timing, walked into anyway.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) **an active colour grade splits the run and costs almost the whole win** — 1.52× → 1.04×, measured; (2) **local contrast is not ported**, so Texture and Clarity stay on the CPU — it needs three blur kinds (`box_blur`, `wide_blur`, the guided filter) where sharpening needed one, which is why it was scoped out; (3) **nothing inside a mask is accelerated**, so masked HSL — the case actually reported as slow — is still M8.3d's; (4) the first render after switching the toggle on spends ~150 ms compiling shaders; (5) the shader is rebuilt and the pipelines recreated on **every encode**, which the bench's round-0 column shows and which a pipeline cache would remove; (6) `scratch_planes` is 4 whatever the masking setting, so the allocation does not depend on a slider.

### M8.3b — a resident GPU chain, and HSL across it (2026-09-10). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.3b — a resident GPU chain, and HSL across it (2026-09-10). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works, confirmed by use"*, with **no defects found by using it**. ⚠ Read that narrowly: what was exercised is the **global** HSL slider with the toggle on, which is what the feature does. Masked HSL is untouched by it, and the ~150 ms first-render shader compilation was not reported as noticeable. N GPU stages share one round trip, and the global HSL slider runs on the GPU behind a Settings toggle. 2244 → **2257 tests**; 63 goldens ran and **none moved**. Spec `2026-09-10-resident-gpu-tail-design.md`, plan `2026-09-10-resident-gpu-tail.md`; the bench is `crates/gpu-pipeline/examples/gpu_hsl_bench.rs`.

**Measured, 1600×1068 on an Apple M2: CPU ~21 ms against GPU ~10–11 ms — about 2×**, with a divergence of **0.00034 of an 8-bit level**. ⚠ **Round 0 is 152 ms**: the first encode compiles the shader, which a user pays once on the first render after enabling the toggle.

- **⚠⚠ THE BARRIER QUESTION IS ANSWERED: WebGPU DOES guarantee memory visibility between dispatches within one compute pass.** Measured rather than read — three exposures at +1.0, −0.5 and +0.25 EV equal one at +0.75, and **gains multiply, so a missing barrier gives a wrong product rather than a plausible image**. ⚠ And the alternative is **inert**: a sabotage putting each dispatch in its own pass passes everything, so if a backend ever lacks the in-pass barrier the fix costs nothing. Recorded because a sabotage that does not fail is a finding, not a formality.
- **⚠⚠ `GpuStage` IS DELIBERATELY NOT `PipelineStage`, and the two cannot be one.** `apply(ImageBuf) -> ImageBuf` takes CPU memory and returns CPU memory, so it **forces a round trip by its signature** — right as the seam, wrong as the unit of GPU work. `GpuChain` holds `Vec<Box<dyn GpuStage>>` and *implements* `PipelineStage`, so the existing pipeline sees one stage doing N stages' work and nothing in `pipeline` changed.
- **⚠ `GpuStage::cpu()` is not decoration, and the SPEC REVIEW found it missing.** `apply` has no failure channel, so a chain failing on the GPU must produce the CPU answer — and a trait exposing only `encode` would have **nothing to fall back to**. Each stage carries its own twin; a parallel list on the chain would be two lists that can disagree about their order.
- **⚠⚠ `sign(x) * pow(abs(x), 1/3)`, NEVER `pow(x, 1/3)`** — WGSL's `pow` returns NaN for a negative base, and the CPU uses `cbrt` *specifically because it is sign-preserving*; a wide working space produces scene-referred negatives routinely. ⚠⚠ **And the test that named this could not detect it**: its fixture `[-0.05, 0.3, 0.2]` gives l=0.056, m=0.198, s=0.191 — **all positive** — so `pow` never saw a negative base and the sabotage passed. Now `[-0.5, 0.02, 0.03]`, which gives l=−0.353, **computed rather than guessed**. The nineteenth instance of a test naming a bug it cannot see.
- **⚠⚠ AND AN ASSERTION THAT WAS WRONG ABOUT CORRECT CODE: "a neutral pixel comes back bit-identical" is FALSE.** A grey in ProPhoto has **non-zero Oklab chroma** — the matrix rows do not sum equally — so `[0.4, 0.4, 0.4]` sits at the `EPS = 1e-6` boundary, the CPU took the early-out and the GPU's slightly different chroma did not. ⚠ Which also says something about the stage itself: **only pure black has chroma exactly zero, so `EPS` barely ever fires and `CHROMA_FADE` is the real protection for neutrals.**
- **⚠ The band logic never enters the shader.** `HueTable::build` already collapses eight bands and their smoothstep blending into a 1024-entry table — 12 KB, built once on the CPU — and `GpuHslStage` uploads **the CPU stage's own table** rather than rebuilding it, so the two cannot disagree about blending.
- **⚠⚠ SUBSTITUTION NEEDS NO CHANGE TO `pipeline`, AND IT IS NAME-MATCHING.** `accelerate(tail, edits, ctx)` replaces the stage named `hsl` by **rebuilding it from `edits.hsl`** — a `dyn PipelineStage` exposes only `name()` and `apply()`, but the caller still holds the `Edits`. ⚠ **It does not scale to a dozen stages**: the right answer then is a `StageAccelerator` hook `pipeline` calls at construction, which loses today only because `RenderSpec` is `Copy + PartialEq` and an `Arc<dyn Trait>` is neither. Three guards: at most one `hsl` in the tail (asserted **with a masked HSL present**, since that is what makes it sound), a tail without HSL returns unchanged, and an accelerated tail renders the same picture.
- **⚠⚠ A REAL BUG THE TESTS CAUGHT: `match (gpu_hsl, gpu_pipeline::shared())` EVALUATES BOTH ELEMENTS.** So `shared()` ran **even with the setting off**, acquiring an adapter on the render worker at ~42 s in a debug build; three render tests began reporting *"no frame produced"* after a one-second wait. It is an `if` now — **with the setting off, nothing GPU-related is touched at all.** ⚠ A tuple scrutinee is not a short-circuit.
- **⚠ The transfer counters are PER CHAIN, and that was a bug rather than a preference.** Process-wide statics read `(6, 4)` instead of `(1, 1)` because `cargo test` runs in parallel and other chains' transfers landed between the reads. The chain was correct; **the observable was contaminated** — the same class as this repo's temp-path collisions.
- **⚠ Upload goes through a `MAP_WRITE` staging buffer**: 1.86 ms against `write_buffer`'s 3.90 for 19.6 MB. ⚠⚠ **Zero-copy is NOT reachable** — there is always one memcpy into mapped memory, and a plain CPU memcpy of the same bytes is 0.80–0.93 ms, which is the floor. That retires M8.3a's stated top recommendation.
- **⚠ `gpu_hsl` rides `FrameSpec` beside `resampler`, per request** — a global setting the user changes with a photo open, so a toggle takes effect on the next render with no engine rebuild. ⚠ Unlike the resampler it is in **no** `PrefixStepKey` and must not be: HSL is a *tail* stage, so the prefix computes the same thing either way and every cached checkpoint stays valid.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **masked HSL is NOT accelerated, and it is the case reported in use as slow** — a mask's sub-pipeline lives inside `MaskStage`, which `accelerate` sees as one opaque stage; reaching inside it belongs with M8.3d; (2) **only HSL** of eleven per-pixel stages; (3) **no ping-pong buffer**, so spatial stages cannot join until M8.3c adds one; (4) **~150 ms of shader compilation on the first render** after enabling the toggle; (5) **off by default**, so nobody gets a rendering change they did not ask for; (6) `encode` rebuilds the shader module and compute pipeline **every call** — wasteful, and measured as not the bottleneck, so deliberately not cached yet; (7) nothing helps **export**, still ~93% demosaic upstream of every stage `wgpu` would port; (8) ⚠ the GPU tests **skip without an adapter**, so they are unverified on Linux CI.

### M8.3a — the GPU seam and the proof (2026-09-10)

**M8.3a — the GPU seam and the proof (2026-09-10).** One pipeline stage runs as a `wgpu` compute shader, checked against the CPU stage by a harness, with the round-trip cost measured in the repo. 2233 → **2244 tests**; 63 goldens ran and **none moved** — this adds a crate and touches no pixel path. Spec `2026-09-10-gpu-seam-design.md`, plan `2026-09-10-gpu-seam.md`; the probe is `crates/gpu-pipeline/examples/gpu_equivalence.rs`, kept.

⚠⚠ **THIS SLICE IS DELIBERATELY SLOWER AND NOTHING IN THE APP USES IT.** Measured on a 1600×1068 f32 buffer: CPU 2.8–4.2 ms against GPU 10.2–16.6 ms, **3.1–4.7× slower**, and **bit-exact across all 5,126,400 samples**. That is the design — see the caveats — not a defect to be "fixed" by wiring it in as a default.

- **⚠⚠ THE TRANSFER IS EVERYTHING, AND IT DECIDES THE WHOLE MILESTONE.** Compute is **0.04 ms**; moving a 19.6 MB buffer is **~6 ms** (upload 2.4–3.0, readback 3.2–6.9), a factor of ~70. This turns this file's own standing prediction — *"a single GPU stage inside a CPU pipeline is likely net-NEGATIVE"* — from an argument into a number. Three consequences: M8.3a is ~6 ms slower **by construction**; **M8.3b's ceiling is ~5×, not 10×**, because the transfer is the floor; and ⚠⚠ **on this machine the GPU shares physical memory with the CPU, yet 19.6 MB takes 2.4 ms (~8 GB/s) — so wgpu is *copying*, not mapping. Hunting a zero-copy path is the highest-value thing in M8.3b, ahead of porting any further stage.** Do not port ten shaders and then discover the floor could have been removed.
- **⚠⚠ THE GPU FLUSHES SUBNORMALS TO ZERO AND THE CPU DOES NOT, so "bit-exact" is NOT achievable in general even for a multiply.** Found here, not reasoned about: **1,821,428 of 12,750,000 samples differed — exactly 1/7**, the share of the fixture that was `f32::MIN_POSITIVE`. ⚠ And it appeared **only** in the test whose gain was below 1, because a gain above 1 cannot produce a subnormal — so the original single-EV test was blind to it. It is now `a_subnormal_result_is_flushed_to_zero_on_the_gpu`, **named rather than worked around**, and the bit-exactness test exercises **both sides of neutral**. ⚠ It does not matter for photographs (a subnormal is below ~1.2e-38; a scene-referred sample is 1e-4 to 10) — but **every future stage's equivalence test wants the both-sides-of-neutral treatment**, and this is exactly the class of thing the harness exists to find.
- **⚠ Exposure is the right first stage precisely because it *should* be exact.** The gain `2^ev` is computed CPU-side and passed as a uniform, so the shader is one multiply with no `exp2`. Any divergence therefore means **plumbing**, not float drift — which is what a first slice must be able to distinguish. ⚠⚠ **The corollary, and it is a real risk to the milestone: this slice does NOT answer how far a transcendental stage diverges.** Whether GPU `HslStage` (Oklab + `atan2`) lands within a usable tolerance is **M8.3b's first question**, and if it does not, M8.3b's shape changes.
- **⚠⚠ 65535 WORKGROUPS PER DIMENSION, and a naive per-float 1D dispatch fails at fit resolution ALREADY** — `1600 × 1068 × 3 / 64 = 80,100`. Per pixel it is 26,700, which fits, but a 26 Mpx native rung needs 407,000. **2D from the start**, with a test image deliberately exceeding `65535 × 64` pixels, because a 1D dispatch passes every small fixture and fails on the first real photograph.
- **⚠⚠ GPU TESTS COST ~42 s IN A DEBUG BUILD AND ~0.1 s IN RELEASE.** Acquiring an adapter is **44–75 s in debug against 21 ms in release**, measured under identical load; the **second** call in the same process is **259 µs**, so it is one-time process initialisation. Hence `GpuContext::shared()`, guarded by its own test — without it five GPU tests would each pay a minute. ⚠ **Iterate with `cargo test --release -p gpu-pipeline`.** ⚠⚠ **The root cause is NOT identified, and the doc comment says so rather than guessing.** Ruled out by measurement: dependency `opt-level = 2`, dependency `debug-assertions`, backend enumeration (`METAL` alone was no faster than `PRIMARY`), machine contention (release stayed at 21 ms with another process at 100% CPU), and Gatekeeper re-verification (the same binary three times: 62 s, 47 s, 44 s). ⚠ What **did** help: **not** using `Instance::default()`, whose `InstanceFlags::from_build_config()` enables wgpu validation in every debug build — 151 s → 45 s.
- **⚠ The goldens stay CPU and never move (user's call).** The equivalence harness is what will protect the shipped path from M8.3b onward, so it converts to **8-bit levels** rather than comparing raw floats — a linear difference near black reads as enormous while being invisible, the correction the Whites slider and M8.4's demosaic comparison each needed. ⚠ A size mismatch reports **infinite** divergence rather than comparing what overlaps: zipping two lengths silently ignores the tail, so a truncated readback would look like agreement. ⚠ The CPU path stays **forever as the oracle**, the role `DecodeOptions::camera_native` already plays.
- **⚠ `apply` returns `ImageBuf`, not `Result` — the trait has no failure channel — so every GPU error degrades SILENTLY to the CPU stage.** `apply_with` exists so that path is testable; without the split the fallback could only be reached by unplugging a GPU. Its test asserts the output equals the **CPU stage's** exactly, since asserting merely "non-empty" would pass against a fallback returning the input unchanged.
- **⚠ Three `wgpu` 29 API facts, each hit by the compiler rather than read in advance:** `PipelineLayoutDescriptor::bind_group_layouts` is `&[Option<&BindGroupLayout>]`; `push_constant_ranges` became `immediate_size`; and `PollType::Wait` is a **struct variant** (`{ submission_index, timeout }`). ⚠ `InstanceDescriptor` has **no `Default`**, so all five fields are named explicitly.
- **⚠ Tasks 1 and 2 landed as ONE commit.** `GpuContext`'s `device` and `queue` are `pub(crate)` with no caller until the stage exists, which fails `-D warnings` as dead code — the trap this file records for *bin* crates, arriving in a **library** through `pub(crate)`. ⚠ And a commit went in with clippy failing before that was caught, for at least the fifteenth recorded time; it was squashed so every commit on the branch is green.
- **⚠ `assert_same` summarises rather than dumping.** A bare `assert_eq!` on two 12-million-element slices printed **254 MB** of numbers, which is not a diagnosis. Any assertion over a full-frame buffer needs to report *where* it differs, not *what* it contains — and the summarised message is what identified the subnormal in one run.
- **Accepted caveats:** (1) ⚠⚠ **nothing in the app uses it** — no Settings toggle, no substitution mechanism, nothing renders on GPU when Rustroom launches; defensible only because a single GPU stage is measurably net-negative, and the risk it accepts is the W5 failure mode (creative LUTs shipped fully tested and 100% dead), mitigated by the probe, which is a genuine end-to-end run but **is not the app**; (2) **~6 ms slower per render** by construction; (3) **transcendental divergence unanswered**, M8.3b's first task; (4) neither the prefix, the masks nor the spatial stages are touched; (5) **no zero-copy and no resident buffer** — every `apply` is a full round trip, which is the whole reason it is slower; (6) nothing here helps **export**, ~93% demosaic inside libraw and upstream of every stage `wgpu` would ever port; (7) ⚠ **the GPU tests SKIP without an adapter, so they are unverified on Linux CI** — without that stated, the next person reads 2244 green tests and believes the seam is covered everywhere it runs.

### M8.2 — an on-disk thumbnail cache (2026-09-10). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE

**M8.2 — an on-disk thumbnail cache (2026-09-10). ✅ CONFIRMED BY USE** — *"works, confirmed by use"*, with **no defects found by using it**, which is worth recording: this is a *lib* module with an injected directory and a carrier test, and the class of bug this file records fifteen times over lives in canvas and panel wiring, of which M8.2 has almost none. A folder you have opened before fills its thumbnails from disk in ~1.26 ms each instead of re-extracting them at ~190 ms each. 2219 → **2233 tests**, 63 goldens ran and **none moved** — the proof this touches no pixel path. Spec `2026-09-10-thumbnail-cache-design.md`, plan `2026-09-10-thumbnail-cache.md`; the probe is `crates/app/examples/bench_thumb_cache.rs`, kept.

- **Measured, then achieved.** Cold **190.41 ms** per entry against warm **1.26 ms**, 60 of 60 served from cache — **151×**. ⚠ The spec projected 1.10 ms from an *in-memory* JPEG decode and said so; the extra 0.16 ms is the real disk read, which is why the plan's last task re-measures against the real store rather than quoting the projection as a result. ~60 KB per photo, so the author's 830-entry folder is **49.7 MB**.
- **⚠⚠ A FULL-SIZE CAMERA JPEG COSTS 2.6× A RAW TO THUMBNAIL, WHICH INVERTS THE OBVIOUS GUESS.** RAW **105.1 ms**, JPEG/PNG/TIFF **277.7 ms**. `raw_decode::extract_thumbnail` pulls the camera's small **embedded preview** out of the RAW and decodes only that; a 12 MB camera JPEG has no embedded preview, so `image_decode::thumbnail` decodes all 26 Mpx and then downscales. **The cache helps non-RAW sources more.** ⚠ It also names the lever for the **cold** open, deliberately out of scope here: a JPEG can be decoded at 1/8 scale in the DCT domain far more cheaply than decoding it whole. Nothing in M8.2 touches the first open of a folder.
- **⚠⚠ IT CACHES THE EXTRACTED PREVIEW, NOT THE FINISHED THUMBNAIL, AND THE RATIO IS WHAT DECIDES IT.** The obvious design mirrors `ThumbCache` — key on `ThumbKey` (photo + edits fingerprint), a drop-in. But extraction is 191 ms and rendering an edited thumbnail over it is ~5 ms, so keying the *disk* cache on edits makes it useless for the case `thumb_loader.rs` already flags as the expensive one — *"a changed edit costs another ~95 ms here"* — and leaves a file behind for **every edit state a photo has ever had**. Keyed on the file instead, a changed edit costs ~6 ms rather than ~196 ms. The two levels then each cache what they are named for: **disk holds previews, memory holds rendered thumbnails**, and neither needs invalidation code.
- **⚠⚠ `DefaultHasher` IS UNUSABLE FOR AN ON-DISK KEY, and this is the trap worth remembering.** `std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher`'s algorithm is explicitly allowed to change between Rust releases, so a filename built from it would **silently invalidate the entire cache on a toolchain upgrade** — a 26-second regression appearing for no reason anybody could connect to anything. `thumb_key::edits_fingerprint` gets away with it precisely because it never leaves memory. FNV-1a is five lines and stable by definition; no dependency.
- **⚠⚠ AND THE PINNED VECTORS EARNED THEIR PLACE ON THE FIRST RUN.** The FNV-64 prime is `0x100000001b3` — **eleven** hex digits, so the readable grouping is 3-4-4. Written `0x1000_0000_01b3` it becomes `0x1000000001b3`, a **different number that still hashes plausibly**: the low 32 bits of the output even matched. Nothing but a known-answer test would have caught it, and the symptom in production would have been a cache that simply never hit.
- **⚠ The entry is a small header plus JPEG q90, not a bare `.jpg`, and the header does three jobs** — each a failure it makes unrepresentable. (1) **Versioning**: a format change bumps `VERSION` and old entries miss, rather than old bytes being reinterpreted as the new format. (2) **Collision safety**: the identity is re-checked on read, so an FNV collision is a **miss** rather than **someone else's photograph in your grid** — ~3e-10 over 100k entries, and a bad enough failure to be worth five lines. (3) **Dimensions are the authority**, so a payload disagreeing with its header is a miss. ⚠ Writes are **atomic** — `.tmp` then rename — or a crash mid-write leaves a truncated JPEG that decodes to garbage.
- **⚠ Identity is `(path, mtime, size)`**, one `stat`.
